Tachy-Tony (The Engine-Overheat)
Tony runs the heart so fast that the filling chambers never have time to load blood.
Unstable? Synchronized-Zap. Stable? Adenosine-Reset.
Brady-Bill (The Slow-Mo Curse)
Bill makes the heart beat so slowly that the brain blacks out from lack of pressure.
Usually a wiring issue. Atropine might speed him up, but an external battery (Pacing) is the real fix.
Anaphylaxis-Annie (The Global Leak)
Annie turns blood vessels into sieves and slams the airway door shut with explosive edema.
Triggered by allergens. Epinephrine is the only key to constrict the pipes and open the lungs simultaneously.
Septic-Sam (The Vasodilation-Vortex)
Sam uses a Cytokine-Tsunami to paralyze blood vessels, causing total pressure collapse.
Sam demands the Hour-1-Bundle: massive fluids, cultures, and early Pressor-Power (Norepinephrine).
Cardiogenic-Carl (The Broken Piston)
Carl fails to push. Blood backs up into the lungs, drowning the patient from the inside.
Fluid is the enemy. Carl needs Inotrope-Ignition to boost pump strength and an immediate trip to the Cath Lab.
Hypovolemic-Hank (The Dry-Run)
Hank strikes when volume is missing. There simply isn't enough juice left to keep the lights on.
Replace what is lost! If it's blood, give blood. If it's water, give crystalloids.
Epi-Eric (The Adrenaline-Jumpstart)
Eric violently constricts the pipes and screams at the heart to beat faster.
The king of the Code Blue. He diverts all remaining blood to the brain and heart during the fight.
Ami-the-Armor (The Rhythm-Shield)
Ami stabilizes the heart's electrical wires to keep the static storm of V-Fib from returning.
A Class III antiarrhythmic. It buys critical time for the heart to find its normal beat again.
Atropine-Alice (The Brake-Cutter)
Alice cuts the Vagus-Brake, completely removing the inhibitory signals slowing down the heart.
An anticholinergic assassin. She stops the Rest and Digest system from ending the match prematurely.
Adenosine-Andy (The 6-Second Flatline)
Andy stops the heart completely for a few terrifying seconds, forcing it to reboot into a normal rhythm.
Used for SVT. It feels like a massive thump in the chest to the conscious patient.
Tension-Tony (The Heart-Crush)
Tony traps air in the chest on a one-way valve, building pressure until the Great Vessels are squashed flat.
A clinical diagnosis! Do not wait for X-Ray. Execute the Needle-Decompression-Nudge in the 5th intercostal Space immediately.
Narcan-Nancy (The Opiate-Evictor)
Nancy violently rips opiates off the brain's receptors, bringing the patient back to life instantly.
Beware the short half-life. Nancy might wear off before the opiates do, throwing the patient back into a coma.
Gluca-Gwen (The Sugar-Summoner)
Gwen forces the liver to dump its entire emergency stash of sugar into the blood.
Beyond low sugar, Gwen is the secret key to restart the engine during a lethal Beta-Blocker overdose.
Aspirin-Ace (The Platelet-Slip)
Ace makes the blood-clotters slippery so they can't block the Coronary-Canyons.
Reduces mortality in Myocardial Infarction by preventing the Clot-Monster from growing any larger.
Heat-Stroke-Harry (The Internal Oven)
Harry cooks the body's proteins from the inside out. Sweat production has utterly failed.
A true emergency. Harry requires immediate, aggressive physical cooling (ice water/fans) before the brain permanently melts.
Frosty-Frank (The Metabolic Freeze)
Frank slows cellular time down to a crawl until the heart stumbles into fatal V-Fib.
Nobody is dead until they are warm and dead! Frank requires extremely careful, active internal rewarming.
Drowning-Drake (The Fluid Barrier)
Drake fills the fragile lungs with water, or triggers an iron-tight spasm of the vocal cords to lock air out.
Hypoxia is the ultimate killer. Drake requires immediate ventilation and high PEEP to flush fluid out of the alveoli.
Burn-Ben (The Barrier Break)
Ben destroys the skin shield. Core water evaporates instantly, and bacterial armies march in.
Massive volume loss is the silent threat. Ben requires enormous amounts of Ringer's Lactate in the first 24 hours.
Carbon-Monoxide-Carl (The Hemoglobin Hijack)
Carl binds to the oxygen bus 240 times stronger than O2. The pulse oximeter lies to you.
The patient suffocates despite ample oxygen in the room. Carl demands 100% O2 or a hyperbaric pressure chamber.
Organophosphate-Otto (The Cholinergic Storm)
Otto blocks the cleanup of nerve signals; the entire parasympathetic system is stuck on Full Fire.
Otto requires massive, repeated doses of Atropine-Alice until the lungs are finally dry.
Beta-Blocker-Ben (The Heart-Slug)
Ben suppresses the beta-receptors, slowing the heart's rate and squeeze down so much that it nearly stalls.
If standard Atropine fails to break the lock, Gluca-Gwen is the chemical bypass key needed to restart the engine.
Tricyclic-Ty (The Electrical Chaos)
Ty blocks crucial sodium channels, widening the QRS complex and throwing the heart into a deadly cardiac rhythm.
The specific antidote is Sodium Bicarbonate—it floods the channels with sodium to flush Ty out and stabilize the wires.
Pregnant-Pam (The Return-Block)
The heavy uterus physically crushes the Inferior Vena Cava when lying flat, preventing blood from returning to the heart.
During CPR, the uterus must be manually shifted to the left, otherwise compressions are pumping an empty heart.
Pediatric-Paul (The Respiratory Trigger)
In children, cardiac arrest is rarely a primary pump failure; it is almost always driven by fatal hypoxia.
Ventilation is the absolute priority. Airway management saves pediatric lives before the heart ever stops.
Trauma-Tanya (The Death Spiral)
Tanya alters blood physics: blood absolutely refuses to clot when the body gets cold and acidic.
Damage Control Resuscitation: Keep them warm, stop the bleed, avoid crystalloids, and pump high ratios of blood products.
Obese-Oliver (The Physical Barrier)
Oliver's sheer mass makes achieving adequate chest compression depth and effective ventilation a monumental physical ordeal.
Manual CPR fatigue rescuers instantly. Mechanical CPR devices and advanced airway planning are mandatory here.
Defi-Dan (The Resetter)
Dan sends a violently controlled electrical punch directly through the heart muscle to end all chaotic activity.
Dan discharges every cardiac cell simultaneously, creating a moment of total silence so the pacemaker can restart the beat.
BVM-Bill (The Manual Breath)
Bill forcefully presses oxygen down into the lungs when the patient's own bellows fail.
Avoid gastric inflation! Squeezing Bill too hard forces air into the stomach, guaranteeing a vomit tsunami.
IO-Iggy (The Bone-Highway)
When peripheral veins collapse into hiding, Iggy violently drills a direct fluid highway right into the bone marrow.
The bone marrow is a non-collapsible vein. Anything you can push in an IV, you can push through Iggy.
Laryngoscope-Larry (The Tongue-Lifter)
Larry physically wrestles the heavy tongue out of the way, lighting a path through the dark tunnel to the vocal cords.
Larry is the essential scouting tool required for Airway-Annie to successfully place the Golden Tube.
Stroke-Steve (The Brain-Ischemia)
Steve blocks a vital arterial supply line in the head. Every passing minute, millions of neurons permanently die.
Time is Brain! Steve demands either the Clot-Dissolver (Lyse) or the Mechanical Grabber (Thrombectomy) immediately.
Seizure-Sidus (The Electrical Firestorm)
Sidus forces the brain to fire at maximum capacity uncontrollably, burning incredible energy and risking permanent melting.
Sidus needs GABA-Garry (Benzodiazepines) immediately to extinguish the runaway electrical fire.
Brain-Bleed-Brawler (The Pressure-Cooker)
The Brawler leaks expanding blood into the rigid skull. Because the bone won't yield, intracranial pressure spikes instantly.
The Brawler triggers the Cushing Reflex (High BP, Low Pulse) as the brain desperately fights to push blood against the rising crush.
Hypo-Harry (The Mimic)
Harry flawlessly disguises himself as Stroke-Steve or Seizure-Sidus, tricking medics until sugar reveals his true identity.
The brain needs glucose like a car needs gas. Without juice, the engine completely stalls. Always check the sugar!
FAST-Fiona (The Fluid-Finder)
Fiona shoots high-frequency sound to hunt down hidden, pooling blood in the belly or trapped around the heart in seconds.
A positive Fiona signal in a hemodynamically unstable trauma patient is a direct, one-way ticket to the operating room.
Lactate-Larry (The Suffocation-Score)
Larry acts as the cellular distress signal, revealing exactly how badly the tissues are starving and crying for oxygen.
High Larry means occult shock is happening at the cellular level, regardless of how normal the blood pressure currently looks.
Troponin-Troy (The Muscle-Damage Detector)
Troy is exclusively released when cardiac muscle cells are actively dying and breaking apart.
Troy is highly specific—if you find these nuggets in the bloodstream, you have absolute proof of a Myocardial Infarction.
Blood-Gas-Bella (The Acid-Base Balance)
Bella reveals the invisible metabolic scale: is the wrestler acidic or basic, and are the lungs or the kidneys to blame?
Bella is the ultimate high-fidelity dashboard for fine-tuning mechanical ventilation and targeted fluid resuscitation.
Triage-Raven (The Life-Decider)
In mass casualty chaos, Raven makes the ruthless, split-second decisions about who gets the limited medical resources.
Normal medical ethics invert here. The ultimate goal is the survival of the many, not the desperate rescue of the individual.
Scoop vs Stay (The Tactical Choice)
The ultimate operational fork: Immediate, frantic transport for surgery bleeding, versus methodical on-scene stabilization for medical codes.
Treat as you go. But critical bleeding and airway obstruction are always addressed before the wheels roll.
HEMS-Heidi (The Sky-Cavalry)
Heidi completely bypasses ground traffic, bringing the highest level of specialized doctor and equipment directly to the dirt.
Heidi radically expands the geographical capture radius for highly time-sensitive interventions (Stroke Centers / Level 1 Trauma).
C-Spine-Chris (The Spine-Guard)
Chris ensures that the fragile spinal cord isn't shredded by unstable, shattered vertebrae during rescue movements.
Respect the Log Roll. The patient must be turned as a single, rigid tree trunk to avoid permanently angering Chris.
Handover-Hank (The MIST Protocol)
Hank perfectly transfers critical field knowledge from the muddy EMS team to the sterile shock room without dropping a byte.
A dropped baton is lethal. A poor Hank kills the patient through hospital ignorance and delayed interventions.
Shock-Room-Sgt (The Chaos-Control)
The Sgt coordinates trauma surgeons, anesthesiologists, and nurses in a perfectly choreographed, silent dance.
Without the Sgt commanding the room from the foot of the bed, the high-tech shock room instantly degrades into a noisy chicken coop.
Transfusion-Tank (The Blood-Flood)
When Hypovolemic-Hank drains the blood, the Tank re-enters the system, refilling the wrestler with actual, life-saving hemoglobin and platelets.
Clear fluids only dilute clotting factors. In massive hemorrhage, only blood replaces blood.
Recovery-Ranger (The Safety Guard)
The Ranger stands guard, monitoring the chaotic equilibrium after the Golden Hour Gauntlet has been violently survived.
The post-resuscitation phase is incredibly critical: the war is won, but the assassins will return if the Ranger isn't violently aggressive.
Doc FrizzleBob (The Final Decision)
Cuts through the noise. Operates on pure clinical instinct backed by hardcore physiological lore.
Treat the life-threats, not the labs. If the pump is dry, fill it. If air is trapped, vent it. Stay fluffy!
Synthesis Quest 1 (The Crushed Heart)
Identify the mechanical stopper (Tamponade) squeezing the heart.
Which intervention clears the blood from the pericardial sac before the pump stalls forever?
Synthesis Quest 2 (The Silent Choke)
Activate the ABCDE sequence under maximum stress.
Who secures the way (Airway-Annie) and who breaks the fatal allergic reaction (Epi-Eric)?
Synthesis Quest 3 (The Quivering Void)
The ultimate algorithmic decision tree.
Name the rhythm (V-Fib). Compress, shock, or push drugs? You have 5 seconds to decide. Go!
Hypo the Hypothalamus
Portal Command – Send short-range chemical orders via blood, bypassing nerves.
Dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin. Metoclopramide blocks dopamine → galactorrhea.
GH the Giant
Paradoxical Rise – Fails to suppress during oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT).
Acromegaly causes insulin resistance. Diagnose with high IGF-1 and failure to suppress.
Piti the Anterior Pituitary
Tropic Command – Dispatches FSH, LH, TSH, ACTH, GH, PRL to six target organs simultaneously.
Large non-functioning adenoma compresses the stalk, causing secondary hypopituitarism — all axes fail together.
Prolly the Prolactin
Tonic Suppression – Unique hormone controlled by constant INHIBITION not stimulation.
Stalk compression blocks dopamine → mild prolactin rise. Treat macroprolactinoma with dopamine agonists (cabergoline).
CRH the Commander
Axis Drive – ACTH + High Cortisol = ACTH-dependent Cushing’s. Low ACTH + High Cortisol = Adrenal adenoma.
Drives cortisol with circadian rhythm losing its pulse under stress. Interpret ACTH levels to locate the lesion.
ADH the Water Keeper
V2 Insertion – Retain free water in the collecting duct.
Central DI lacks ADH (treat with desmopressin). Nephrogenic DI resists ADH (treat with low-salt diet/thiazides).
Thyro the Thyroid Axis
Peripheral Conversion – Convert T4 to the highly active T3 in peripheral tissues.
Pregnancy increases TBG → total T4 rises, but free T4 is normal. Do not adjust dose based on total T4!
Cortisol the Stress Master
Mobilize glucose at the cost of muscle, bone, and immune function.
Exogenous steroids suppress the HPA axis. Abrupt withdrawal during infection causes fatal adrenal crisis.
Feedback Freda
Diagnostic Directions – High peripheral hormone + low tropic hormone = autonomous peripheral gland.
Use stimulation tests (Synacthen) for suspected deficiency. Use suppression tests (DST, OGTT) for suspected excess.
Hashi the Destroyer
Lymphocytic Infiltration – Slowly run the body at half-speed via Th1 destruction.
Severe hypothyroidism causes myxoedema (non-pitting oedema); check delayed relaxation of ankle reflexes.
Graves the Impersonator
TSI Mimicry – TSI antibodies impersonate TSH, locking the receptor open and flooding the system.
Exophthalmos persists even after thyroid treatment because orbital fibroblasts have their own TSH-R. Treat with selenium.
Nodule Norman
The TSH Fork – Low TSH = hot/autonomous (rarely malignant). Normal/High TSH = Needs US/FNA.
Papillary cancer (80%) spreads via lymph nodes. Follicular cancer (15%) spreads via blood.
Thyroid Storm Tom
Supercritical Melt – Acute physiological stress triggers lethal high-output failure.
You MUST give PTU before Lugol’s iodine, or the iodine load will flood out as new hormone.
Hypo the Hypothyroid Drug
Prodrug Conversion – Relies on peripheral deiodinase; takes weeks to reflect dose changes.
Absorption is impaired by food, iron, calcium. Dose must increase 15-50% immediately upon pregnancy confirmation!
Parathyroid Pete
Calcium Reclamation – High Ca, Low PO4, High urine Ca.
Primary hyperparathyroidism is the most common outpatient cause of hypercalcaemia. Diagnosed often incidentally.
Zona the Architect
Triple Hormone Threat – Addison’s destroys all three cortical layers simultaneously.
Zona Glomerulosa makes Aldosterone (driven by RAAS, NOT ACTH). Fasciculata makes Cortisol. Reticularis makes Androgens.
Vitamin D the Sunshine Hormone
Dual Hydroxylation – Must be activated twice (liver then kidney) to act; gut calcium absorption depends on it.
Sarcoidosis macrophages have 1α-hydroxylase activity, causing unregulated active calcitriol and hypercalcaemia.
Aldo the Aldosterone
Volume Controller – ENaC insertion raises pressure at the cost of potassium.
Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn’s) causes hypertension + hypokalaemia with suppressed renin.
Cushing the Cushioned
Ectopic Overdrive – SCLC ectopic ACTH causes profound hypokalaemia, rapid onset, less classic spread.
Screen with 24h urinary free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, or low-dose dexamethasone suppression test.
Addison the Insufficient
MCR Stimulation – High ACTH cross-reacts with MCR to cause hyperpigmentation (palmar creases, buccal mucosa).
Secondary adrenal insufficiency has LOW ACTH, therefore NO hyperpigmentation. The tan is the diagnostic clue.
Phe the Hidden
Paroxysmal Spells – The classic triad: headache, sweating, palpitations.
Never give beta-blockers without alpha-blockade first; unopposed alpha causes lethal paradoxical hypertension!
Conns the Connector
Vein Sampling – Adrenal CT is insufficient to distinguish bilateral hyperplasia from unilateral adenoma.
Unilateral source = laparoscopic surgery. Bilateral source = medical management with spironolactone.
BAH Clara
Enzyme Blockade – Lack of cortisol removes negative feedback; high ACTH drives massive androgen overproduction.
Classic salt-wasting causes neonatal crisis. Non-classic mimics PCOS in adults. Diagnose with elevated 17-OHP.
MEN the Syndrome Families
Genetic Destiny – RET proto-oncogene mutations dictate medullary thyroid cancer prophylactic resection.
MEN2B = Medullary Thyroid Cancer, Phaeochromocytoma, Mucosal Neuromas, NO parathyroid.
Waterhouse the Crisis
Sick Day Rules – Double or triple oral steroid dose during fever; IM/IV if vomiting.
Do NOT wait for lab results. Give 100mg IV hydrocortisone + large volume 0.9% NaCl immediately for unexplained hypotensive shock.
Incidentaloma Ida
Dual Threat Matrix – Is it hormonally active? AND Is it malignant (>4cm, >10 Hounsfield Units)?
You MUST exclude phaeochromocytoma via plasma metanephrines before attempting any adrenal biopsy, or risk a fatal hypertensive crisis.
Insu the Insulin
Biphasic Release – Cleaves C-peptide from proinsulin to unlock the body’s only glucose-lowering mechanism.
Endogenous insulin = high C-peptide. Surreptitious exogenous insulin injection = undetectable C-peptide.
Gluca the Glucagon
Glycogenolysis – Mobilizes hepatic stores within minutes to fight severe hypoglycaemia.
Glucagon rescue injections fail in alcoholics or prolonged starvation because hepatic glycogen stores are already depleted.
T1D the Autoimmune
Absolute Deficiency – Without insulin, the body metabolizes itself into fatal acidosis.
DKA occurs readily in T1D because zero residual insulin means unopposed lipolysis. T2D rarely develops DKA due to residual insulin.
T2D the Resistance
The Slow Siege – Visceral fat drives resistance → hypersecretion → beta cell exhaustion.
Metformin is first line. Add GLP-1 RA if established ASCVD, Heart Failure independent of glucose.
Metty the Metformin
Weight Neutrality – Lowers fasting glucose without risking hypoglycaemia.
Hold metformin 48h for iodinated contrast; contrast-induced AKI causes drug accumulation, leading to rare but fatal lactic acidosis.
GLP-1 Gloria
Glucose-Dependent Satiety – Only releases insulin when glucose is high = low hypo risk.
Unmatched for weight loss and cardiovascular MACE reduction, but causes dose-dependent GI nausea and delays gastric emptying.
SGLT2 Stan
Osmotic Diuresis – Reduces HF hospitalizations and CKD progression independent of glucose.
Euglycaemic DKA (ketones high, glucose normal) and genital thrush are class effects. Watch for Fournier’s gangrene.
DPP-4 Dave
Enzyme Blockade – Modest oral incretin effect, weight neutral, safe.
Produces less effect than GLP-1 RAs because it only prevents degradation of physiological levels, rather than providing pharmacological super-doses.
Sulfo the Sulfonylurea
Glucose-Independent Release – High risk of severe hypoglycaemia + weight gain.
Avoid renally cleared glibenclamide in the elderly; metabolites accumulate causing prolonged, dangerous hypoglycaemia.
DKA the Crisis
FRIII Protocol – 0.1 units/kg/hr fixed rate insulin infusion.
Total body potassium is depleted despite presenting hyperkalaemia. Insulin drives K⁺ back into cells; you MUST add KCl to IV fluids!
HHS the Hyperosmolar
Profound Paralysis – Residual insulin prevents ketosis, allowing glucose to rise unchecked.
Replace fluids slowly (0.9% NaCl) to avoid cerebral oedema. Do NOT start insulin immediately unless glucose fails to fall with fluids alone. LMWH is essential!
Hypo the Warning
Autonomic Warning – Sweating and tremor precede neuroglycopenic coma.
Recurrent hypos cause Hypoglycaemia Unawareness — autonomic failure where the threshold drops and warning symptoms are lost.
Macrovascular Max
Endothelial Dysfunction – Diabetes triples ASCVD risk.
Glucose control prevents microvascular disease, but macrovascular protection requires high-intensity Statins, ACEI, and SGLT2I/GLP-1 RAs.
Complications Combo
AGEs & Polyol Pathway – Chronic glycation destroys small vessels and pericytes.
Loss of pain sensation (neuropathy) + repeated micro-trauma = painless foot ulcers and the radiologically destroyed Charcot joint.
The Diabetes Attending
Systemic Challenge – DKA electrolytes vs. eGFR drug limits vs. Fasting Hypo localization.
Map every decision to its pharmacological, physiological, or anatomical basis. No gestalt. Every answer needs a mechanism.
Osteo the Osteoporosis
Silent Collapse – Fracture threshold crossed without symptoms.
Denosumab stops osteoclasts, but stopping it causes massive rebound fractures. Never stop without transitioning to a bisphosphonate!
RANKL the Bone Regulator
Immune-Bone Coupling – Why inflammation melts bone.
Rheumatoid arthritis causes periarticular erosion via RANKL; anti-TNF biologics and Denosumab block this exact destruction pathway.
Hyper Calcium Harry
End-Organ Calcification – Bones, stones, groans, psychic moans.
Primary hyperparathyroidism = High PTH, High Ca. Malignancy = Low PTH, High Ca, High PTHrP. Treat severe with 3-4L 0.9% NaCl + IV Zoledronate.
Hypo Calcium Helle
Neuronal Trigger – Low calcium drops the threshold for action potentials.
Hypomagnesaemia impairs PTH release AND action. Refractory hypocalcaemia will not fix with calcium alone; you must check and replace Mg!
Renal Bone Renee
The Fatal Cascade – High FGF-23 → Low Calcitriol → Low Ca → Secondary Hyperparathyroidism.
Prolonged parathyroid stimulation becomes autonomous ('Tertiary'), causing high PTH even after a renal transplant!
Paget the Focal
Focal Chaos – Paracrine-driven local hyperactivity followed by disorganized repair.
Massively enlarged skull bone compresses the 8th cranial nerve, causing hearing loss. Treat with IV Zoledronate.
SIADH Sally
Inappropriate Retention – Small Cell Lung Cancer (ectopic ADH) secretly diluting the blood.
Correcting sodium too fast (>8-10 mmol/L/24h) causes Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome (locked-in syndrome). Restrict fluids.
Diabetes Insipidus Dana
Water Deprivation – Fails to concentrate urine when dehydrated.
Central DI responds to desmopressin. Nephrogenic (Lithium) does not. Paradoxically, thiazide diuretics reduce urine output in Nephrogenic DI!
Thyroid Cancer Tracy
Histological Destiny – Cytology dictates surgical approach and radioactive iodine strategy.
Follicular carcinoma is impossible to diagnose on FNA; you need whole histology to see capsular/vascular invasion!
MEN1 Marco
Secretin Paradox – Secretin normally inhibits gastrin, but causes a paradoxical MASSIVE RISE in gastrinoma.
MEN1 gastrinomas are multicentric. Stop PPIs before testing fasting gastrin, as PPIs artificially elevate it in everyone!
The Endocrinology Attending
Cross-Axis Integration – Primary hyperaldosteronism lateralization vs. Autoimmune polyglandular failure vs. MEN1 surgical limits.
Name the diagnosis, explain the mechanism, complete the investigation, and prescribe the treatment. Gestalt is dead.
DIY Epistemic Sabotage
Narrative Mnemonic – You remember stories, not lists.
Draw your own damn disease! If you can map the mechanism to a visual metaphor, you will never forget it on the wards. Stay fluffy!
Lisino-the-Pril (ACE Inhibitor)
The Pressure Drop.
Triggers Bradykinin (Cough). Watch for Angio-Edema-Annie & hyperkalemia.
Amlodi-the-Pine (Calcium Channel Blocker)
The Pipe-Relaxer.
Targeted at vessels, not the heart. Causes Edema-Eddie (swollen ankles).
Metopro-the-Lol (Beta-Blocker)
The Heart-Brake.
Excellent for Ischemic-Ache. Masks Hypo-Harry; triggers Asthma-Arthur if selectivity fails.
Lasix-the-Loop (Furosemide)
The Flood-Gate.
High-potency. Steals potassium (Hypo-K-Karl) and risks Oto-Toxic-Oliver at high doses.
Aspirin-the-Ace (Antiplatelet)
The Slip-and-Slide.
Lifetime commitment for Coronary-Canyons. Irritates Percy-the-Ulcer.
Rivaro-the-Ban (DOAC)
The Factor-Freeze.
No INR monitoring. Hard to reverse (needs Andexxa). Renal failure toxicity.
Heparin-the-Heavy (UFH/LMWH)
The Instant-Thin.
UFH needs the aPTT-Check. Watch out for HIT-the-Hunter.
Warf-the-Old-Guard (Warfarin)
The Slow-Bleed.
Requires the INR-Tether. Vulnerable to Food-Fights (greens). Teratogenic!
Metformi-the-Base (Biguanide)
The Sugar-Stopper.
No hypoglycemia risk! Rare but lethal Lactic-Lucy in renal failure.
Insu-the-Key (Insulin)
The Cell-Opener.
The Final-Boss for Type 2. Hypo-Harry is always lurking. Rotate sites!
Atorva-the-Statin (HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitor)
The Gunk-Cleaner.
Prevents the Clot-Pop. Can cause Myo-Muscle-Ache and Liver-Limp.
Levothyro-the-Pulse (T4 Replacement)
The Metabolism-Spark.
Take on an empty stomach! Excess causes Hyper-Hanna (palpitations).
Morphine-the-Monarch (Opioid)
The Pain-Eraser.
Gold standard for agony. Causes Consti-the-Sloth & Breathing-Ben's depression.
Ibupro-the-Brake (NSAID)
The Fire-Extinguisher.
Eats the stomach (Percy-the-Ulcer) and hits the kidneys (Renal-Ray).
Paraceta-the-Ghost (Acetaminophen)
The Fever-Killer.
Gentle on stomach, but has a Liver-Lethal limit (NAPQI toxicity).
Gabapenti-the-Numb (Neuropathic Ally)
The Nerve-Quietener.
Not for acute pain. Causes Dizzy-Dan and massive sleepiness.
Amoxi-the-Standard (Penicillin)
The Wall-Wrecker.
Watch for Allergy-Annie and Clostrid-the-Colitis (C. diff).
Ceftriaxo-the-Heavy (3rd Gen Cephalosporin)
The Meningitis-Mauler.
Go-To for serious Gram+ infections. Causes Biliary-Sludge.
Vancomy-the-Vault (Glycopeptide)
The MRSA-Masher.
Needs Trough-Levels to save kidneys. Watch for Red-Man-Ray.
Azithro-the-Macrolide
The Protein-Sapper.
The Z-Pak classic. Prolongs the QT-Interval-Clock!
Salbuta-the-Rescue (SABA)
The Airway-Opener.
Rapid onset. Causes Tremor-Tim and Tachy-Tina.
Flutica-the-Steward (ICS)
The Swelling-Stopper.
Chronic control. Must rinse mouth to avoid Thrush-the-Fungus.
Tiotro-the-LAMA (Anticholinergic)
The Secretion-Dryer.
24-hour airway management. Causes dry mouth and urinary retention.
Predni-the-Systemic (Oral Steroid)
The Total-Body-Cooler.
The Double-Edged Sword. Long-term: Buffalo-Hump-Herb & Thin-Skin-Thelma.
Omepra-the-PPI
The Acid-Lock.
Superior for Percy-the-Ulcer. Long-term drops Mg²⁺ and invites C-Diff.
Metoclopra-the-Mover (Prokinetic)
The Gut-Accelerator.
Crosses the BBB. Can cause The-Twitch (Extrapyramidal symptoms).
Ondansetro-the-Stopper (Antiemetic)
The Vomit-Shield.
Gold standard for chemo-nausea. Causes Consti-the-Sloth and QT prolongation.
Lactulo-the-Breeze (Osmotic Laxative)
The Water-Puller.
Also a Brain-Saver; traps ammonia to help Encephalo-Ed in liver failure.
Levodopo-the-Replacer
The Motion-Restorer.
Carbidopa protects it peripherally. Causes On-Off-Oscillations.
Pheny-the-Stabilizer (Phenytoin)
The Fire-Extinguisher.
Stops seizure firestorms. Causes Gingival-Gas (gum overgrowth).
Donepezi-the-Memorist (AChE Inhibitor)
The Signal-Booster.
Fights Alzheimer-Fog. Causes Wet-Symptoms (drooling, slow heart).
Sumatripta-the-Migraine-Mauler
The Vessel-Shrinker.
Not for heart disease patients—it constricts all pipes!
Diazepa-the-Bouncer (Benzodiazepine)
The Instant-Calm.
Dangerous with Alcohol. Highly addictive.
Sertrali-the-Mood-Lifter (SSRI)
The Happy-Reservoir.
Takes 4 weeks to work. Watch out for Serotonin-Syndrome.
Lithiu-the-Anchor (Mood Stabilizer)
The Seesaw-Stabilizer.
The Lithium-Level-Check is law. Toxic to Thyroid/Renal.
Haloperido-the-Lock (Antipsychotic)
The Dino-Handcuffs.
The Old Hammer. Causes Lead-Pipe-Rigidity (NMS) and The-Lean.
Spirono-the-Sparing (Diuretic)
The Potassium-Guard.
Essential for failing hearts. Can cause Mon-Boob-Mike.
Kay-the-Supplement (Potassium Chloride)
The Spark-Plug.
Replaces K-Tokens. NEVER give IV push, or the patient dies!
Calciu-the-Stabilizer (Calcium Gluconate)
The Heart-Shield.
Protects from Hyper-K-Karl. Doesn't lower K+, just buys time.
Bicarbonate-the-Buffer

Social-Solo-Sam

Hospice-the-Haven

Barthel-the-Butler

MMSE-the-Mental-Map

ISAR-the-Screener

Heart-Fail-the-Flood

Antidote-the-Vitamin-K

Hydration-the-Elixir

Mobilize-the-Now
The Stasis-Breaker. Shatters the grip of Sarcopenia-Wither and Pete-the-Pressure-Sore.

Nutri-the-Supplement

Direct combat against Malnutri-Molly. Food is medicine.
Social-the-Service

Reminiscence-the-Room

Visual and haptic stimuli forcefully stabilize neuronal orientation.
Physio-the-Fixer

Targeted rebuilding of postural core muscles and lost proprioception.
Ergo-the-Enabler

Adapting the physical world to match the patient's current abilities.
Logo-the-Voice

Vital mechanical rehabilitation of bulbar functions to prevent pneumonia.

The Holistic-Harmony. Synthesizes 50 data points into one safe discharge plan.
Treat the whole human. Start low, go slow. Is he safe at home? Stay Ruffy!

Spatial Logic

Uncle FrizzleBob's Golden Rule
Anatomy Anarchy
The body is a Rube Goldberg machine. Destroy the sterile flashcards. Learn the map!
Iron-Man Ian (Iron Metabolism)
The Hepcidin Lock. During inflammation, Ian is locked in the warehouse so Bacteria Pirates can't steal him.
Low Ferritin = Ian is broke. High Ferritin + Low TIBC = Ian is hoarding during chronic disease.
The Macro-Twins (B12-Bill & Folate-Phil)
The Megaloblastic Glitch. DNA fails to replicate, so they just grow fat without dividing.
Bill needs his VIP pass to enter the Terminal Ileum. No Bill = Nerve Damage. Phil is just a leafy-green local.
Sickle-Sam (HbS)
The Vaso-Occlusive Jam. Under stress (cold, acid, low O2), Sam stiffens into a blade and clogs the highway.
Protects against Malaria (The Parasite Tax) but shreds the Spleen (Autosplenectomy) by age 10.
Thal the Great (Thalassemia)
The Globin Imbalance. Missing chains make the hemoglobin lopsided and highly fragile.
Crew-cut skull X-ray because his bone marrow is working overtime to fix the mess.
G6PD-Pete (The Oxidative Victim)
The Fava Bean Trigger. Without his shield, Pete gets roasted by oxidative stress and sulfa-bombs.
X-linked. The Spleen-Bouncer bites out the oxidized junk (Heinz bodies), leaving bite cells.
Spherocyte Sid (Spectrin/Ankyrin Defect)
The Spleen Bait. Sid has no skeleton. The spleen despises perfect circles and destroys them.
High MCHC is the giveaway—he is packed too tight!
PNH-Paul (Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria)
The Midnight Hit. Without his anchor, the Complement hornets assume he's an intruder and pop him at night.
Look for the morning aftermath: dark urine from nighttime hemolysis.
Lead-Pipe Larry (Lead Poisoning)
The Enzyme Choke. Larry jams up ALAD and Ferrochelatase, shutting down the heme factory.
Causes sideroblastic anemia; ringed sideroblasts form as iron gets stuck in the mitochondria waiting for heme.
Epo-Eric (Erythropoietin)
The Hypoxic Scream. When O2 is low, Eric screams at the marrow to start mass-producing red cells.
If the kidneys fail, Eric dies, and the marrow sleeps (Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease).
Reticulocyte Rick (The Rookie)
The Marrow Metric. Rick is the raw recruit. If he's surging (>2%), the marrow is fighting the anemia.
If Rick is <1% during anemia, the marrow factory is broken or missing ingredients.
Haptoglobin Harry (The Janitor)
The Cleanup Crew. Harry binds free hemoglobin to save the kidneys from toxic damage.
If Harry is entirely missing from the blood, it means there was a massive murder (hemolysis) and he used himself up cleaning the mess.
Direct Coombs Carl (The Detective)
The Tag Reader. Carl detects if the immune system has placed a hit-marker on the body's own cells.
Direct Coombs looks for antibodies ALREADY attached to the RBC.
The Agglutinin Sisters (Cold Chloe & Warm Wally)
The Clump. Chloe clumps in the extremities (fingers/nose). Wally attacks at core body temperature.
Chloe = Mycoplasma (Walking Pneumonia). Wally = SLE or CLL.
Diamond-Blackfan Dan (Pure Red Cell Aplasia)
The Factory Strike. A congenital defect where the red cell assembly line simply never opens.
Look for physical anomalies: triphalangeal or absent thumbs combined with pure red cell aplasia in an infant.
Neutrophil Ned (The First Responder)
The Left Shift. When the bacterial war gets too big, Ned calls in his unbaked teenage brothers (Bands) to fight.
Red dies fast and turns into pus. Without him, the body is a wide-open fortress.
Eosinophil Eddie (The Pink Assassin)
The Toxic Granules. Eddie unleashes major basic protein to dissolve invaders too big to eat.
The star of the NAACP (Neoplasm, Allergy, Asthma, Collagen vascular disease, Parasites).
Basophil Benny (The Rarest)
The Hidden Trigger. Benny is incredibly rare; he dumps histamine to cause extreme vasodilation.
If Benny is elevated in the blood, DO NOT ignore it. Check for CML—he is often the hidden driver of the leukemia train.
Monocyte Monty (The Long-Termer)
The Tissue Transformation. Monty cruises the blood, but when he enters tissue, he transforms into the ultimate garbage disposal.
He eats the debris Ned leaves behind and presents the evidence to the T-cells.
Lymphocyte Lou (The Special Ops)
Adaptive Memory. Lou doesn't just kill; he remembers. He holds the blueprints for lifelong immunity.
Viral infections (like EBV/Mono) cause Lou to morph into giant, atypical reactive lymphocytes.
Aplastic Annie (The Empty House)
The Marrow Wipeout. The stem cells are annihilated. RBCs, WBCs, and platelets all crash to zero.
Bone marrow biopsy yields a Dry Tap (nothing but fat). Triggered by radiation, drugs, or Parvovirus B19.
Myelofibrosis Max (The Stone Maker)
The Fibrotic Squeeze. Max replaces the plush marrow with stiff collagen fibrosis.
Red blood cells must physically squeeze through the fibrotic stone to escape, permanently deforming into Teardrop Cells.
JAK2-Jake (The Constitutive Trigger)
The Unstoppable Signal. Jake ignores the off-switch. He tells the marrow to divide forever.
The root villain behind the Myeloproliferative Wars: Polycythemia Vera, Essential Thrombocythemia, and Myelofibrosis.
Polycythemia Paul (The Red Bloat)
The Viscous Sludge. Too many red cells turn the blood flow into thick, dangerous mud.
Patients get intensely itchy after a hot shower (aquagenic pruritus) due to mast cell degranulation.
Essential Toby (Thrombocythemia)
The Platelet Paradox. Toby makes massive amounts of dysfunctional platelets, causing simultaneous clotting and bleeding.
Diagnosis of exclusion. You must rule out reactive thrombocytosis (like iron deficiency or infection) first!
MDS-Manny (Myelodysplastic Syndrome)
The Pre-Leukemic Limbo. The marrow makes cells, but they are ugly, mutated, and die before leaving the factory.
High risk of transforming directly into Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
HLH-Hank (The Internal Cannibal)
The Cytokine Storm. The immune system goes rogue, and macrophages begin eating the body's own healthy blood cells.
Ferritin levels explode into the tens of thousands as Hank rampages. A true hematologic emergency.
Gaucher's Gary (The Crinkled Rhino)
The Lipid Trash Pile. Gary lacks the enzyme to break down lipids, so they accumulate inside macrophages.
Crinkled paper cytoplasm on biopsy. Severe hepatosplenomegaly and avascular necrosis of the femur.
Neupogen Nate (G-CSF)
The Chemo-Recovery. Nate artificially stimulates the marrow to pump out new neutrophils.
Deployed after brutal chemotherapy regimens to pull the patient out of the neutropenic danger zone.
The Marrow Bouncer (CD34+ Stem Cell)
The Origin Seed. Every single cell in the hematology universe starts by passing his check.
Target CD34+ cells for bone marrow transplants—they are the blank slates that rebuild the system.
Von Willebrand Vinny (The Glue)
The Platelet Bridge. Vinny connects platelets to the exposed collagen of a broken vessel wall.
Most common inherited bleeding disorder. Vinny also carries Factor VIII on his back to keep it from degrading.
Bernard-Soulier Ben (The Receptor Glitch)
The Sticky Failure. Ben's platelets are huge, but they lack the receptor to grab Vinny's glue.
Ristocetin test shows NO clumping. Unlike VWD, adding normal plasma does not fix Ben.
Glanzmann's Glenn (The Handshake Failure)
The Aggregation Block. Glenn has no handshakes, so platelets can stick to the wall, but CANNOT stick to each other.
Bleeding time is prolonged, but platelet count is completely normal.
ITP-Izzy (Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura)
The Anti-Platelet Hit. IgG antibodies mark platelets for death, and the spleen executes them.
The marrow responds by pumping out massive Megakaryocytes trying to replace the losses.
TTP-Terry (The Terrible Five)
The Micro-Clot Storm. Huge vWF multimers don't get chopped up, acting like massive spiderwebs that shred passing red cells (Schistocytes).
Remember FAT RK: Fever, Anemia (MAHA), Thrombocytopenia, Renal, Neuro symptoms.
HUS-Hugh (Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome)
The Toxin Shredder. Similar microthrombi to TTP, but triggered by undercooked meat toxins.
Typically hits children. Dominant symptoms are renal failure and bloody diarrhea; skips the neuro symptoms of TTP.
DIC-Dan (Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation)
The Paradox. The coagulation cascade fires everywhere at once, consuming all factors, resulting in massive bleeding elsewhere.
Sepsis, trauma, or obstetrical complications. PT and PTT are both elevated.
Hemophilia Harry (The Royal Bleeder)
The Intrinsic Break. The intrinsic cascade fails, preventing a solid secondary hemostatic plug.
X-linked recessive. Hallmark symptom is Hemarthrosis (deep bleeding into the joints). PT is normal!
Factor Seven Sam (The Extrinsic King)
The Spark. Sam triggers the entire clotting cascade the moment tissue damage exposes him to the blood.
He has the shortest half-life of all the factors. When Vitamin K drops, Sam is the first to die (PT rises first).
The Ten-Kicker (Common Pathway)
The Convergence. Whether the alarm was Intrinsic or Extrinsic, they all meet at Factor X to finish the job.
If the Common Pathway is broken, BOTH the PT and PTT times will be elevated.
Vitamin K-Kevin (The Mob Boss)
The Activator. The factors are useless, unarmed thugs until Kevin adds a carboxyl group so they can bind to calcium.
Neonates lack gut bacteria to make Kevin, which is why they get a Vitamin K shot at birth.
Warrick the Leaker (Warfarin)
The Epoxide Saboteur. Warrick halts the recycling of Vitamin K, slowly starving the cascade of active factors.
Because Protein C (the brake) drops first, Warrick causes a transient hypercoagulable state. Bridge with Heparin!
Hep the Heparin (The Enhancer)
The Immediate Halt. Hep binds to AT-III, instantly neutralizing Thrombin and Factor Xa.
Reversal agent is Protamine Sulfate. Watch out for HIT (Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia).
Protein C & S (The Breaks)
The Regulatory Stop. They ensure a clot doesn't keep growing until it blocks the entire blood vessel.
Deficiency means the patient is chronically hypercoagulable (prone to DVTs at a young age).
Factor V Leiden (The Unstoppable)
The Mutant Immunity. Factor V is mutated so that Protein C physically cannot cleave it. The brakes are broken.
The clotting cascade stays ON. Suspect in young, healthy patients presenting with unprovoked DVTs/PEs.
ABO-Arthur (The Antigen Guard)
The Universal Betrayal. O is the universal donor; AB is the universal recipient. Cross him, and you die.
Giving the wrong ABO type causes acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (preformed IgM antibodies attack instantly).
Rh-Rhonda (The Rhesus Mother)
The Second Baby Trap. Sensitization happens during the first birth. The antibodies wait to attack the next Rh(+) pregnancy.
Give RhoGAM at 28 weeks and postpartum to hide the Rh(+) signal and prevent sensitization.
TRALI-Tricia (Transfusion Lung Injury)
The White-Out. Donor antibodies attack the recipient's neutrophils in the pulmonary capillaries, flooding the lungs with fluid.
Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema occurring within 6 hours of a transfusion.
TACO-Tom (Circulatory Overload)
Pushing too much blood volume too fast overwhelms a weak heart.
Unlike TRALI, TACO presents with high blood pressure, JVD, and high BNP. Treat with diuretics.
The Spleen Bouncer (Filtration Plant)
The Quality Control. He removes inclusions (Howell-Jolly bodies) and destroys antibody-coated cells.
If removed, patients are fatally susceptible to encapsulated Ninja bacteria (Strep pneumo, Neisseria, H. flu). Vaccinate!
Fibrinogen Fred (The Final Glue)
The Hard Set. Thrombin cleaves Fred into Fibrin, turning the temporary platelet plug into a concrete wall.
Without Fred, the clot dissolves under blood pressure.
Plasminogen Pam (The Clot-Dissolver)
The Demolition. When activated by tPA, Pam becomes Plasmin and digests the fibrin clot to restore blood flow.
Administered clinically (tPA) for acute ischemic strokes, but contra-indicated if the patient is bleeding!
D-Dimer Dan (The Evidence)
The Breadcrumb Trail. Dan only exists if a massive clot was formed AND broken down.
Highly sensitive, not specific. A negative D-Dimer rules out a Pulmonary Embolism, but a positive one doesn't confirm it.
Epi the Epithelium
Barrier Seal. Blocks all non-lymphocyte tokens from crossing the board.
Basement membrane is Type IV collagen + laminin. Split it like a cheap rug, and you get Alport syndrome.
Brush Border Barney
Hyper-Absorb. Tap to digest and draw 3 nutrient cards.
Gluten wrecks Barney's hair (Villous atrophy = Coeliac disease). No hair, no absorption.
Clara the Ciliated
Mucociliary Escalator. Move 1 pathogen token to the Pharynx discard pile every turn.
Kartagener's syndrome = defective dynein arms. Immotile cilia mean chronic sinusitis and 50% chance of situs inversus.
Squamous Sue
Keratin Armor. Sacrifice top layer to negate mechanical or chemical damage.
Pemphigus vulgaris attacks the spines (desmoglein-3) in the stratum spinosum, causing suprabasal blisters.
Urothelial Ulrich
Shape-Shift. Change form to nullify chemical burns from urine tokens.
Umbrella cells use uroplakin to stop urea back-diffusion. Visible haematuria? Look out for urothelial carcinoma.
Gland Greta
Exocrine Eruption. Deal heavy enzymatic damage to food tokens.
Parotid is purely serous (dark). Sublingual is predominantly mucous (pale). Sjögren's kills the acini.
Goblet the Glycoprotein
Mucin Blast. Create a 2-layer protective gel field.
Goblet cells in the oesophagus? That's Barrett's intestinal metaplasia. Risk of adenocarcinoma goes up.
Type II Pneumocyte Pete
Surfactant Synthesis. Reduce alveolar surface tension to 0. Prevent collapse.
Premmies lack Pete's surfactant, causing Respiratory Distress Syndrome. Antenatal steroids speed up Pete's maturation.
Mesothelial Mia
Frictionless Glide. Nullify organ Friction.
Asbestos fibres pierce her, causing 20-50 year latency Mesothelioma.
Endothelial Eddie
Gatekeeper. Control leukocyte rolling and vascular tone (NO).
Liver sinusoids lack a basement membrane and have large fenestrae for free exchange.
Collagen Carl
Tensile Strength. Grant indestructible structural scaffolding.
Glycine is every 3rd position. No Vitamin C = poor prolyl hydroxylation = Scurvy (unstable collagen, bleeding).
Fibro the Fibroblast
Matrix Remodel. Transform into Myofibroblast to contract wounds.
Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency allows neutrophil elastase to eat Fibro's elastin, causing emphysema.
Macro the Macrophage
Tissue Adaptation. Gain specific abilities based on organ zone.
Heart failure causes pulmonary alveolar macrophages to eat leaked RBCs to become haemosiderin-laden heart failure cells.
Mast Cell Mona
Degranulation. Instantly inflict massive vasodilation and bronchospasm.
Leukotrienes cause more sustained asthma and bronchospasm than histamine.
Adipose Ada
Thermogenesis / Satiety. Generate heat or suppress appetite.
Brown fat uses UCP1 to uncouple electron transport, making heat instead of ATP.
Cartilage Carla
Compressive Resistance. Absorb massive mechanical loads.
Chondrocytes have NO blood vessels; they heal terribly. Loss of Carla in joints = Osteoarthritis eburnation.
Bone Barry
Remodel. Couple osteoclast destruction with osteoblast creation.
Paget's disease shows chaotic mosaic cement lines and giant abnormal osteoclasts.
Elastic Ellie
Recoil. Return stretched tissue to resting state instantly.
Marfan syndrome = FBN1 (fibrillin) mutation. Poor scaffold leads to aortic root dissection and lens subluxation.
Sarco the Sarcomere
Cross-Bridge Cycle. Consume 1 ATP to deal massive mechanical force.
No ATP after death = myosin can't detach from actin = Rigor mortis.
Cardiac Carla
Functional Syncytium. Share electrical action potentials instantly.
