Nelly the Neutrophil
Oxidative Burst.
Arrives first via IL-8. Uses NADPH oxidase to make superoxide (HOCl). CGD patients lack this enzyme, suffering recurrent catalase-positive infections.
Mack the Macrophage
Polarization.
M1 (IFN-γ-activated): kills pathogens with ROS, M2 (IL-4/IL-13-activated): promotes healing and fibrosis. Presents antigens on MHC II to CD4+ T cells.
Denise the Dendritic Cell
Cross-Presentation.
The most powerful APC. Can uniquely present exogenous viral antigens on MHC I to prime naive CD8+ T cells in the lymph node.
NK the Natural Killer
Missing Self Detection.
Kills virally infected or tumor cells that downregulate MHC I to hide from T cells. Uses perforin/granzyme. Performs ADCC via CD16.
Compy the Complement
The Unstoppable Cascade.
Classical, Lectin, and Alternative pathways converge on C3b opsonization and C5b-9 (MAC lysis). Regulated by CD55 (DAF) and CD59.
Anna Anaphylatoxin
C3a: Panic. C5a: Chaos.
The alarm signals. C3a strongly attracts neutrophils and triggers mast cells. In sepsis, massive C5a causes simultaneous inflammation and neutrophil immunosuppression.
Interferoni the Type I Interferon
Viral Early Warning.
Triggered by viral nucleic acids. Signals via JAK-STAT to upregulate PKR (blocks viral translation) and increase MHC I expression on adjacent cells.
Infla the Inflammation
Controlled Chaos.
Vasodilation (histamine) → Permeability (bradykinin) → Diapedesis (selectins/integrins). Resolves via IL-10/TGF-β or progresses to chronic fibrosis.
Granny Granuloma
The Walled Garden.
Built by macrophages + Th1 cells (IFN-γ) when acute clearance fails. Anti-TNF therapy (infliximab) destroys the wall, risking fatal reactivation of latent Tb.
Tommy T Cell
The Two-Signal Verification.
Signal 1 = TCR + MHC. Signal 2 = Co-stimulation (CD28 + CD80/86). Without Signal 2, the T cell enters anergy (permanent shutdown).
Theo Th1
Macrophage Recruitment.
Fights intracellular pathogens. Secretes IFN-γ to supercharge macrophages and upregulate MHC II. Drives delayed-type hypersensitivity and autoimmune tissue damage.
Tara Th2
Parasite Purge.
Driven by IL-4. Secretes IL-4 (IgE class switch), IL-5 (eosinophil activation), and IL-13. The primary driver of Type I hypersensitivity (allergy/asthma).
Rex Treg
Civil War Prevention.
Suppresses immunity via IL-10, TGF-β, and CTLA-4 contact. FoxP3 mutation causes IPEX syndrome (lethal multi-organ autoimmunity in infant boys).
Barb B Cell
Class Switch Recombination.
AID enzyme alters heavy chains. T-cell help (CD40L) is required for memory and switching. BTK mutation causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia (no mature B cells).
Iggy Immunoglobulin
Fc Effector Module Swapping.
IgM (pentamer, immediate complement activator), IgG (most abundant, crosses placenta), IgA (dimer, mucosal), IgE (mast cell bound, allergies).
Sadie the Cytotoxic T Cell
Perforin Punch.
Recognizes antigens on MHC I. Kills via perforin (pores) + granzyme B (apoptosis). PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint exhaustion in tumors.
Memo the Memory Cell
Rapid Recall.
Lower activation threshold, larger clone size, and tissue-resident persistence (TRM cells). Basis of vaccine immunity and the germinal center reaction.
Cyndy Cytokine
Escalation.
IL-8: neutrophil by NLRP3 inflammasome. IL-6 drives CRP in liver, elevated in COVID-19. TNF-α drives cachexia and sepsis. Suppressed by IL-10.
Kylie Cytokine Storm
Hyperferritinemic Rampage.
Uncontrolled IL-6, IFN-γ, macrophage amplification. In primary HLH, missing lymphocyte perforin prevents CTLs from shutting off the loop.
Gell and Coombs
The Four Mischiefs.
I: Immediate IgE. II: Antibody-mediated surface cytotoxicity. III: Soluble immune complex depositing in tissues. IV: Delayed cell-activated (48-72h).
Ana Anaphylaxis
Immediate Degranulation.
Allergen cross-links IgE on mast cells. Preformed histamine causes immediate vasodilation/bronchoconstriction. Epinephrine 1:1000 IM is the only first-line rescue (reverses shock via α1/β1/β2).
Hemo the Hemolytic
Friendly Fire MAC.
Antibodies attack specific cell surfaces. Causes Goodpasture's (anti-GBM), Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia, and Myasthenia Gravis (receptor blockade without direct lysis).
Icko Immune Complex
Glomerular Trap.
IgG complexes form in blood during antigen excess. They deposit in small vessels (glomeruli, synovium) = complement activation + neutrophil destruction (e.g., SLE, Serum Sickness).
Della Delayed
Th1 Grudge.
Cell-mediated, no antibodies! CD4+ Th1 cells recognize antigen, secrete IFN-γ, and activate macrophages. Drives contact dermatitis, tuberculin skin test, and Type 1 Diabetes.
Allie Allergy
The Allergic March.
Epithelial defect → Th2 dominance (IL-4/IL-5/IL-13). Allergen immunotherapy desensitizes by shifting the response from Th2 to Treg and inducing IgG4 blocking antibodies.
Masto the Mast Cell
Leukotriene Sustenance.
Activation releases preformed histamine (minutes). Newly synthesized leukotrienes (hours later) cause bronchoconstriction 1000x more potent than histamine. Blocked by montelukast.
Eosie the Eosinophil
Major Basic Toxicity.
Releases Major Basic Protein (MBP) to kill helminths. Driven by IL-5 (Blocked therapeutically by mepolizumab). Causes tissue remodeling in asthma and Hypereosinophilic Syndrome.
Lupi the Lupus
The Great Imitator.
Defective apoptotic cell clearance exposes nuclear antigens. TLR9/TLR7 activate Type I IFN and autoantibody production. Treat all patients with hydroxychloroquine.
Rhea Rheumatoid
Pannus Invasion.
Synovial inflammation drives invasive pannus formation → cartilage/bone erosion. Anti-CCP antibodies (ACPA) are highly specific. Synovial fluid is neutrophil-rich with low glucose.
Sid Sjögren
Glandular Drought.
Lymphocytic infiltration destroys salivary/lacrimal glands (anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB). Causes extreme xerostomia/dry eyes, and can cause Type 1 Renal Tubular Acidosis.
Scleroder Max
Fibrosis Architecture.
Endothelial injury → Raynaud's → TGF-β driven fibrosis. Diffuse (anti-Scl-70, early ILD) vs. Limited (anti-centromere). Renal crisis MUST be treated with ACE inhibitors despite AKI.
Inflamma the Myopathy
CD8+ Friendly Fire.
Polymyositis: CD8+ CTLs destroy muscle expressing aberrant MHC I. Dermatomyositis: Type I IFN drives microangiopathy (Gottron's papules, heliotrope rash). Anti-Jo-1 = antisynthetase syndrome.
Vascy Vasculitis
Caliber Classification.
Large (Giant Cell Arteritis = blindness risk, immediate steroids). Medium (PAN, Kawasaki). Small (ANCA-associated: GPA/Wegener's = PR3; MPA = MPO).
Betty B27
The Backdoor Spondyloarthropathy.
HLA-B27 misfolding triggers the IL-23/IL-17 axis. Causes AS, Psoriatic, Reactive (can't see, pee, climb a tree), and IBD-arthritis. Sacroiliitis and enthesitis are hallmarks.
Thyra Thyroid
Receptor Mimicry.
Hashimoto's: Th1-mediated destruction → hypothyroidism. Graves' IgG mimics TSH, continually activating the receptor → hyperthyroidism and proptosis (orbital fibroblasts express TSH-R).
Diab the Type 1
The Honeymoon Illusion.
CD8+ T cell-mediated destruction of beta cells. Anti-GAD65/IA-2 are markers, not the pathogenic drivers. Teplizumab (anti-CD3) can delay clinical onset in high-risk patients.
Good the Goodpasture
Linear IF Strike.
IgG antibodies directly attack the GBM/alveolar membrane. Causes pulmonary hemorrhage + Rapidly Progressive GN. Immunofluorescence shows smooth, LINEAR IgG deposition.
Scid the Severe Combined
Complete Void.
Complete failure of T-cell development (and often B/NK cells). Fatal if given live vaccines (e.g., BCG-fatal). Maternal T-cells crossing the placenta can cause fatal GVHD in the infant.
Aggie Agammaglobulinemia
Encapsulated Vulnerability.
Pro-B fails to transition to pre-B. No mature B cells, no tonsils, no germinal centers. Highly susceptible to encapsulated bacteria (pneumococcus, H. influenzae) after maternal IgG fades at 6 months.
Cody Common Variable
Late-Onset Failure.

Normal B-cell numbers but defective antibody production (low IgG/IgA). Paradoxically presents with recurrent sinopulmonary infections, severe autoimmunity (cytopenias), and highly increased lymphoma risk.
Comple Complement Deficiency
Neisseria Target.
MAC deficiency (C5-C9) specifically predisposes to meningococcal/gonococcal infections. C1-INH deficiency causes bradykinin-driven hereditary angioedema (unresponsive to epinephrine).
Trans the Transplant
Graft-vs-Host Betrayal.
Hyperacute rejection is driven by preformed donor-specific antibodies (prevented by crossmatching). GVHD occurs when donor T-cells attack recipient tissues (skin, gut, liver).
Cyclo the Cyclosporin & Tacrolimus
Calcineurin Blockade.
Bind cyclophilin/FKBP12 → inhibit calcineurin → block NFAT dephosphorylation → prevent IL-2 transcription. Highly nephrotoxic (afferent arteriolar constriction).
Rapa the mTOR
G1-S Barricade.
Binds FKBP12 to inhibit mTOR. Blocks IL-2-driven T-cell proliferation (not production). Non-nephrotoxic. Impairs wound healing, used post-transplant and for CAR-[T].
Myco the Mycophenolate
De Novo Starvation.
Inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH). Selectively starves T and B cells, which uniquely rely entirely on de novo purine synthesis and lack a salvage pathway. Teratogenic.
Anti-TNF the Alliance
Granuloma Breaker.
Blocks TNF-α signaling. Highly effective for RA and IBD. Because TNF maintains granulomas, blockade risks fatal reactivation of latent TB. (Etanercept is a decoy receptor, fails in IBD).
Check the Checkpoint
Brake Release.
Anti-CTLA-4 (Ipilimumab) and anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab) remove inhibitory brakes on T-cells to fight tumors. Causes severe immune-related adverse events (irAEs) like colitis and pneumonitis.
Jak the JAK Inhibitor
Multi-Cytokine Silence.
Blocks intracellular JAK-STAT signaling, silencing dozens of cytokine signals simultaneously. Causes high risk of Varicella Zoster (shingles) reactivation—check immunity before starting.
IL-17 Ivan
Epithelial Bodyguard.
IL-17 (from Th17) drives psoriasis and ankylosing spondylitis (axSpA). Anti-IL-17A is effective in skin/joints but worsens Inflammatory Bowel Disease because IL-17 is protective in the GI mucosa.
Cell the Cellular Pathology
Adaptation.
Apoptosis is clean. Necrosis is inflammatory. Coagulative necrosis (ischemia) leaves ghost outlines. Liquefactive necrosis (brain/abscesses) causes enzymatic self-digestion.
Nec Necroptosis & Pyroptosis
Programmed Inflammation.
Death that shouts. Pyroptosis: inflammasome → caspase-1 → IL-1β release via gasdermin pores. Gain-of-function NLRP3 mutations cause CAPS (treat with anakinra).
Ferri the Fibrosis
Rogue Healing.
Persistent TGF-β signaling activates Smad2/3 → fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition → excessive architectural collagen (e.g., IPF, Cirrhosis). Pirfenidone blocks this pathway.
Onco the Oncogenesis
The Ten Broken Rules.
Hallmarks include immune evasion, replicative immortality, and the Warburg effect (aerobic glycolysis). Tumors actively recruit M2 macrophages and Tregs to suppress the local immune response.
The Immunology Attending
Master Clinical Synthesis.
The ultimate quest: Every drug, mechanism, and pathology card interacts. If you give Anti-TNF to a RA patient, you disable Granny Granuloma. If you lack BTK, you lose Barb B-Cell.
ARDS-the-Alveolar-Axe
The Wet-Lung-Wallop. Axe floods the alveoli with protein-rich Sludge, turning the lungs into stiff, unexpandable Stone.
Cytokine-driven damage to the alveolar-capillary barrier creates Baby Lungs — small patches of functional tissue in a sea of collapse.
PEEP-the-Prop
The Balloon-Support. Keeps the tiny Alveolar-Balloons from snapping shut at the end of every breath.
Increases Functional Residual Capacity. Caveat: Too much PEEP crushes the Heart-Pump (Decreases Preload).
Vent-the-Vandal
The Over-Stretch. Pushes too much air into too little lung, tearing tissue apart.
Volutrauma and Barotrauma. Turn Protective-Ventilation into Destructive-Air-Hammer.
Prone-the-Pivot
The Gravity-Flip. Let the Back-Lungs breathe while the Front-Lungs rest.
Homogenizes and strain. Moves the weight of the heart and get off the dorsal alveoli to improve the Ventilation-Perfusion-Match.
Norad-the-North-Star
The Pressure-Anchor. Clamps the leaky Peripheral-Pipes to ensure the Brain-and-Heart-Vaults stay pressurized.
The Vasopressor of Choice. Increases MAP without over-revving the heart-engine.
Dobuta-the-Dynamo
The Piston-Push. Screams at the failing heart-engine to squeeze harder.
Used in Cardiogenic-Carl. Caveat: It's a vasodilator — he might drop the MAP while boosting the flow.
Art-Line-the-Archer
The Real-Time-Radar. Gives the Beat-by-Beat truth, profiling every Pulse-Pressure-Variation.
Allows for frequent blood gases. If the waveform Dampens, the Archer is hitting a wall or pipes are kinked.
Swan-the-Ganz
The Deep-Diver. Swims through the heart into the lungs to see the pressure in the Left-Atrium-Lobby.
Differentiates Heart-Failure-Flood from Septic-Leak. Rare now, but essential for Complex-Cases.
CRRT-the-Constant
The 24-Hour-Sieve. Slowly cleans the blood, removing Toxin-Tokens without crashing the blood pressure.
Gentle. Mimics the natural kidney for wrestlers who are too unstable for a fast Flush.
Hyper-K-the-Killer
The Electrical-Eraser. Shorts out the heart's wiring, leading to the Sine-Wave-Silence.
Stops the resting membrane potential. Treat with Calcium-the-Shield to protect wires, then Insulin-the-Evictor.
Acid-the-Abyss
The Protein-Malter. Turns the blood sour, causing Pressor-Ponies to stop and the heart to stumble.
A sign of Tissue-Starvation. If the cells can't breathe, they vomit acid. A signal of Energy-Failure.
Citrate-the-Clot-Stopper
The Machine-Shield. Eats the calcium in the dialysis circuit so blood doesn't Clot-the-Filter.
Regional means it only works inside the machine. Caveat: If the liver can't process it, causes Calcium-Crashing.
Septic-Sam
The Capillary-Collapse. Opens all Volume-Valves and turns vessel-walls into Leaky-Cheese.
Immune-overdrive causes massive vasodilation. Blood hides in Peripheral-Puddles, leaving the brain dry.
Procal-the-Predictor
The Bacterial-Beacon. Glows bright when Bacterial-Punks are in the blood, dim for Viral-Vandals.
Guides when to start — and when to stop — the Antibiotic-Artillery.
Lactate-the-Debt-Collector
The Hypoxia-Tax. Represents the Oxygen-Debt from failing aerobic metabolism.
High Lactate = Tissue Ischemia. Clearing the Lactate proves the Resuscitation-Rescue is winning.
Source-Control-the-Striker
The Root-Removal. Knows that Antibiotic-Ammo fails if the Nest isn't destroyed.
Ibi pus, ibi evacuo. (If there is pus, drain it). If the line is dirty, pull it.
ICP-the-Intracranial-Pressure
The Skull-Squeeze. Swelling brain crushes the Oxygen-Entry-Vessels.
The skull is a Closed-Box. If ICP reaches MAP, the Brain-Death-Bell rings.
Osmotic-the-Osmotic
The Water-Sucker. Pulls water out of swollen brain-tissue and into the blood.
Creates an Osmotic-Gradient. Caveat: Mannitol causes Diuresis-Drain, 3% Saline keeps volume in pipes.
Propofol-the-Milk
The Mainframe-Mute. Puts the brain to sleep and covers the Oxygen-Burn-Rate.
Allows the Daily-Wake-Up-Test. Caveat: PRIS (Infusion Syndrome) causes acidosis and heart failure.
Dex-the-Precedex
The Conscious-Calm. Provides Analgo-Sedation — sleepy but can answer the Neuro-Check.
Doesn't stop the breathing-drive. Great for Ventilator-Weaning. Caveat: Can cause Brady-Bill (Slow heart).
TPN-the-Total-Parental
The Vein-Feed. Bypasses the Gut-Gate to feed directly through the blood.
The Last Resort. TPN loves the Liver-Limp and Line-Infection-Ingles. If the gut works, use the gut!
Stress-Ulcer-the-Shadow
The Acid-Erosion. Eats the stomach lining during the Stress-Storm, causing a Hidden-Bleed.
Prevented by PPI-the-Lock or H2-the-Hinderer.
Ileus-the-Idle
The Static-Snake. Intestines stop moving, causing Belly-Bloat and Vomitus-Vex.
Often caused by Opioid-Overload or Electrolyte-Emptying.
Liver-the-Limp
The Detox-Failure. Stops cleaning the blood, letting Ammonia-the-Fog cloud the brain.
Watch for Cerebral-Edema-Swelling. It is a race for the Transplant-Train.
DIC-the-Disseminated
The Clot-and-Bleed. Uses up all Clot-Tokens in tiny, useless fights, leaving nothing for Major-Leaks.
A Consumption-Coagulopathy. Treat the underlying Sam-Sepsis to stop the spiral.
Platelet-the-Plug
The Hole-Stoppage. The first line of defense against Capillary-Leaks.
In the ICU, Plugs get eaten by Sam-Sepsis and Spleen-the-Sponge.
FFP-the-Flow
The Liquid-Gold. Restores the Coagulation-Cascade when the INR-Alarm is ringing.
Essential for Wart-Reversal and Massive-Hemorrhage.
TEG-the-Thromboelastography
The Real-Time-Clot-Movie. Tells exactly why blood isn't clotting: Factor-Failure, Platelet-Pouchy, or Fibrin-Frenzy.
Guided Goat-Directed-Therapy. Don't guess — TEG it!
Hydrocort-the-Sepsis-Support
The Vessel-Sensitizer. Helps the Norad-Pressor work better by making vessels sensitive to the signal.
Replaces Relative-Adrenal-Insufficiency.
Dantrolene-the-Inferno-Cooler
The Calcium-Cutter. Stops the Muscle-Meltdown in Malignant Hyperthermia.
Prevents the runaway release of calcium from the Sarcoplastic-Silo.
Sugamma-the-Reverser
The Muscle-Wake-Up. Grabs Paralyzer-Punks and drags them away from the Nerve-Junction.
Immediate reversal of neuromuscular blockade. No Wet-Side Effects like Neostigmine.
Fentanyl-the-Fast-Acting
The Surgical-Calm. The go-to for continuous Analgesia-Infusion in the ventilated wrestler.
Rapid onset. Caveat: Causes Chest-Wall-Rigidity-DIFF if pushed too fast.
Ringer-the-Balanced
The Physiological-Fill. The Gold Standard for filling the Septic-Tank.
Closer to blood than Normal-Saline-the-Salty, which can cause Chloride-Acid-Abyss.
Albumin-the-Colloid
The Water-Magnet. Stays in the Pipe-Highway and pulls fluid out of the Tissue-Swamps (Edema).
Used when crystalloids fail or after large-volume Ascites-Draining.
Diuresis-the-Dry-Down
The Squeeze-Out. Removes the Extra-Weight post-shock to let the lungs breathe.
Lasix-the-Lasix is the main tool. Being Too-Wet increases the Ventilator-Time.
PLR-the-Leg-Lift
The Fluid-Challenge-Without-Fluid. Tells if the heart wants more volume before you pour it in.
The Reversible-Auto-Transfusion. If MAP goes up, the heart is Fluid-Responsive.
Re-Intubate-the-Panic
The Emergency-Return. When the Golden-Tube is removed too early and the Airway-Assassins return.
High-risk move. Swelling (Edema) makes the second pass much harder than the first.
Tension-the-Tony
The Machine-Induced-Crush. The ventilator Pops a lung-blob, squeezing the heart.
Always disconnect the vent first in sudden PEA to rule out Auto-PEEP or Tension-Tony.
HIT-the-Hunter
The Clot-Irony. Makes platelets clump together while numbers drop, causing Venous-and-Arterial-Jams.
Immune-mediated riot. Stop Heparin immediately and use Argatroban-the-Alternative.
PE-the-Phantom
The Highway-Block. A clot-monster from the Leg-Deep-Veins jams the Lung-Entrance.
In the ICU, the Phantom is often completely silent until it is too late.
VAP-the-Vent-Pneumonia
The Machine-Breach. Bacterial-Punks crawl down the Golden-Tube to start a riot.
Prevented by Head-Up-Position and Oral-Chlorhexidine-Cloe.
CLABSI-the-Line-Infection
The IV-Invasion. Staph-the-Skin-Steward enters the Blood-Highway through the CVC-Portal.
Scrub the Hub! If the line is infected, it must be Evicted.
C-Diff-the-Colitis
The Gut-Explosion. Takes over the Bowel-Basement after Antibiotic-Artillery kills the good guards.
Smells like a Horse-Barn. Treat with Vanomy-the-Vault (Oral).
ESKAPE-the-Superbugs
The Armor-Plated-Punks. Multidrug-Resistance shields laugh at standard Antibiotic-Ammo.
They use Efflux-Pumps and Enzyme-Blasters (Carbapenemases) to survive.
Wean-the-Wrestler
The Test-Drive. The machine steps back, letting the wrestler breathe alone for 30-120 mins.
Passes if the Heart-Rate and Work-of-Breathing remain stable and low.
Delirium-the-Daze
The Hallucination-Haze. Makes the wrestler see Shadow-Monsters and pull at their tubes.
Caused by Sleep-Sabotage, Benzodiazepine-Bouncers, and Sam-Sepsis.
PICS-the-Post-ICU-Struggle
The Long-Shadow. The wrestler remains weak and forgetful for months after leaving the Vital-Vigil.
ICU-Acquired-Weakness. The muscles melted away during the long sleep.
Comfort-Care-the-Transition
The Peaceful-Exit. When the Scrimmage is lost, focus shifts to a Quiet-Mat without pain.
Withdrawal of Life-Sustaining Treatment. Morphine and Midazolam ensure the final breath is soft.
The CVC-Cavalry
The Main-Line. Allows for Pressor-Pumps, TPN-Feeding, and Fast-Fluid-Filling.
Allows CVP monitoring. Caveat: Watch for Pneumo-the-Puncture during placement.
The Foley-Sentry
The Organ-Perfusion-Monitor. Tells the surgeon if Kidney-Filters are getting enough Blood.
Oliguria-the-Small-Flow is the very first sign of Shock-Sam.
The Dialysis-Disaster
The Panic-Drain. When the body's filters fail completely and the AEIOU-Alarms ring.
High potassium or pulmonary edema that won't respond to Lasix requires the machine NOW.
The ECMO-the-Extra-Lung
The Ultimate-Bypass. Takes blood outside the body, gasses it with oxygen, and pumps it back.
The Highest-Level-Support. Buys weeks of time for the biological heart or lungs to heal.
The ICU Attending
The Meta-Physiologist.
Is the CO2 rising? Is the MAP holding? Is the Lactate clearing? Balance the system! Stay fluffy!
FrizzleBob's Quest 1
The Acid-Blockade.
Identify the Sensitivity-Tool to help pressors work (Hydrocort-Support) and the Brain-Tool for the acid (CRRT-the-Constant).
FrizzleBob's Quest 2
The Air-Trap.
Identify the Machine-Induced-Killer (Tension-the-Tony). The very first move: Disconnect the Vent!
FrizzleBob's Quest 3
The Sarcoplasmic-Fire.
Identify the Inland-Inferno (Malignant Hyperthermia) and deploy the Calcium-Cutter (Dantrolene-the-Inferno-Cooler).
Pump-Fail-Pelican
The Fluid-Flood. Pelican can't push the water forward, so it backs up into the Lung-Balloons, cansing the Drown-Gasp.
When the Heart-Engine loses its Squeeze-Power, hydrostatic pressure forces fluid into the alveoli.
Rhythm-Riot-Raccoon
The Chses-Quiver. Raccoon makes the Atrial-Chambers twitch randomly. This stops the Steady-Drammer and creates Clot-Monsters.
Re-entrant electrical loops in the atria lead to an Irregularly-Irregular ventricular response.
Squeeze-Stall-Shark
The Oxygen-Starve. Shark bites down on a Coronary-Pipe, stopping the Fuci-Flow. The engine starts to Recrosis-Melt.
Plaque rupture leads to thrombus formation, cutting off blood supply.
Valve-Leak-Vulture
The Back-Splash. Every time the heart squeezes, Vulture lets half the blood leak backward into the Lung-Chambers.
Ioceapetent mitral valve leaflets allow retrograde flow during systels.
Obstruct-the-Ox
The Air-Trap. Ox gets air in, but can't get Waste-Smoke out. He becomes Hyper-Inflated.
Loss of elastic recoil and airway narrowing leads to air trapping and chronic Acid-Base-War.
Spasm-the-Spider
The Narrow-Clench. Spider weaves Muscle-Webs around the Airway-Tunnels, making every breath a Whistle-Scream.
Reversible bronchoconstriction triggered by Allergy-Alarms or Cold-Air-Sparks.
Clot-the-Cobra
The Lung-Strike. Cobra travels from Leg-Veins and bites the Main-Lung-Pipe, stopping Gas-Exchange instantly.
DVT embolizes to the pulmonary arteries, causing a Dead-Space-Glitch.
Moni-the-Muck-Monster
The Alveoli-Gunk. Moni fills Lung-Balloons with Infection-Sludge, blocking Osyra-the-Oaygen.
Bacterial or viral invasion causes inflammatory exudate to fill the alveolar spaces.
Sweet-the-Sugar-Bear
The Honey-Blood. Bear floods Blood-River with Sugar-Tokens, Caramelizing Nerves and Kidney-Filters.
Insulin resistance or deficiency leads to chronic hyperglycemia and microvascular damage.
Thyroid-the-Throttle-Toad
The Speed-Dial. Toad turns System-Velocity to 100 (Sweating/Racing) or 0 (Freezing/Sluggish).
Thyroid hormones regulate basal metabolic rate and the synthesis of Na+/K+ ATPases.
Corti-the-Crush-Camel
The Stress-Hump. Carries body through Long-Sieges. Too much = Moon-Face-Buffer; Too little = Pressure-Crash.
Glucocorticoids regulate glucose metabolism, immune response, and vascular tone.
Calci-the-Bone-Bat
The Mineral-Drain. Bat sucks calcium out of Bone-Pillars, dumping it into Bleed-River. Causes Brain-Fog.
Hyperparathyroidism or Malignsncy-associated PTftrp increases esteoclast activity.
Krea-the-Clog-Crab
The Filter-Stall. Crab sits in Kidney-Fortress and pinches Waste-Pipes shut. Urea-Trash builds up.
Reduced nephron function leads to the accumulation of nitrogenous waste and electrolyte chaos.
Sodium-the-Salt-Seal
The Brain-Swell. Seal pulls water into Brain-Cells, causing Confusion-Daze or Seizure-Sparks if salt drops.
Osmotic shifts across the blood-brain barrier due to hypotonicity.
Potass-the-Spark-Python
The Heart-Short-Circuit. Python wraps Heart-Wires. Too tight = Engine-Stop; Too loose = Chaos-Rhythm.
Potassium dictates resting membrane potential. Deviations lead to lethal arrhythmias.
Bicarb-the-Buffer-Beaver
The Acid-Dam. Beaver builds Base-Dams to stop the Acid-Flood from melting System-Enzymes.
Renal compensation for metabolic or respiratory acidosis through bicarbonate reabsorption.
Cirrho-the-Scar-Snake
The River-Block. Squeezes Liver-Roads, forcing blood into Esophagus-Veins and leaking fluid into Belly-Basin.
Fibrosis increases portal vascular resistance, leading to porto-systemic shunting.
Ulcer-the-Ant-Acid
The Wall-Erosion. Eats through Stomach-Armor, causing Burning-Pain or The-Black-Stool-Bleed.
Imbalance between protective factors (mucus/bicarb) and aggressive factors (acid/pepsin).
IBD-the-Internal-Fire
The Gut-Riot. Immune-Army gets confused and attacks Intestinal-Walls, causing Bloody-Brawls and Tunnel-Blocks.
Chronic transmural or mucosal inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract.
Pancre-the-Self-Eater
The Chemical-Burn. Accidentally releases Digestive-Tigers inside own house, melting Abdominal-Arena.
Premature activation of pancreatic enzymes leading to autodigestion and systemic inflammation.
Anemi-the-Pale-Panda
The Energy-Drought. Panda has too few Red-Cell-Trucks to carry Oxyra-the-Oxygen. Wrestler becomes Weak-and-Pale.
Decreased red cell mass leads to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.
Clot-the-Kraken
The Leg-Anchor. Wakes up in Deep-Leg-Veins, stopping Blood-Return and waiting to jump to the lungs.
Virchow's Triad: Stasis, Endothelial Injury, Hypercoagulability.
Lympho-the-Lump-Lynx
The Gland-Invasion. Lynx makes Lymph-Bunkers swell up with Clone-Soldiers, taking over Immune-Defense.
Malignant proliferation of lymphocytes within the lymphatic system.
Blast-the-Marrow-Thief
The Factory-Clog. Thief floods Marrow-Factory with Immature-Rookies. No real Red-Cells can be made.
Clonal expansion of hematopoietic precursors crowds out normal hematopoiesis.
Sepsis-the-Systemic-Storm
The Arena-Crash. Infection-Fire spreads to Blood-River. Pressure-Pipes leak and Organs stall.
Dysregulated host response to infection leading to life-threatening organ dysfunction.
Methi-the-Resistant-Rat (MRSA)
The Shield-Breaker. Ignores Standard-Penicillin-Punches. Requires the Vancomycin-Hammer to kick from ring.
MRSA carries the mecA gene, altering its penicillin-binding proteins.
C-Diff-the-Gut-Vandal
The Toxic-Tsunami. Good-Bacteria die, Vandal takes over the gut and causes The-Watery-Riot.
Clostridioides difficile overgrowth and toxin production leading to pseudomembranous colitis.
Viral-the-Hepatitis-Hacker (Hep B/C)
The Slow-Liver-Burn. Hides in Liver-Cells for years, turning Working-Cells into Scar-Stone.
Chronic viral replication leading to immune-mediated hepatocyte destruction and cirrhosis.
Lupus-the-Wolf-Mask (SLE)
The Self-Sabotage. Wolf puts on a mask and tricks the Immune-Army into attacking Everything: skin, joints, kidneys.
Type III hypersensitivity reaction involving immune complex deposition in multiple organs.
Arthritis-the-Rust-Gator (RA)
The Morning-Stiff. Clamps down on Joint-Hinges, making them Hot-and-Rusty until they Deform-and-Lock.
Chronic inflammatory synovitis leading to joint destruction and pannus formation.
Gout-the-Glass-Goat
The Needle-Stomp. Stomps on Big-Toe-Arena, leaving Glass-Needles (Urate) that cause Agony-Sparks.
Monosodium urate crystal deposition in joints triggering an acute inflammatory response.
Vascul-the-Vessel-Viper
The Pipe-Poison. Viper bites Blood-Vessel-Walls, causing them to Inflame-and-Burst or Narrow-and-Starve organs.
Inflammation of blood vessel walls leading to ischemia, aneurysm, or hemorrhage.
Stroke-the-Sudden-Stall
The Brain-Power-Cut. Clot-Monster blocks Brain-Highway, causing one half of the Wrestler to Go-Dark.
Ischemic interruption of cerebral blood flow leading to neuronal death.
Seizure-the-Electric-Storm
The Signal-Chaos. A Static-Shock explodes in the Brain-Bunker, causing Wrestler to Twitch-and-Shake.
Synchronous, high-frequency neuronal firing in the cerebral cortex.
Delir-the-Confusion-Cloud
The Mind-Fog. Toxic-Vapor fills brain, making Wrestler Talk-to-Ghosts and Forget-the-Arena.
Acute, fluctuating disturbance in attention and awareness, often secondary to systemic illness.
Neuro-the-Wither-Worm (Neuropathy)
The Wire-Fray. Worm chews on Nerve-Insulation (Myelin), causing Numbness-Silence or Burning-Static-Pain.
Peripheral nerve damage, often due to high Sugar-Tokens or Alcohol-Toxins.
Statin-the-Plaque-Scrubber
The Highway-Clean. Scrobs Cholesterol-Sludge off Artery-Walls and stabilizes Plaque-Boulders.
HMG-CoA reductase inhibition reduces cholesterol synthesis and stabilizes plaques.
Beta-the-Pulse-Brake (Beta-Blockers)
The Engine-Quiet. Tells Heart-Engine to Slow-Down and Squeeze-Gentle, prteecting from Adrenaline-Spikes.
Antagonism of beta-adrenergic receptors reduces heart rate, contractility, and BP.
Steroid-the-Immune-Mute (Prednisone)
The Riot-Control. Screams QUIET at Immune-Army, stopping Inflammatory-Brawl but leaving Gates-Open.
Glucocorticoids suppress multiple inflammatory pathways by modulating gene transcription.
Warf-the-Old-Guard (Warfarin/DOACs)
The Blood-Slick. Makes Blood-River slippery. Clot-Monsters cannot form, but Scuffs won't stop Leaking.
Inhibition of Vitamin K epoxide reductase or direct inibition of Factor Xa/Thrombin.
Frail-the-Glass-Wrestler (Frailty)
The Brittle-Stat. Low Reserve-Tokens. A Small-Scuff causes Total-System-Collapse.
Multi-system decline in physiological reserve, making the individual vulnerable to minor stressors.
Poly-the-Pill-Pile (Polypharmacy)
The Interaction-Explosion. 10 Chemical-Allies in ring start Fighting-Each-Other, causing Daze-and-Falls.
Adverse drug-drug and drug-disease interactions in patients taking multiple medications.
Fall-the-Gravity-Ghost
The Ground-Slam. Ghost trips Silver-Wrestler, leading to Hip-Pillar-Break and Bed-Stasis-Trap.
Multi-factorial risk (vision, balance, meds, environment) leading to accidental falls.
Demen-the-Memory-Thief
The Lore-Eraser. Slowly deletes Wrestler's-Manual until they forget How-to-Eat and Who-is-Coach.
Progressive neurodegeneration leading to cognitive and functional decline.
VINDICATE-the-Master-Tool
The Arena-Scan. Forces Detective to look at every Antagonist-Clan before final Verdict.
A mnemonic for constructing a comprehensive differential diagnosis.
Red-Flag-the-Alarm-Hawk
The Danger-Scream. Ignores Minor-Scuffs. Screams only at Lethal-Reggies hiding in the ring.
Identifying symptoms that suggest a life-threatening underlying condition.
Occam-the-Slicer (Parsimony)
The Unified-Field. Slicer cuts through 10 symptoms to show they are all caused by one Lupus-Wolf.
The principle that the simplest explanation is most likely to be correct.
Hickam-the-Dictator (Complexity)
The Multi-Match-Reality. Dictator reminds Detective that Multi-Morb-Max has 3 monsters at once!
Counter-principle to Occam; relevant in elderly and complex multimorbid patients.
Chronic-the-Eternal-Match
The Marathon-Drain. Antagonist doesn't try to win in one round; just Wears-Down Wrestler-Frame over years.
Managing long-term conditions where goal is stability/function, not The-Final-Cure.
Palli-the-Comfort-Swan (Palliative Care)
The Goal-Shift. Stops Aggressive-Brawl. Focuses 100% on Comfort-and-Dignity for Final-Round.
Improving quality of life for patients with life-limiting illness.
Rehab-the-Rebuilder
The Training-Camp. After Aoute-Brawl, helps Wrestler regain Strength-Stats to Return-to-Home-Arena.
Huitl-disciplinary recovery focusing on physical, occupational, and speech therapy.
Screen-the-Early-Scouter (Prevention)
The Pre-Emptive-Strike. Finds Cancer-Miner while a Tiny-Seed, before it enters the ring.
Secondary prevention: identifying asymptomatic disease to improve outcomes.
Doc FrizzleBob (The Internal Medicine Attending)
The Diagnostic Orchestrator. Look at the whole arena! Connect the dots and stay fluffy!
If the kidney is failing, check the heart. The Grandmaster sees the hidden links.
Synthesis Quest 1: The Drowning Ox
Identify the Fluid-Antagonist (CHF) and Air-Trapper (COPD). Deploy Diuretic-Knight safely!
Lung-Balloons are full of Gunk AND Water. Don't trigger the Spasm-Spider!
Synthesis Quest 2: The Sugar-Storm
Identify Infection-Trigger (Pneumonia) and Acid-Burn (DKA). Deploy Insulin & Fluid-Refiller!
Sweet-the-Sugar-Bear arrives with Moni-the-Muck-Monster. System is melting.
Synthesis Quest 3: The Silver-Stumble
Use Pill-Auditor to find Interaction-Explosion. Create Safe-Landing-Zone for Silver-Wrestler.
Glass-Wrestler arrives post-Gravity-Ghost fall. 15 Pill-Piles + Memory-Thief. Survive the round!
Sodium-the-Volume-Lord (Na+)
The Water-Warp. Pulls Water-Tokens whenever he goes. The high Sodium is a Mimic: whatever it does with fluid, Osmolality has already noted it.
The Osmotic-Anchor. Fixing Hypo-Nats too fast = Osmotic-Demyelination Syndrome (aka Kayfaboggle).
Potassium-the-Spark-Plug (K+)
The Voltage-Trigger. Controls the Resting-Heart of heart wires. Off Balance? The Heart gets confused.
Hyper-K-the-Killer creates Peaked-T-Wave-Mountains. Hypo-K-Nail opens the Valley. Beware of Error.
Calcium-the-Concrete (Ca2+)
The Membrane-Stabilizer. Keeps Nerve-Gates steady. Hypo-Cal = Gates Slamming, Hyper-Cal = Gates shut.
Regulated by Parathyroid-Hormone. If Mag-the-Magnet is low, Calcium won't rise.
Mag-the-Magnet (Mg2+)
The Gatekeeper's-Helper. The Universal-Relaxer holding the Potassium/Calcium gates shut.
Low Mag triggers Torsade-de-Told. The Ignored-Electrolyte causing Mystery-Glitches.
Hemoglobin-the-Carrier (Hb)
The Oxygen-Tank. Determines available Breath-Fuel. Dark color = low Hemoglobin = fainting from Cargo-Penalty.
The Cargo-Ship. Without Iron-Bolts, the ship can't carry oxygen-crates.
Platelet-the-Plug (Plt)
The Hole-Sealer. First-Responders to a Leak-Crisis. Low count (Thrombo-the-Thin) = bleeding from scratches.
Too high = Clot-the-Blocker. Beware-HIT-the-Hunter is in the ICU!

Buys time and keeps the baby alive until the Surgical-Team arrives.
Indo-the-Lock
The Gate-Closer. Forces the Duct to snap shut, halting the Lung-Flood.
Also heavily used to prevent IVH in extremely premature babies.
PPHN-the-Pressure
The Valve-Reversal. Lung-pipes clamp shut, forcing blood to completely skip the lungs.
Devastating high resistance. Requires Nitric-the-Gas to relax the iron grip.
Nitric-the-Gas
The Pipe-Opener. Selectively relaxes the pipes only in the lungs, not the systemic host.
Targeted cGMP-activation. The ultimate weapon against PPHN.
Hydrocort-the-Stress-Shield
The Vessel-Sensitizer. Primes the heart and pipes to finally hear adrenaline signals.
Deployed when the baby's own Adrenal Factory is too immature to mount a stress response.
Dopamine-the-Driver
The Pump-Beast. Mechanically drives blood pressure up when the Micro-heart fails.
The first-line pressor deployed in many NICUs to fight Hypotension-the-Hollow.
CDH-the-Hole
The Space-Occupier. The gut invades the chest, brutally squashing the Lung-Balloons.
Usually left-sided (Bochdalek). Lung hypoplasia is the true killer, not the hernia itself.
TEF-the-Miswire
The Pipe-Mixer. The Food-Pipe and Wind-Pipe are dangerously soldered together.
Associated with VACTERL. Food dumps to lungs, air dumps to stomach.
Choanal-the-Closed-Nose
The Nose-Block. Newborns are obligate nose breathers. Blocked nose = choking until crying.
Crying forces open the Mouth-Gate, bypassing the blocked nose temporarily.
Hirschsprung-the-Static
The Nerve-Gap. A segment of colon is missing Neural-Drivers, remaining completely Static.
Aganglionic segment causes everything upstream to balloon into a Mega-Colon.
Colostrum-the-Gold
The Immune-Primer. Paints the Gut-Gate with antibodies.
The First-Vaccine. The ultimate defense against Necro-the-Entero.
HMF-the-Fortifier
The Growth-Boost. Mimics the Placental-Feed with hyper-dense protein and calcium.
Preemies miss the 3rd-trimester Nutrient-Dump and require massive extra caloric supply.
TPN-the-Vein-Feed
The Bypass-Fuel. When the gut is offline, the blood directly carries the food.
Pure chemical fuel essential for building the brain and bones of ELBW knights.
Osteo-the-Soft-Bone
The Skeleton-Sag. Without womb-level calcium, the bones turn to soft rubber.
Osteopenia of Prematurity. Requires aggressive high-dose mineral supplementation.
HIE-Cool-the-Cap
The Chemical-Freeze. Slows metabolic time to halt Excitotoxicity in the brain.
Must initiate within 6 hours of birth to save the Knight's brain.
ROP-the-Laser
The Vessel-Burner. Destroys Wild Vessels before they can peel the retina off.
A brutal trade: sacrifices peripheral vision to guarantee central vision.
IVH-the-Drain
The Pressure-Release. Manually vents blood-stained fluid from the brain to the belly.
The mechanical fix when Hydrocephalus forces the skull to expand too fast.
NAS-the-Console
The Sensory-Shield. Dark rooms and swaddling defeat the chaotic Withdrawal-Riot.
The first-line behavioral defense to reduce Morphine reliance in drug-exposed babies.
The Apgar-Scribe
The Transition-Judge. Scores whether the Knight is winning the brutal fight to breathe air.
Heart rate is the single most heavily weighted Stat in the score.
The Pre/Post-Ductal-Sat
The Shunt-Detector. A numerical gap proves blood is skipping the lungs via the Duct.
The universal Gold-Standard screen for critical congenital heart defects.
The Red-Reflex Sentry
The Vision-Guard. If the reflex bounces back white, Retino-the-White-Reflex is hiding inside.
The simplest, fastest check that universally saves eyes and lives.
The Newborn-Screen-Scroll
The Hidden-Glitches-Finder. Sweeps the blood for metabolic errors before symptoms hit.
Executed precisely at 24-48 hours of life to prevent permanent brain damage.
Poly-the-Thick-Blood
The Sludge-Flow. Blood becomes so dense it physically jams the Micro-Pipes, triggering seizures or NEC.
A classic trap for Small-for-Gestational-Age (SGA) Knights.
Hydrops-the-Total-Flood
The Fluid-Overload. The body entirely loses fluid regulation, drowning in its own water.
Immune (Rh) or Non-immune (Heart/Parvo) triggers. Extremely high mortality.
Anemia-of-Prematurity
The Oxygen-Carrier Shortage. The Marrow-Factory goes on strike, halting red cell production.
Immature kidneys simply refuse to synthesize enough EPO until the baby ages.
Osteo-the-Rickets
The Fragile-Frame. Depleted calcium/phosphorus causes bones to literally snap during routine Nappy-Changes.
The devastating result of missing the massive 3rd-trimester placental calcium dump.
Nephro the Nephron
Segmental Vulnerability — Cortex houses glomeruli/PCT/DCT; Medulla houses loops/collecting ducts
Every segment has its own specific transport machinery and its own unique clinical vulnerabilities.
GFR Gary
Filtration Math — Net Filtration Pressure is 1–10 mmHg
Creatinine rises late. It will not elevate until ~50% of GFR is permanently lost.
Filtration Barry
Charge & Size Repulsion — Defends against albumin leak
Loss of heparan sulfate from the GBM causes selective albumin leak before structural size-barrier failure.
Auto the Autoregulation
Pressure Defense — Tubuloglomerular feedback manages NaCl delivery.
ACE inhibitors dilate the efferent arteriole; NSAIDs constrict the afferent. Together, they drop GFR.
Tubulo the PCT
Fanconi Drop — Generalized PCT dysfunction
Fanconi causes glucosuria with normal blood glucose, alongside aminoaciduria and phosphaturia.
Henley the Loop
Medullary Concentrating Engine
Loop diuretics block NKCC2, completely abolishing the medullary gradient and causing massive diuresis.
Disco the DCT
Thiazide Shift — Blocks NCC
Thiazides block NCC, causing volume depletion which triggers hypercalcaemia and hypocalciuria.
Collect the Collecting Duct
Hormonal Final Say
Liddle syndrome features an ENaC gain-of-function mutation that phenocopies aldosterone excess, but only responds to amiloride.
"Nephrotic Ned"
Oncotic Collapse — Loss of plasma oncotic pressure.
Loss of urinary anticoagulants makes this a hypercoagulable state. Membranous nephropathy carries the highest renal vein thrombotic risk.
"Nephritic Neil"
Inflammatory Blockade — Reduced GFR, oliguria, hypertension.
Red cell casts are formed in the tubules and are strictly pathognomonic of glomerular bleeding.
"IgA Ivan"
Mesangial Deposition Strike
Haematuria occurs concurrently (synpharyngitic, 1-2 days) with the URTI, distinguishing it from post-streptococcal GN.
"Membranous Mary"
Spike & Dome Subepithelial Thickening
Secondary causes account for 20%. You must screen for occult solid tumour malignancy in all adults over 50.
"Minimal Chang"
T-Cell Permeability Factor
Dramatic, selective albuminuria with essentially normal light microscopy. Highly responsive to steroids.
"FSGS Frankie"
Podocyte Collapse — Loss is irreversible
Recurrence after renal transplantation in primary FSGS strongly indicates a circulating permeability factor (like suPAR).
"Lupus Nephritis Lucie"
Immune Complex Mine — 'Wire loop' subendothelial deposits
The 'Full House' immunofluorescence pattern is virtually diagnostic of lupus nephritis.
"ANCA Vasculitis Vince"
Endothelial Arson — Crescent formation without immune deposits
Presents as a pulmonary-renal syndrome; rapidly progressive GN combined with alveolar haemorrhage.
"Post-Strep Percy"
Alternative Pathway Consumption
C3 is low but C4 is normal, revealing isolated alternative complement pathway activation.
"Alport the Hereditary"
Basement Membrane Lamellation
Type IV collagen mutations cause progressive GBM splitting, leading to nephritis and sensorineural deafness.
"Acid-Base Alice"
Respiratory & Renal Compensation
Winter's Formula: Expected pCO₂ = 1.5 × HCO₃ + 8 ± 2. Use it to check if respiratory compensation is appropriate.
"Anion Gap Andy"
MUDPILES Protocol — Methanol, Uraemia, DKA, Propylene Glycol, Isoniazid, Lactic Acid, Ethylene Glycol, Salicylates
Metformin causes Type B lactic acidosis (without tissue hypoxia), driving a pure high anion gap metabolic acidosis.
Normal AG Norma
Bicarbonate Wasting / H+ Retention
Type 1 distal RTA fails to secrete H+, meaning the urine can never be acidified below pH 5.5 despite systemic acidosis.
Metabolic Alkalosis Maggie
The Maintenance Lock
The kidney can excrete any HCO3 load, unless locked into maintenance by hypovolaemia or hypokalaemia.
Potassium Perry
Cardiac Membrane Destabilization
In hyperkalaemic arrest, give Calcium Gluconate first. It does not lower K+; it stabilizes the myocardium to prevent VF.
Sodium Stella
Tonicity Shift
Correct hyponatraemia slowly (<10 mmol/L per 24h). Rapid correction floods the adapted brain, causing cerebral oedema.
Magnesium Magda
The Refractory Block
Hypomagnesaemia impairs ROMK function. Hypokalaemia will be completely refractory to K+ replacement until Mg is fixed.
Phosphate Phil
Cellular Energy Depletion
Refeeding syndrome drives phosphate intracellularly, causing severe ATP depletion, haemolysis, and respiratory failure.
RTA Rita
The Acid Trap Matrix
Type 4 RTA (hyporeninaemic aldosteronism) is the only RTA characterized by high serum potassium.
Uric Acid Ulric
Inflammasome Trigger — MSU crystals activate macrophages
Never initiate allopurinol (urate-lowering therapy) during an acute gout attack; it mobilises stores and worsens the flare.
AKI the Acute
The Staging Triad — Creatinine rise, or urine output drop
Pre-renal AKI presents with urine Na < 20 and a concentrated urine osmolality > 500 mOsm/kg.
ATN the Tubule Destroyer
Intraluminal Obstruction
Rhabdomyolysis causes haem-pigment ATN; it requires aggressive IV isotonic saline to prevent tubular obstruction.
AIN the Interstitial
T-Cell Infiltration & Tubulitis
PPI-associated AIN often lacks the classic fever/rash and presents insidiously as unexplained CKD.
Hepatorenal Hugo
Maximal Renal Vasoconstriction
Kidneys from HRS patients function perfectly if transplanted. The failure is entirely haemodynamic, driven by cirrhosis.
CKD the Chronic
Systemic Dominoes
Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in CKD. Most patients die of heart disease before reaching dialysis.
Dialysis Danny
Diffusion & Ultrafiltration
Arteriovenous fistulas (AVF) are preferred over central lines because they carry the lowest risk of infection and thrombosis.
Peritoneal Pearl
Osmotic Pull — Glucose drives ultrafiltration
Peritoneal dialysis preserves residual renal function much better than intermittent haemodialysis.
Transplant Tina
Triple Therapy Defense
Calcineurin inhibitor nephropathy (fibrosis/atrophy) remains the leading cause of late graft loss, ironically worsened by CNI nephrotoxicity.
ADPKD Ada
Cystic Renin Drive — Early severe hypertension
You must screen for intracranial aneurysms if there is a family history. It's the leading cause of early death before ESRD.
Renovascular Rex
Ischaemic Panic — Maximal RAAS activation
ACE inhibitors cause acute kidney injury in bilateral RAS by removing the efferent constriction keeping the GFR alive.
Nephrolithiasis Nick
Supersaturation Crystallization
Never restrict dietary calcium for calcium stones; doing so increases free gut oxalate absorption, worsening the stones.
Proteinuria Petra
The Dipstick Limit
Standard urine dipsticks only detect albumin. They will read negative for the overflow tubular Bence Jones proteins in myeloma.
ACEi Amy
Intraglomerular Decompression
Dual RAAS blockade (ACEi + ARB) provides no additional renal benefit but massively increases the risk of AKI and hyperkalaemia.
Diuretics Dmitri
Sequential Nephron Blockade
Severe nephrotic patients need IV loop diuretics because massive gut wall oedema prevents oral drug absorption.
Erythropoietin Ernie
Hypoxia Sensor & Red Cell Proliferation
Pushing Hb targets higher than 120 g/L in CKD increases the risk of stroke without providing any mortality benefit.
Phosphate Binder Percy
Intestinal Chelation
Binders must be taken exactly with meals. Calcium-based binders risk worsening vascular calcification in severe CKD.
Calcimimetics Carla
Allosteric Modulation
Preferred for secondary hyperparathyroidism in dialysis because it lowers PTH without raising calcium, unlike active vitamin D.
Contrast Nephropathy Connie
Medullary Ischaemia + Direct Toxicity
Metformin is not nephrotoxic itself, but must be held 48 hours prior to contrast to prevent fatal lactic acidosis if AKI occurs.
TMA Tamara
Microvascular Shearing & Platelet Consumption
Antibiotics are absolutely contraindicated in STEC-HUS; killing the bacteria triggers a massive release of Shiga toxin.
Myeloma Kidney Mick
Tubular Overload & Obstruction
Myeloma cast nephropathy causes severe AKI, which must be distinguished from AL amyloidosis which causes nephrotic syndrome.
Sickle Cell Renal Sydney
Papillary Sloughing & Necrosis
The extreme 1200 mOsm/kg hypoxic environment of the renal medulla causes RBC sickling and damage even in sickle cell trait.
Lupus Anticoagulant Lena
In-Vitro Paradox / In-Vivo Thrombosis
'Lupus Anticoagulant' is a misnomer: It prolongs the APTT in laboratory tests but causes catastrophic micro-thrombosis clinically.
Kidney Biopsy Betty
Tri-Partite Processing
Every core must be processed for Light Microscopy, Immunofluorescence, and Electron Microscopy simultaneously to diagnose glomerular disease.
Urinalysis Ursula
Non-Invasive Diagnostics
Broad waxy casts indicate advanced CKD; the tubules have dilated to compensate for mass nephron dropout, creating wide, slow-flowing casts.
Electrolyte Emergencies Eddie
Cardiac Hierarchy Protocol
Correct hyponatraemia slowly (max 8-10 mmol/L/24h). Fast correction destroys the brain via osmotic demyelination syndrome.
RAAS Pharmacology Renata
Pleiotropic Protection
Finerenone is a non-steroidal MRA preferred in diabetic CKD; it reduces fibrosis independently of its haemodynamic effects.
The Nephrology Attending
Mechanistic Justification
Map every clinical diagnosis to its cellular mechanism. Justify every treatment decision with an underlying physiological principle. No approximations.
FrizzleBob's Golden Rule
Narrative Memory
You remember the stories, not the lists. If you understand the machine, the pathology becomes inevitable. Stay fluffy!
Homy the Homunculus
MCA Stroke — Target's contralateral face and arm are paralyzed.
The leg representation descends into the interhemispheric fissure. Bilateral ACA territory ischemia mimics spinal cord disease.
Broca & Wernicke
Conduction Aphasia — Target speaks fluently but cannot repeat a single word. Broca builds speech (expressive). Wernicke understands it (receptive).
The arcuate fasciculus connects both speech hubs. Damage between them causes Conduction Aphasia — fluent speech, intact comprehension, broken repetition.
Fronty the Frontal Lobe
Frontal Release — Re-equips primitive grasp and rooting reflexes.
Irritative lesion (seizures) makes eyes look AWAY. Destructive lesion (stroke) makes eyes look TOWARD the lesion.
Parry the Parietal Lobe
Hemispatial Neglect — The left half of the opponent's world ceases to exist.
Dominant side handles math and fingers (Gerstmann). Non-dominant side integrates the spatial map.
Tempo the Temporal Lobe
Uncal Herniation — Crush CN III to dilate the pupil, then cause false-localizing hemiplegia.
Hippocampus encodes memory. The Uncus herniates through the tentorium to cause the blown pupil.
Occi the Occipital Lobe
Macular Sparing — MCA/PCA dual blood supply protects central vision during PCA stroke.
Meyer's loop damage is pie in the sky (superior defect). Parietal optic radiation damage is pie on the floor (inferior).
Insula Izzy
Autonomic Arrhythmia — Manipulate internal body state and cardiac rhythm.
Buried deep in the Sylvian fissure. Right insular stroke triggers sympathetic storms and arrhythmias.
Limby the Limbic System
Anterograde Amnesia — Opponent cannot form new declarative memories.
Mammillary body atrophy (Wernicke-Korsakoff) permanently breaks the Papez episodic memory circuit.
Basso the Basal Ganglia
Direct vs Indirect — Dopamine strengthens the direct (go) and weakens the indirect (stop).
Parkinson's loses dopamine (stuck in stop). Huntington's loses the indirect pathway early (stuck in go).
Thalamo the Thalamus
Dejerine-Roussy — Inflict burning, dysaesthetic pain weeks after a VPL infarct.
Every sensory modality except smell must synapse here before reaching the cortex.
Dorsal the Dorsal Column
Romberg Fall — Opponent falls over the moment they close their eyes.
Fine touch and proprioception ascend ipsilaterally and do not cross until the medial lemniscus in the medulla.
Spino the Spinothalamic Tract
Cape Distribution — Syringomyelia expands the central canal, cutting the crossing fibers.
Pain and temperature cross the midline almost immediately in the anterior commissure of the spinal cord.
Cortico the Corticospinal Tract
UMN Spasticity — Inflict hyperreflexia, spasticity, and a positive Babinski sign. No wasting.
The internal capsule is the bottleneck. A tiny lacunar infarct here causes massive, dense contralateral hemiplegia.
Cere the Cerebellar Pathways
Intention Tremor — Opponent's movements worsen as they approach the target.
Output crosses to the contralateral thalamus, then the corticospinal tract crosses back. Net result: ipsilateral control.
Russel the Rubrospinal
Decerebrate vs Decorticate — Dictate the opponent's coma posture based on lesion height.
Cortical loss = decorticate (arms flexed). Lesion below red nucleus = decerebrate (all limbs extended).
Spino the Spinal Cord Cross-Section
ASA Syndrome — Paraplegia and pain loss below lesion, but proprioception survives.
The anterior spinal artery feeds motor and pain tracts. The posterior spinal arteries feed the dorsal columns.
Brown the Brown-Séquard
The Cleanest Cut — Ipsilateral motor/proprioception loss, contralateral pain loss.
The ultimate test of crossing rules. Pain crosses early, motor and touch cross late.
Conus the Conus & Cauda
Sphincter Sabotage — Saddle anesthesia and loss of anal tone demands urgent surgery.
Conus = UMN signs mixed with LMN bladder. Cauda Equina = Pure LMN flaccid weakness and areflexia.
Middy the Midbrain
Weber's Strike — Ipsilateral CN III palsy + contralateral hemiplegia.
Houses the cerebral peduncles and oculomotor nerves. Parinaud's syndrome (pineal tumor) blocks upgaze.
Ponty the Pons
Locked-In Syndrome — Bilateral ventral destruction leaves only vertical gaze and blinking.
The center for horizontal gaze. An MLF lesion causes Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia (INO).
Meddy the Medulla
Wallenberg's Curse (Lateral Medulla) — Ipsilateral face pain, Horner's, hoarseness, and ataxia.
Controls breathing (pre-Bötzinger). Lesions here are life-threatening.
Cranio I–IV
Pupillary Light Reflex — CN II senses the light, bilateral Edinger-Westphal nuclei send CN III to constrict.
A painful third nerve palsy with a blown pupil is a posterior communicating artery aneurysm emergency.
Cranio V–VII
Bell's vs Stroke — LMN VII palsy drops the whole face. UMN spares the forehead.
CN VII has the longest intracranial course. An isolated CN VI palsy is a false localizing sign for raised ICP.
Cranio VIII–XII
Jugular Foramen Mass — Compress IX, X, and XI to destroy swallowing and shoulder shrug.
Uvula deviates AWAY from a CN X lesion. Tongue deviates TOWARD a CN XII LMN lesion.
The Cerebellum
Archicerebellum Spin — Flocculonodular lobe lesions destroy balance and trigger nystagmus.
Vermis controls the trunk (paleocerebellum). Lateral hemispheres control distal limbs (neocerebellum).
Vertigo Vera
Test of Skew — Differentiate a benign inner ear from a posterior circulation stroke.
Pure vertical nystagmus is ALWAYS central. Direction-changing horizontal nystagmus is central.
Brachy the Brachial Plexus
Waiter's Tip (Erb's Palsy) — C5/C6 upper trunk avulsion during shoulder dystocia.
Lower trunk (C8/T1) injury causes Klumpke's claw hand PLUS Horner syndrome from T1 sympathetic drag.
Radi the Radial Nerve
Spiral Groove Crush — Target loses wrist and finger extension, but preserves elbow extension.
The triceps motor branch is given off BEFORE the nerve wraps around the humeral shaft.
Ulna the Ulnar Nerve
Ulnar Paradox — A wrist lesion creates a WORSE claw than an elbow lesion.
A high lesion paralyzes FDP, meaning the fingers can't flex to form the full claw.
Medi the Median Nerve
Carpal Tunnel Crush — Nocturnal paraesthesia in the lateral 3.5 digits.
Thenar wasting means the nerve is dying. Benediction hand only happens with a high (elbow) lesion.
Femmo the Femoral Nerve
Psoas Hematoma — Compress the nerve within the psoas to kill hip flexion and knee extension.
Absent knee jerk + positive femoral stretch test + anterior thigh numbness.
Sciati the Sciatic/Peroneal
Foot Drop — Common peroneal palsy loses dorsiflexion and eversion.
How to tell peroneal palsy from L5 root lesion? L5 also loses inversion (tibialis posterior).
Derma the Dermatomes
Sensory Level — Pinpoint the exact spinal segment of a cord transection.
The thumb is C6. The middle finger is C7. The pinky is C8. Always.
Reflex Rex
Jendrassik Manoeuvre — Pull clasped hands apart to amplify gamma motor neuron activity.
Hyperreflexia + Clonus + Babinski = UMN lesion. Areflexia + Wasting = LMN lesion.
Autonomo the ANS
Adrenal Bypass — The adrenal medulla acts as a modified sympathetic ganglion, releasing directly to blood.
Sympathetic preganglionics are short. Parasympathetic preganglionics are long.
Horner the Horner
Hydroxyamphetamine Test — Dilates central and preganglionic lesions, fails in postganglionic.
Ptosis, Miosis, Anhidrosis. An acute Horner with neck pain is a carotid dissection until proven otherwise.
Derma Root Pain
Spurling's Shock — Axial compression of rotated neck reproduces cervical radicular pain.
Posterolateral disc herniations in the lumbar spine compress the exiting nerve root ONE LEVEL BELOW the disc.
Peripheral Percy
Dying Back (Length-Dependent) — The longest axons fail first, causing stocking-glove sensory loss.
Guillain-Barré Syndrome shows high CSF protein with normal cell counts (dissociation) and absent reflexes.
Ventri the Ventricular System
Hakim's Triad — Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus causes wobbly, wacky, and wet (gait, dementia, incontinence).
Aqueductal stenosis is obstructive. Post SAH failure of arachnoid granulations is communicating.
Meningo the Meninges
Lucid Interval — Epidural hematoma patients wake up, talk, and then suddenly herniate.
Epidural = Arterial (Middle Meningeal), Biconvex. Subdural = Venous (Bridging Veins), Crescent.
Hernia the Herniation
False Localization — Contralateral peduncle pushed against tentorial notch causes IPSILATERAL hemiplegia.
A fixed dilated pupil is the earliest reliable clinical sign of uncal herniation (parasympathetic fibers on outside of CN III).
Blood Brain Barry
Vasogenic Edema — Bacterial meningitis breaks the tight junctions; water pours in.
Tumor vasculature lacks a blood-brain barrier, which is why gadolinium contrast lights up tumors on MRI.
Cerebral Vera Vasculature
Subclavian Steal — Arm exercise reverses vertebral artery flow, causing posterior circulation ischemia.
Sudden unilateral deafness + facial numbness + contralateral body numbness = AICA stroke.
Aneurysm Annie
Thunderclap Headache — Saccular aneurysm rupture into subarachnoid space.
A painful CN III palsy is a Posterior Communicating Artery (PCoA) aneurysm until proven otherwise.
Dural Sinus Derek
The Great Mimic — Cerebral Venous Thrombosis causes raised ICP, seizures, and focal deficits.
Treat with anticoagulation (LMWH) even if the venous infarct has already caused hemorrhagic transformation.
Spino Cord Syndromes Summary
Central Cord Syndrome — Hyperextension in elderly patients destroys the central cervical cord.
Arm motor fibers lie centrally, leg fibers lie peripherally. Therefore, arms are much weaker than legs.
Spine Anatomy Sandy
Neurogenic Claudication — Spinal stenosis causes bilateral leg pain when walking, relieved by bending forward.
In the cervical spine, the root exits ABOVE its numbered vertebra. In the lumbar spine, it exits BELOW.
Sleep Anatomy Sam
REM Intrusion — Loss of orexin drops the patient directly from wakefulness to atonic REM sleep (Cataplexy).
The VLPO and ARAS mutually inhibit each other. Orexin from the lateral hypothalamus stabilizes the awake state.
Pain Percy
Gate Control Theory Activate large A-beta touch fibers to inhibit C fiber pain transmission.
Referred pain happens because visceral and somatic afferents converge on the exact same dorsal horn neurons.
Visual Percy
Pie in the Sky — Anterior temporal lobectomy damages Meyer's loop, causing superior quadrantanopia.
The macula occupies 50% of the primary visual cortex, explaining central vision sparing in PCA strokes.
Eye Move Eddie
One-and-a-Half Syndrome — PPRF + MLF lesion on same side. Only contralateral abduction survives.
MLF lesions cause INO (adduction failure). Bilateral INO in a young patient is Multiple Sclerosis until proven otherwise.
Memory Mike
Transient Global Amnesia — Sudden anterograde amnesia caused by venous backflow hitting the hippocampus.
Hippocampus is essential for encoding. Remote memories survive hippocampal destruction due to systems consolidation.
Hypothala the Hypothalamus
Pan-hypopituitarism — Craniopharyngioma crushes the stalk, destroying endocrine and autonomic control.
Lateral hypothalamus = hunger (orexin). Ventromedial = satiety. Suprachiasmatic = master clock.
Pituitary Pete
Apoplexy — Sudden hemorrhage of adenoma causes thunderclap headache and visual loss.
Suprasellar extension hits crossing nasal fibers, causing bitemporal hemianopia (tunnel vision).
The Neuroanatomy Attending
Localize. Name. Explain. — Map the Horner's, the ataxia, and the hoarseness to the exact vessel.
You don't know it until you can trace the wiring backward from the deficit to the lesion without looking it up.
Uncle FrizzleBob's Rule of the Street
Epistemic Sabotage — Destroy the boring format to directly preserve the factual integrity.
You remember stories, not lists, one who knows where a structure lives can predict what happens when it dies.
The Plumber's Cousin
Total Shutdown. Contralateral hemiplegia, homonymous hemianopia, AND higher cortical dysfunction (dysphasia/neglect).
High mortality, severe disability. Proximal MCA or ICA occlusion.
Manny MCA
Dominant Disconnect. Contralateral hemiplegia + hemisensory loss. If dominant: Aphasia. Non-dominant: Neglect.
The most common stroke territory. Follows the motor homunculus.
Annie ACA
Frontal Filter Failure. Contralateral leg weakness + sensory loss. Urinary incontinence + personality change (abulia).
Hits medial frontal/parietal cortex. The filter is gone.
Vic Vertebral
Cross-Wiring. Produces crossed signs: ipsilateral cranial nerve palsy with contralateral long tract signs.
Dizziness, Diplopia, Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Drop attacks. Highly dangerous to misdiagnose in the ED.
Larry Lacune
Pure Precision. Pure motor OR pure sensory stroke. NO cortical signs (no aphasia, neglect, or hemianopia).
Caused by lipohyalinosis of deep perforators. Strongly linked to hypertension and diabetes.
Wally Wallenberg
Crossed Pain. Ipsilateral face pain/temp loss + contralateral body pain/temp loss. Ipsilateral ataxia and Horner's.
PICA occlusion. Touch and proprioception are completely spared!
Benny Basilar
The Lock-In. Quadriplegia, anarthria, but consciousness and vertical gaze are fully intact.
A devastating natural history. One of the few syndromes where thrombectomy is attempted well beyond 6 hours.
Otto Occipital
Alexia Without Agraphia. Contralateral homonymous hemianopia. Can write, but cannot read (if dominant).
Macular vision is spared due to dual blood supply (MCA collaterals at the occipital pole).
Tia the Transient
The Warning Shot. Focal ischemia resolving within 24h (most <60m). High ABCD2 score mandates same-day review.
Requires urgent dual antiplatelet therapy for high-risk patients. Do not ignore.
Sam the SAH
Thunderclap. Worst headache of life, maximum severity at onset. Due to ruptured berry aneurysm.
Ottawa SAH Rule: If CT is negative after 6h, mandatory LP for xanthochromia. Vasospasm risk days 4-14.
The Penumbra Princess
Salvage Operation. The target of all acute stroke therapy. Brain tissue that is ischemic but not yet dead.
IV alteplase eligible within 4.5 hours. Thrombectomy extends to 24h with favorable perfusion imaging.
Hank the Hemorrhage
Absolute Contraindication. Sudden focal deficit + headache, vomiting, reduced consciousness. NO tPA.
Hypertensive small vessel (basal ganglia) vs. Amyloid angiopathy (lobar). Reverse anticoagulation instantly.
The NIHSS Inspector
Predictive Threshold. Score >= 6 suggests large vessel occlusion. Score < 4 is minor stroke.
A dynamic, serial scoring tool. Essential for predicting the need for thrombectomy.
Cissy Circle of Willis
The Redundancy Ring. Connects anterior/posterior circulations via communicating arteries (ACoA, PCoA).
ACcA is the most common site of berry aneurysms. Most humans have an incomplete circle, limiting collateral flow.
Frank the Thrombolysis Window
Time is Brain. Call EMS -> CT Head -> Ischemic & <4.5h = IV alteplase. If LVO = thrombectomy up to 24h.
Do NOT lower BP in acute ischemic stroke unless >220/120 or thrombolysis given.
The Stroke Prevention Squad
The Secondary Shield. Antiplatelet (non-cardioembolic) vs. Anticoagulant DOAC (cardioembolic AF).
High-intensity statin for ALL ischemic strokes regardless of baseline LDL. Carotid endarterectomy for symptomatic stenosis >50%.
Dopa the Dopamine
The Quad-Core Modulator. Nigrostriatal (movement), Mesolimbic (reward), Mesocortical (motivation), Tuberoinfundibular (prolactin).
Block D2 for psychosis, but you will worsen movement and raise prolactin simultaneously.
Perry Parkinson
The Lewy Body Eraser. Resting tremor (4-6 Hz), lead-pipe rigidity, and mandatory bradykinesia.
Loss of substantia nigra pars compacta. Hyposmia and REM sleep behavior disorder predate motor signs by YEARS.
