THE POSITION-MAP.
DETERMINES VERTEX (HEAD-DOWN) vs BREECH (BOTTOM-DOWN).
APGAR-Scribe
THE WELCOME-SCORE.
SCORE ON APPEARANCE/PULSE/GRIMACE/ACTIVITY/RESPIRATION sums up Ringo.
Whiff-Test Detective
THE FISHY-FINDER.
IF IT SMELLS LIKE DEAD FISH, BACTERIAL-VAGINOSIS IS PRESENT.
Fern-Sign
THE FERN-LEAK-CONFIRM.
FERN-CRYSTAL MEANS THE UTERINE-FORTRESS HAS BEEN BREACHED (Water broke).
Doc FrizzleBob
THE LIFE-GUARANTOR.
IS THE BABY HAPPY? Is the mother stable? Deliver the truth!
Quest 1: The Outlaw Tube
CASE: 23yo, 1-sided pain, hCG 3000, empty uterus.
QUEST: Identify the Outlaw and choose the weapon: Metho-the-Melt or Laparo-Laura?
Quest 2: The Late Fade
CASE: Monitor shows heart rate dropping after contraction ends.
QUEST: Identify the rhythm (Late-Larry) and name the failing negotiator (Placenta-Phil).
Quest 3: The Menopausal Bleed
CASE: 60yo, hasn't bled in 10 years, sudden spotting.
QUEST: Name the Onco-Outlaw to rule out (Edna) and the tool needed (D&C-Dan).
Gordon the Gorilla (Self-Sufficiency)
The Infinite Ego. Gordon screams at himself to grow, ignoring the body's "Stop" signals.
Mutations in EGFR or RAS keep the growth signal floored even when the key is out of the ignition. (Autocrine Loop / ERBB2 (HER2))
The P53 Police Bulldog (Tumor Suppressor)
The Broken Badge. Normally stops the cycle or hits "Self-Destruct". When the badge breaks, anything goes.
"The Guardian of the Genome." If P53 is down, the cell ignores the damage and keeps wrestling. (Li-Fraumeni Syndrome/Mutation)
Angiogenesis Annie (The Road Builder)
Illegal Infrastructure. Annie builds new blood vessels to bring snacks (O2/Glucose) to the tumor core.
Tumors can't grow past 2mm without Annie. Bevacizumab is the bulldozer that tears her roads down. (VEGF / Bevacizumab (The Roadblock))
Telomerase Terry (The Eternal Wrestler)
Immortal Ends. Terry puts caps back on his shoelaces (Chromosomes) so they never fray.
Normal cells have a Hayflick Limit. Terry ignores it. He doesn't age; he just grows. (TERT Promoter Mutations)
Metastasis Max (The Wanderer)
Basement Membrane Breach. Max dissolves the ropes and leaves the ring to invade the pit area.
EMT (Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition). Max loses his anchors (Cadherins) and enters the bloodstream highway. (E-Cadherin / Snail & Twist)
Rb the Gatekeeper (The G1/S Referee)
The Open Gate. If phosphorylated, he lets the cell cycle start. If mutated, the gate is always open.
Master regulator of the G1 to S phase transition. (Retinoblastoma)
BCL-2 BOB (The Anti-Death Shield)
Apoptosis Block. He prevents the mitochondria from releasing the "Apoptosis Grenade."
Overexpressed in Follicular Lymphoma. Cells that should die are kept artificially alive. (Overexpressed in t(14;18))
Warburg Wally (The Glycolysis Junkie)
Aerobic Fermentation. Even with plenty of oxygen, Wally insists on fermenting his sugar.
This massive, inefficient glucose appetite makes tumors glow on PET scans. (High FDG Uptake (PET Scan))
PD-L1 Peter (The Invisibility Cloak)
The "Self" Mask. Peter wears a mask that tells T-Cell Bouncers "I belong here."
Checkpoint inhibitors rip this mask off so the immune system can attack. (Immune Checkpoint Target)
RAS the Rogue (The Broken Switch)
Unstoppable Relay. Once flipped to 'ON' by a growth factor, he stays there forever.
A major downstream signaling protein. If it can't turn off, the cell divides endlessly. (Permanent 'ON' State)
MYC the Megaphone (The Amplifier)
Deafening Roar. MYC amplifies every single growth signal into a catastrophic shockwave.
A transcription factor overdrive, famously driving Burkitt Lymphoma. (t(8;19) on card — likely should be t(8;14))
BRCA Brenda (The DNA Repairwoman)
Untied Mayhem. When Brenda is on strike (mutation), double-strand breaks go unfixed.
High risk for breast and ovarian cancer mayhem. (Double Strand Break Repair Failure)
APC the Trash Compactor
Compactor Failure. Usually degrades Beta-Catenin. Without APC, it builds up.
Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP) forces the colon to grow 1000s of polyps. (FAP / Beta-Catenin Buildup)
VHL the Snorkel
Phantom Suffocation. Normally detects oxygen. If mutated, the cell thinks it's suffocating.
The hypoxic panic summons Angiogenesis Annie to build massive vessels. (Renal Cell Ca)
NF-1 the Brakeman
The Snapped Reins. He normally keeps RAS in check.
Without her, nerves grow uncontrollably into tumors. (Neurofibromatosis Type 1) — pronoun inconsistency noted
ALL-in Alice (Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia)
The Schoolyard Takeover. Alice fills the marrow with 'Blasts' until there's no room for normal blood.
Most common childhood cancer. Hides in the 'Sanctuaries' (CNS and Testes). (TdT+ / Child < 15yo / t(12;21) Good / t(9;22) Bad)
AML Archie (Acute Myeloid Leukemia)
The Needle Strike. Archie's Auer Rods trigger DIC.
APL is a bleeding emergency. Treat with ATRA (Vitamin A) to force blasts to grow up. (Auer Rods / MPO+ / t(15;17) APL)
CLL Larry (Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia)
The Fragile Crowd. Larry lives forever but is easily crushed during a blood smear.
Elderly patients. "Wait and Watch." Can transform into aggressive large B-cell lymphoma. (Smudge Cells CD5+)
CML Charlie (Chronic Myeloid Leukemia)
The Tyrosine Rocket. Charlie is powered by a constitutively active fuse.
Treat with Imatinib (The Fuse-Cutter). High basophils, low LAP score. (Philadelphia Chromosome / t(9;22) / BCR-ABL)
Burkitt's Barry (The Starry Night)
Jawbreaker Blast. Extremely fast doubling time driven by MYC.
"Starry Sky" histology is caused by macrophages eating the massive debris field of dying cells. (t(8;14) / c-myc / EBV)
Hodgkin's Harry
The Reactive Mob. He's a lonely malignant B-cell hiding in a massive crowd of reactive inflammation.
The tumor is mostly healthy cells; the Reed-Sternberg cells are rare giants. (Reed-Sternberg "Owl Eyes" / CD15+ / CD30+)
Follicular Fiona
Painless Fluctuation. Her nodes wax and wane over months without symptoms.
Driven entirely by the BCL-2 Anti-Death Shield. Hard to cure, very slow-moving. (t(14;18) / BCL-2 Overloader)
Mantle Cell Manny
Cell Cycle Smash. A very aggressive bouncer that overdrives the G1/S transition.
Poor prognosis, older males. Highly aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma. (t(11;14) / Cyclin D1 driver)
Marginal Zone Mike
The Inflammatory Squatter. Mike only sets up shop where chronic inflammation has been burning for years.
Eradicating the H. pylori infection can sometimes cure the gastric MALToma entirely. (MALToma / Associated with Chronic Inflammation)
Multiple Myeloma Monty (The Bone-Cracker)
Osteolytic Sabotage. Dissolves the skeleton.
"CRAB": Calcium up, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions. Light chains in urine. (M-Spike (IgG/IgA) / CRAB Symptoms)
Waldenstrom Wally
The Giant Antibody. Makes the blood thick like sludge.
Causes visual and bleeding issues. Crucially: No bone lesions! (IgM M-Spike / Hyperviscosity)
Polycythemia Paul
Erythroid Overload. Paul makes far too many red blood cells.
Classic presentation: Pruritus (severe itching) after a hot shower. (JAK2 Mutation)
Essential Toby (Thrombocythemia)
The Clot-Bleed Paradox. Toby makes so many defective platelets you bleed and clot at the same time.
A disorder of megakaryocytes. Diagnosis of exclusion. (JAK2 / Massive Platelet Counts)
Myelofibrosis Max
Fibrotic Eviction. Max replaces the marrow factory with useless scar tissue.
'Teardrop' RBCs happen because they have to squeeze out of the fibrotic marrow. (Teardrop RBCs / Bone Marrow turns to stone)
Hairy Cell Harry
The Velvet Web. Harry gets tangled in the marrow and spleen.
Causes a 'dry tap' on marrow aspiration. Highly responsive to Cladribine. (TRAP Positive / Splenomegaly)
Small-Cell Sam (The Neuroendocrine Ninja)
Hormonal Sabotage. Sam spells that make too much water (SIADH) or look like a moon-face (Cushing).
Very aggressive, too small for surgery, but Sam hates Chemo/Radiation. (Central Lung / ACTH / ADH / Lambert-Eaton)
Renal Cell Rex (The Polycythemia King)
The EPO Overdose. Rex makes too much Erythropoietin, turning blood into sludge.
Loves the renal vein. If he reaches the IVC, he climbs to the heart like a malignant ladder. (VHL Mutation / Clear Cell / t(3;?))
Pancreatic Pete (The Silent Assassin)
Trousseau's Sign. Pete makes blood clot in random places (Migratory Thrombophlebitis).
Usually found too late. If Pete is in the head of the pancreas, look for the 'Double Duct' sign. (CA 19-9 / Courvoisier's Law (Painless Jaundice))
Squamous Sid
Calcium Crush. Sid secretes fake Parathyroid Hormone, leaching calcium.
Causes severe Hypercalcemia (Stones, Moans, Groans). (PTH-P producer / Central lung cancer)
Adeno Addie
Glandular Architecture. Addie builds mucin-producing factories in the periphery.
The most common lung cancer in non-smokers. (Peripheral lung cancer / Non-smokers)
Colon Cal (The Apple-Core)
The Stricture Choke. Left-sided lesions obstruct and cause 'pencil stools'.
Right-sided lesions bleed silently, causing iron-deficiency anemia. (Left-sided (Obstruction) vs. Right-sided (Bleeding))
Hepatocellular Herb
The Scar-Dweller. Herb sets up shop in livers destroyed by chronic Hep B/C or alcohol.
Skyrockets AFP. A fatal monster ambush; Spreads haematogenously. Loves hepatic vein. (Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP) / Hepatitis B/C)
Glioblastoma Gus (The Butterfly Glioma)
Corpus Crossing. Gus ignores the brain's midline barrier, spreading wings of necrosis.
Histology shows cells lining up (palisading) around dead tissue. (Crosses Corpus Callosum / Pseudopalisading necrosis)
Teratoma Terry (The 'Monster' Tumor)
The Flesh Lottery. Terry spontaneously grows any tissue in the body.
If it's immature: it's malignant; if mature: generally benign (except in males). (3 Germ Layers)
Seminoma Sam
The Clear Clone. Sam builds uniform sheets of perfect fried-egg cells.
Excellent prognosis because Sam is highly susceptible to radiation. (Fried-egg cells / beta-ALP / Radiosensitive)
Choriocarcinoma Cory
The Blood Cannon. Cory fires 'cannonball metastases' straight into the pulmonary blood stream.
Highly aggressive malignancy of trophoblastic tissue. (up B-HCG / Haematogenous Spread)
BRCA Brenda's Ovarian Cousin
The Silent Swell. She fills the abdomen with ascites before anyone notices.
Psammoma bodies are laminated, calcified concretions seen on histology. (CA-125 / Serous Cystadenocarcinoma)
Pheochromocytoma Phil (The 10% Tumor)
The Catecholamine Storm. Phil dumps adrenaline, maxing out blood pressure.
The classic presentation: Pain, Perspiration, Palpitations, Pallor... (The 5 P's / Catecholamines)
Gastric Gary
The Lymphatic Telegraph. Gary signals his presence in the stomach by enlarging distant, specific lymph nodes.
A supraclavicular node is a massive red flag for abdominal malignancy. (Virchow's Node / Sister Mary Joseph sign)
Melanoma Mel (The Evolving Leopard)
The Deep Dive.
Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter, Evolving. (Bridges Solid to Pharma). (ABCDE / Breslow Depth)
Cisplatin Sid (The Platinum Hammer)
DNA Cross-Linker. Sid hammers the DNA strands together so they can't unzip for replication.
He breaks the kidneys and makes you deaf. Give Amifostine to shield the kidneys. (Nephrotoxicity / Ototoxicity)
Doxorubicin Dot (The Red Devil)
The Heart-Breaker. Dot is beautiful but she creates free radicals that eat the heart muscle.
Use Dexrazoxane (The Shield) to prevent Dot from trashing the pump. (Cardiotoxicity / Dilated Cardiomyopathy)
Vincristine Vinny (The Nerve-Stripper)
Spindle Sabotage. Vinny stops cell division at M-phase by freezing the pipes.
Side effect: 'Foot drop' and 'Glove-and-stocking' numbness. Don't let Vinny touch the CNS (Fatal if intrathecal). (Peripheral Neuropathy / Microtubule Inhibitor)
Cyclophosphamide Cy (The Bladder-Burner)
The Alkylating Agent. Cy cross-links DNA but leaves a toxic trash called Acrolein in the bladder.
Always deploy Mesna to neutralize the Acrolein trash before the bladder starts bleeding. (Hemorrhagic Cystitis / Acrolein)
Methotrexate Matt (The Folate Thief)
Synthesis Starvation. Matt steals the active folate needed to print new DNA.
Rescue the normal cells with Leucovorin (folinic acid bypass). (Inhibits Dihydrofolate Reductase)
5-FU Fred (The Pyrimidine Pirate)
The Fake Nucleotide. Fred jams the DNA printer permanently.
Classic side effect is Hand-foot syndrome. (Inhibits Thymidylate Synthase)
Imatinib Izzy
Targeted Neutralization. Izzy shuts down the specific mutant tyrosine kinase.
Targeted therapy for CML. Turned a fatal disease into a manageable one. (The BCR-ABL Fuse-Cutter)
Trastuzumab Tricia (Herceptin)
Receptor Blockade. Tricia physically blocks the overexpressed HER2 growth receptors.
Watch her: she's cardiotoxic too! (The HER2 Neutralizer)
Pembrolizumab Penny (The Checkpoint Sniper)
The Cloak Ripper. Penny rips the "Invisibility Cloak" off so the T-cells can attack.
Unleashes the immune system, but can cause severe autoimmune toxicities. (PD-1 Inhibitor)
Rituximab Richie (The CD20 Eraser)
The B-Cell Eraser. Richie targets the CD20 antigen, marking every B-cell for destruction.
Watch for PML (JC virus reactivation) due to profound immunosuppression. (Wipes out the B-cell population)
Bleomycin Ben (The Lung Scar-er)
Oxidative Shredding. Ben generates free radicals that shatter DNA into pieces.
Causes devastating, irreversible pulmonary fibrosis. (Pulmonary Fibrosis)
Tamoxifen Tammy (The Estrogen Switch)
The Tissue Toggle. Tammy blocks estrogen in the breast, but acts like super-estrogen in the bone and uterus.
Risk of endometrial cancer! (Antagonist (Breast) / Agonist (Bone/Uterus))
Anastrozole Ana (The Aromatase Stopper)
The Peripheral Drought. Ana stops aromatase from making estrogen outside the ovaries.
Only works in post-menopausal women. (Blocks peripheral estrogen production)
Etoposide Ed (The Topo-II Tangler)
The Untwist Snap. Ed makes the DNA strands get stuck when they try to untwist.
The tension builds until the DNA completely shatters. (DNA supercoiling blocker)
The Oncology Attending (Master Synthesis)
The Final Word.
"Stage it, grade it, name the mutation, and don't kill the patient with the chemo. Stay fluffy — and always double-check the labs." (Stage > Grade)
Corny Cornea (The Window)
The Clear Breach. If Corny is scratched, the Light Punks scatter into painful chaos.
The strongest refractor. Corny breathes O2 directly from the air. Inflammation (Keratitis) creates permanent vandalism (scars) on the lens.
Aquas the Humor (The Pressure)
The Inflation Pump. Fills the chamber to keep the eye from collapsing.
Drained via the Canal of Schlemm. If the drain is sabotaged, Aquas builds up until the pressure turns lethal for the nerves.
Iris the Aperture (The Gate)
The Light Gate. Regulates the photon-count entering the ring.
Controlled by Autonomic Tug-of-War. Sympathetics pull her wide (Fear); Parasympathetics shut her tight (Rest).
Ciliary Sid (The Focuser)
The Lens Squeezer. Sid pulls the strings to make the lens round for near-vision.
When Sid relaxes, the lens flattens for distance. As we age, the lens gets too stiff for Sid to squeeze (Presbyopia).
Crystal the Lens (The Refractor)
The Fine-Tuner. Provides the final adjustment for a sharp image on the sensor.
Crystal stays clear until proteins denature. She is the only part of the camera that can change shape.
Cataract Carl (The Cloud)
The Fog Machine. Dims the world and creates a Halo glare.
Carl is the physical manifestation of oxidized lens proteins. He effectively pulls a dirty curtain over the camera.
Phaco-Phil (The Shredder)
The Phaco-Blast. Phil pulverizes Cataract Carl in seconds and vacuums up the debris.
The modern surgical exorcism of the lens. Phil clears the stage for the artificial replacement.
IOL Irene (The Implant)
The Permanent View. A plastic lens that restores clarity forever.
Irene cannot accommodate like Crystal did, so the patient usually trades near-vision for distance clarity.
Minus-Max (Myopia)
The Distance Blur. Sees the ant on his knee, but the bus is a ghost.
The eye is too long for the lens's power. Correct with Minus (Concave) glasses to push the light back.
Plus-Paul (Hyperopia)
The Near-Focus Strain. Paul has to work hard even to see the horizon.
The eye is too short. The light aims behind the Retina. Correct with Plus (Convex) glasses to pull the light forward.
Asti-Gusti (Astigmatism)
The Fun-House Mirror. Everything is distorted because the focus is uneven.
Corny Cornea is shaped like a rugby ball instead of a basketball. Light has two different focal lines.
Presby-Pete (The Old-Age Sight)
The Arm-Extender. Pete has to hold the newspaper in the next room to read it.
Not a refractive error, but a mechanical failure. Crystal the Lens has simply become too stiff for Ciliary Sid to squeeze.
Glauco-Gus (The Silent Thief)
The Peripheral Fade. Gus steals the edges of the world until only a tunnel is left.
High IOP kills the axons at the optic disc. It is painless and permanent.
Angle-Al (The Emergency)
The Red-Eye Rock. Sudden agony, nausea, and Halos around lights.
The door (angle) to the drain slams shut. Aquas is trapped. The optic nerve starts dying instantly.
Prosta-Pete (Latanoprost)
The Drain Opener. Increases the back-door (uveoscleral) outflow of Aquas.
Pete makes the drain wider. Side effects: Long lashes and turning blue eyes brown.
Timmy-the-Block (Timolol)
The Pump-Stopper. Cuts the production of Aquas at the source.
Less fluid entering means less pressure. Careful: Timmy can sneak into the lungs and cause Bron[chospasm — text cut off at margin].
Roddy & Conny (The Sensors)
The Pixel Army. Roddy sees grey shadows; Conny sees neon colors.
Roddy is the night-fighter (Periphery); Conny is the day-sniper (Macula).
Mac-the-Degenerate (The Center Thief)
The Central Hole. You can see the clock, but never the time.
Mac destroys the fovea. In the Wet form, Annie-VEGF floods the sensor with blood.
Detach-Dan (The Wallpaper Ripper)
The Falling Curtain. A dark shadow moves across the field of vision.
Fluid gets behind the Retina and peels it off. Without the blood supply underneath, the Retina dies.
Diabetic Debbie (Retinopathy)
The Capillary Pop. Sugar-sludge causes micro-aneurysms and leaks.
Chronic ischemia forces Debbie to summon Annie-VEGF, who builds fragile, bleeding [vessels — text cut off at margin].
Optic-Otto (The Cable)
The High-Speed Blackout.
If Otto is inflamed (Optic Neuritis), vision fades and eyes hurt when they move. The classic MS sign.
Papil-Pam (The Signal)
The Pressure Signal.
Pam isn't an eye disease; she's a brain alarm. High intracranial pressure pushes the nerves into the eye.
Vitreo-Vinnie (The Jelly)
The Floater Parade.
As Vinnie shrinks with age, he pulls away from the wall. His shadows are the flies you see in the sky.
Annie-VEGF (The Saboteur)
The Illegal Road Builder.
Annie builds vessels where they don't belong. They leak, they bleed, and they cause sca[rs — text cut off at margin].
Pinky Pete (Conjunctivitis)
The Red Itch.
Inflammation of the outer skin. Bacterial Pete brings the pus; Viral Pete brings the water.
Keratitis Karl
The Cornea-Ripper.
Karl is deep and dangerous. He leaves scars on Corny that light can't pass through.
Uveitis Ursula
The Internal Revolt.
The immune system attacks the iris. Ursula loves to hang out with Rheuma-Rick.
Endo Ed (Endophthalmitis)
The Nuclear Option.
Infection inside the eyeball. Ed can turn the eye into a bag of pus in 24 hours.
Blepha Bill (Blepharitis)
The Crusty Margin.
Chronic inflammation of the lid. Bill clogs the oil pipes, making the tears evaporate too fast.
Stye Stan (Hordeolum)
The Painful Bump.
An acute pustule at the lid edge. Stan is a localized riot in a gland.
Chalazion Chester
The Cold Lump.
A painless, hard nodule. Chester is the aftermath of a blocked oil gland that didn't clear.
Entropion Enno
The Lash-Scratch.
The lid turns in, and the lashes act like sandpaper on Corny Cornea.
Strabi Stevie (Strabismus)
The Misalignment.
The eyes aren't looking at the same spot. This creates two different stories for the brain.
Ambly Annie (The Lazy Eye)
The Brain-Block.
If Stevie isn't fixed, the brain simply deletes the image from the weaker eye. Annie stays lazy forever.
Leuko Leo (Leukocoria)
The White Shadow.
The most dangerous sign in a child. Could be a Cataract or a Retinoblastoma monster.
Obstruction Olli
The Constant Tear.
The drain to the nose is blocked. Olli makes the baby weep 24/7.
Horner Harry
The Sympathetic Break.
The Fight wire is cut. The pupil stays small, the lid drops, and the face stays dry.
Argyll Robertson Al
The Prostitute's Pupil.
Reacts to near objects but ignores light. The classic red flag for Neurosyphilis.
Adie the Atonic
The Slow Dilator.
A large pupil that reacts very sluggishly to light. Usually a post-viral glitch in the ciliary ganglion.
Chiasm Charlie
The Crossing Guard.
A pituitary tumor presses on Charlie. You lose your wingman vision on both sides.
Scotoma Scott
The Blind Spot.
A specific patch of the sensor is dead.
Hemi-Anopsia Hank
The Half-Blind.
You lose the entire left or right side of the world.
Quadrant Quentin
The Quarter-Thief.
Quentin only steals a slice of the pie (e.g., Pie in the Sky deficit).
Isopter Izzy
The Cartographer.
Izzy draws the map of where the sensors are working and where they are dark.
Atropine Alice
The Permanent Wide-Eye.
Alice blocks the Constrict signal. You stay dilated for days and can't read.
Pilocarpine Phil
The Drain Puller.
Phil forces the pupil to shrink, which pulls the trabecular meshwork open to drain Aquas.
Dexa Dot
The Cooling Shield.
Stops the immune riot in Uveitis. Warning: Long-term Dot invites Cataract-Carl.
Fluorescein Flo
The Detective.
Flo stains the gaps in Corny Cornea. Under blue light, she reveals every ulcer and scratch.
Lasik Larry
The Cornea Carver.
Larry planes the surface of the eye to fix the focus.
Vitrectomy Vin
The Jelly-Vac.
Vin removes Vinnie-the-Jelly to clear out blood or reach Detach-Dan.
Buckle Bob
The Belt.
A silicone band squeezed around the eye to push the wall back against the peeling Retina.
Trabeculoplasty Ted
The Drain Laser.
Ted burns small holes in the meshwork to help Aquas escape Gus-the-Glaucoma.
The Slit-Lamp Sentry
The Ultimate Inspection.
The Attending's favorite tool to find the Flare in the soup.
The Ophthalmoscope
The Deep Dive.
Looking at the only place in the body where you can see live nerves and vessels.
The Ophthalmology Attending
The Pimp-Master.
Localize the glitch. Is it the pump, the window, or the cable?
Osteo-Blast & Blast
The Bridge-Builders.
Wolff's Law: No stress = weak bone; too much stress = bridge snaps.
Salter-Harris Sam
The Child-Chassis Break.
Type II most common; Type V (Crush) stops growth forever.
Compartment-Chris
The Fascial Vice.
Surgical emergency! Needs a Fasciotomy-Flight to let muscles breathe.
Non-Union Ned
The False Joint.
Caused by Biological Bankruptcy or Mechanical Anarchy.
Colles-the-Fork
The FOOSH-Fall.
Back-of-the-wrist snaps. Watch for Median-Nerve-Max getting pinched.
Scaphoid-Scott
The Invisible Break.
Hides for 10 days on X-ray. Waist breaks starve the bottom half (AVN).
Humerus-Hank
The Wrist-Drop.
Nerve wraps the middle. Fraying means the wrestler can't Thumbs Up.
Shoulder-Shifting-Sid
The Squared-Off Look.
Tears the Bankart-Bumper. Axillary-Nerve hits make deltoid go dark.
Cauda-Equina-Caleb
The Nerve-Bundle Squash.
911 emergency! Delay increases risk of permanent Diaper-Wrestling.
Open-Book-Oliver
The Volume-Expander.
A Pelvic Binder is the only thing that closes the book to stop internal bleeding.
Hip-Fracture-Hilda
The Granny-Snap.
Intracapsular neck fractures kill blood supply to the ball (Emergency Screws).
Disc-Danny
The Shooting Spark.
The Sciatic-Scream. Most retract, some need the Micro-Discectomy-Vacuum.
ACL-Al
The Pivot-Shift.
Al doesn't heal on his own. Needs a Hamstring-Graft-Rebuild to return to the ring.
Meniscus-Manny
The Jammed Hinge.
Knee clicks/locks. The inner edge has no blood and won't heal itself.
Tib-Fib-Terry
The Shaft-Snap.
Heavy-duty breaks. Kings of the IM-Nail—a titanium rod down the center.
Achilles-Arthur
The False Shot.
Feels like a gunshot. The strongest tendon gives up; wrestler can't stand on toes.
Greenstick-Gary
The Bend-and-Snap.
Kid bones are rubbery. Gary sometimes needs to be Completed to heal straight.
SCFE-Scottie
The Sliding Ball.
Ortho emergency! If Scottie keeps sliding, the hip dies. Needs a Single-Screw-Stop.
Nursemaid-Nancy
The Annular-Tear.
The Supination-Flexion-Flip pops the ligament back and cures Nancy instantly.
Hip-Dysplasia-Dot
The Shallow Socket.
Needs the Pavlik-Harness-Hug to force the ball in so the cup grows deep.
Plate-and-Screw Pete
The Rigid Fix.
Heals by Primary Intent (no callus). King of smooth articular fractures.
IM-Nail-Nate
The Internal Scaffolding.
Shares weight with the bone; encourages Callus-Chris to build around him.
External-Fixator-Ed
The Scaffold-Outside.
Used when skin is too Angry (swollen/infected) for plates. Holds the fortress.
K-Wire-Kelly
The Needle-Fix.
Used for tiny bones or holding pieces for Pete. Pulled out with pliers later.
Arthritis-Artie
The Bone-on-Bone.
Artie eats the Cartilage-Cushion. End-stage wear-and-tear requires Joint Rebellion.
Total-Hip-Holly
The New Foundation.
Most successful op in history. Restores Range of Motion instantly.
Total-Knee-Ken
The Surface-Resurfacer.
Caps the ends of bones. Alignment is everything; if crooked, limp forever.
Loosening-Larry
The Shake-Up.
Bone around the wobble melts (Osteolysis). Needs a Revision-Rebuild.
Rotator-Cuff-Ray
The Wing-Drop.
Wrestler can't hold their shield up. Common in overhead athletes.
MCL-Mitch
The Side-Slump.
The Friendly Ligament with good blood supply. Usually heals with a brace.
Carpal-Tunnel-Carl
The Midnight-Numb.
Numbness in first 3 fingers. Needs a Roof-Release (cut Flexor Retinaculum).
Tennis-Elbow-Tom
The Backhand-Burn.
Not inflammation, but Angiofibroblastic Tendinosis (failed micro-tears).
Septic-Joint-Sgt
The Cartilage-Melter.
Destroys a hip in 24h. Needs Washout-Wilfred to flush with gallons of saline.
Fat-Embolism-Felix
The Marrow-Migration.
The reason we fix femurs fast. If Felix hits lungs, it's a battle for oxygen.
Cauda-Equina-Caleb Redux
The Saddle-Squeeze.
If they can't pee, it's an emergency! Decompress < 48 hours or paralysis.
Open-Fracture-Ophelia
The Bone-Breech.
An Infection-Magnet. Needs IV antibiotics instantly and multiple washouts. Never close primarily!
Osteo-Porosis-Pam
The Silent Swiss-Cheese.
Imbalance of Builders vs. Crushers. Bisphosphonates are the counter-spell.
Osteo-Sarcoma-Sam
The Sun-Explosion.
Sam doesn't follow rules. Grows New Bone in a chaotic sunray pattern (mostly in teens).
Ewing's-Ernie
The Layered-Assault.
A small-round-blue-cell tumor. Loves the Diaphysis (shaft) of long bones.
Paget's-Pat
The Chaotic Rebuild.
Bone becomes huge but wobbly. Can lead to High-Output-Heart-Failure.
Weber-the-Ankle-Wrench
The High-Ankle Squeeze.
Weber C needs Screws-of-Stability because the whole joint is wide open.
Lisfranc-Leo
The Mid-Foot Split.
Easy to miss on X-ray. Stable-Leos are rare; usually needs Bolts-and-Bridges.
Hallux-Valgus-Hal
The Big-Toe Drift.
From Tight-Boot-Terror. Needs an Osteotomy-Cut to point straight again.
Plantar-Fasciitis-Phil
The Heel-Stab.
A tight-tendon problem, not a spur problem. Needs Stretching-Slings.
Cefazolin-Cef
The Surgical Shield.
In Ortho, Biofilm-is-Death. The most important card to prevent a Septic-Slam.
Lovenox-Lenny
The Clot-Cutter.
Ortho patients are Hypercoagulable. Lenny is the law for 14-35 days post-op.
Bisphosphonate-Ben
The Clast-Muzzle.
Muzzles the Bone-Crushers. Beware Jaw-Necrosis-Jinx. Makes bone thick but brittle.
Morphine-Monty
The Heavy-Duty Numb.
Slows breath/gut. Use for the Surgical-Storm, then switch to Irene-Ibuprofen.
The C-Arm-Scribe
The Live-Action-X-Ray.
Lets the surgeon see the Nate-Nail sliding into place in real-time.
The Neuro-Vascular-Bundle
The Survival-Line.
Always check distal pulse! If the bone is fixed but the foot is cold, you lose.
The AO-Philosophy
The Bone-Code.
The 4 commandments. Break the code, and the bone will never heal.
The Fat-Pad-Sign
The Hidden-Fracture-Finder.
Fat pushed out means Blood-in-the-Joint. Even if unseen, the bone is cracked.
Synthesis Quest 1
The FOOSH.
Quest: Identify Colles-the-Fork. Fix: Sugar-Tong-Splint or Plate-and-Screw-Pete.
Synthesis Quest 2
The Frame-Fixer.
Reduction, Fixation, Mobilization. Why are you still holding the drill? Stay fluffy! Quest: Identify Compartment-Chris. Action: Emergency Fasciotomy-Flight.
Synthesis Quest 3
The Twist.
Quest: Identify ACL-Al. Action: Perform Lachman-Test to confirm.
Tympanic-Ty
THE SOUND-VIBRATION. Ty catches the airwaves and kicks the OSSICLE-ORCHESTRA into gear.
If Ty is perforated (Tympanik-Tear), the Bridge is broken. If he's sucked in (Retraction) Choles-the-Steatoma might be growing behind him.
Eustachian-Earl
THE POP. Earl opens up to let the middle ear breathe and equalize pressure.
If Earl goes on strike (Dysfunction), the ear fills with fluid (Serous-Swamp) and Ty the Drummer gets pulled into a vacuum.
Ossicle-Oscar
THE LEVER-FORCE. Oscar takes Ty's vibration and concentrates it onto the Oval Window.
If Oscar gets stiff (Otosclerosis), the Stapes-Footplate gets stuck. The music stops before it hits the brain.
Cochlea-Cora
THE FLUID-WAVE. Cora turns mechanical waves into electrical Brain-Currents.
Cora is lined with Hair-Cell-Soldiers. If they are shell-shocked by loud noise, the high frequencies die first.
Otitis-Externa-Ex
THE CANAL-CLOG. Ex makes the outer ear canal red, swollen, and agonizingly tender to the touch.
Moisture breaks down the wax-shield, letting the Bacterial Punks move in. Ex is surface-riot.
Media-Mitch
THE PRESSURE-BURST. Mitch traps pus behind the drum. It hurts until the drum Pops and the pressure releases.
Usually follows a cold when Eustachian-Earl fails to drain the middle ear swamp.
Choles-the-Steatoma
THE DESTRUCTIVE PEARL. Choles is a skin-sac that grows where it doesn't belong, eating the Ossicle-Oscar bones as it expands.
Not a tumor, but a destructive cyst. If not evicted by surgery, Choles can break into the brain or the inner ear.
Mastoid-Max
THE BONE-STORM. Max is what happens when Mitch moves into the Air-Cells of the skull.
Mastoiditis is a surgical emergency if the Bone-honeycomb melts, the infection can reach the brain.
BPPV-Benny
THE ROOM-SPIN. Benny drops Ear-Crystals into the semicircular canals where they don't belong.
Gravity moves the crystals, telling the brain you're spinning when you're just lying down. Fix it with the Epley-Adjustmus.
Meniere-Monty
THE FLUID-FLOOD. Monty builds up too much fluid in the inner ear until the system Overloads.
The Attacks can last for hours. Monty is the master of Fluctuating Hearing Loss.
Vestibular-Vince
THE BALANCE-BLACKOUT. Vince inflames the balance-nerve, causing days of intense dizziness and nausea.
Usually viral. Unlike Monty, Vince doesn't mess with the hearing—he only sabotages the Level-Sensor.
Acoustic-Artie
THE SLOW-GROWTH SQUEEZE. Artie is a tumor that slowly chokes the hearing and balance signals.
Rule of ENT: Unilateral hearing loss is Acoustic-Artie until proven otherwise by MRI.
Septal-Sam
THE AIRFLOW-BLOCK. Sam is a crooked wall that makes breathing through one side of the Nose-Tunnel impossible.
Often a legacy of a previous Wrestling Match (Trauma). Requires a Septoplasty-Surgical-Rebuild.
Sinus-Sid
THE PRESSURE-HEADACHE. Sid traps mucus in the skull-caves until they become Bio-Reactors.
Occurs when the Ostium-Exit is blocked by swelling. If Sid stays chronic, Poly-Pete moves in.
Epistaxis-Eddie
THE RED LEAK. Eddie starts a blood-riot in the nose. Usually just a Bio-Pressure-Blip.
Posterior Eddie is the Heavyweight—he bleeds down the throat and needs Balloon-Packing to stop.
Poly-Pete
THE GRAPE-CLOG. Pete is a fleshy, Grape-like growth that dandles in the nose, blocking smell and air.
Chronic inflammation-edema of the mucosa. Pete is the sign of an Allergy-War gone long-term.
Strep-Sgt
THE WHITE-COAT RIOT. Sgt covers the tonsils in white Pus-Armor and makes swallowing feel like razor blades.
Usually Group A Strep. If the Sgt isn't defeated, he might send his Rheumatic-Ghost to attack the heart.
Peritonsillar-Phil
THE PUS-POCKET. Phil builds a massive abscess behind the tonsil, pushing the Uvula-Punching Bag to the side.
A surgical emergency! Phil needs a Needle-Aspiration-Crisis or the airway might close.
Epiglottis-Emma
THE AIRWAY-SLAM-DOOR. Emma swells up like a giant red cherry and closes the Respiratory-Airway-Rover.
Usually Hib-driven. Do not look in the throat with a tongue depressor—you might cause the final Door-Slam.
Croup-Chris
THE SUBGLOTTIC SQUEEZE. Chris narrows the pipe just below the vocal cords, making every breath sound like a whistle.
You need cool night air and steroids to calm his Squeeze.
Cordy-the-Vocalist
THE VIBRATE-SPEAK. Cordy flaps together at high speed to create the Voice-Current.
If one Cordy is paralyzed, the voice becomes a Breathy-Whisper.
Singer-Sarah
THE CALLOUS-RASPY. Sarah builds Screamer's Nodules—small callouses from too much Acoustic-Wrestling.
Chronic vocal abuse. Sarah needs Voice-Rest and therapy, not surgery.
Malignant-Max
THE INVASIVE-GRIT. Max is a crusty growth that eats the vocal cords and spreads to the Neck-Nodes.
Squamous Cell Carcinoma. If Max takes over, the whole Voice-Box might have to be evicted.
Reflux-Ray
THE ACID-SPILL. Ray is the Silent Reflux—he spills stomach acid onto the vocal cords at night.
Unlike GERD, Ray doesn't always cause heartburn. He just irritates the Throat-Lining until it swells.
Branchial-Betty
THE CONGENITAL-LUMP. Betty is a leftover Gill-Slit from the womb that fills with fluid.
Betty is always on the Side. If she gets infected, she turns into an abscess.
Thyro-Thad
THE RISING-LUMP. Thad is a leftover track from when the thyroid moved from the tongue to the neck.
If the lump moves up when you stick out your tongue, it's Thad. Requires the Sistrunk-Extraction.
Salivary-Stan
THE GLAND-BLOCK. Stan traps saliva behind a Stone-Obstruction until the gland explodes in pain.
Stan loves the Submandibular gland because the saliva there is thick and runs uphill.
Mumps-Molly
THE CHIPMUNK-CHEEK. Molly makes the face swell up so much the ears stick out.
Viral. Molly is the reason for the MMR-Shield.
Weber & Rinne
THE CONDUCTION-TEST. They tell us if the problem is in the Bridge (Conductive) or the Sensor (Sensorineural).
Rinne: Bone > Air = Conductive. Weber: Lateralizes to bad ear = Conductive; to good ear = Sensorineural.
Otoscope-Oz
THE CANAL-VISION. Oz allows us to look past the wax-guards and see Tympanic-Ty directly.
Oz is the gatekeeper. Without Oz, Mitch and Choles stay hidden in the dark.
Naso-Endo-Ned
THE THROAT-SPY. Ned snakes through the nose to look at Emma-Epiglottis and Cordy-the-Vocalist in real-time.
The gold standard for seeing the Airway-Runway without the patient gagging.
Audiogram-Annie
THE HEARING-MAP. Annie draws the landscape of what the patient can hear and what is lost to the Silence-Shadows.
If the lines are far apart, there's an Air-Bone-Gap—proof of a conductive bridge failure.
Ciprodex-Cid
THE DOUBLE-STRIKE. Cid kills the bacteria and cools down the swelling in Otitis-Externa-Ex.
Use it for 7 days and only use if the Drum (Ty) is intact, unless it's the Otic-Safe version!
Fluticasone-Flo
THE ALLERGY-BRAKE. Flo calms the Mucosal-Riot in the nose, shrinking Poly-Pete and opening Sinus-Sid.
Works locally. Flo doesn't start the fight, she ends it by stopping the recruitment of inflammatory cells.
Oxymetazoline-Oxy
THE INSTANT-OPEN. Oxy shrinks the nasal pipes instantly for Emergency Breathing.
Use it for >3 days and you meet Rhinitis-Rebound-Rob—the nose becomes permanently clogged without the drug.
Meclizine-Mick
THE MOTION-SICKNESS SHIELD. Mick numbs the Balance-Center so the patient can stop vomiting.
Mick doesn't fix the crystals; he just turns down the Brain's Spin-Alarm.
Myringotomy-Mike
THE BYPASS-DRAIN. Mike cuts a hole in Tympanic-Ty and places a tiny pipe to do Eustachian-Earl's job.
Prevents Mitch-Media from returning by keeping the middle ear swamp dry and ventilated.
T&A-Tommy
THE EVICTION. Tommy removes the Tonsil-Towers permanently to stop the Strep-Sgt from ever returning.
Post-op risk: The Day-7-Bleed. When the scabs fall off, things can get bloody!
FESS-Frank
THE CAVE-REBUILD. Frank uses Ned-the-Scope to widen the Ostium-Exits so Sinus-Sid can drain naturally.
Removing the clogs (tissue/polyps) to restore the Aero-Dynamics of the skull.
Tracheostomy-Tray
THE ULTIMATE-BYPASS. Tray creates a new airway door in the neck, bypassing Emma-Epiglottis and the Mouth-Traffic.
A life-saver for long-term Airway-Assassins or those who can't breathe through the Main-Entrance.
Baha-Bob
THE SKULL-VIBRATOR. Bob bypasses the Conductive-Bridge entirely by vibrating the skull to talk directly to Cochlea-Cora.
Perfect for patients with no canal or a destroyed Ossicle-Oscar.
Cochlear-Clara
THE NERVE-PULSE. Clara bypasses Cochlea-Cora entirely, using electrical probes to talk to the brain.
When the Sensor-Failure—Clara doesn't make sound louder; she creates a new Electrical-Language.
Tinnitus-Tim
THE PHANTOM-SCREAM. Tim creates a ringing or buzzing that only the patient can hear.
Often the Cry of dying hair cells in the cochlea. The Brain makes up the sound to fill the silence.
Dysphagia-Dot
THE WRONG-PIPE-SLIDE. Dot makes food go down the Respiratory-Runway instead of the Esophagus-Road.
Dot is generous to Pneumonia-Pete. Dot is the enemy of the Airway-Sentry.
Foreign-Body-Felix
THE OBJECT-BLOCK. Felix is a bead, a bean, or a coin stuck where it doesn't belong.
In the ear: Do not get the bean wet (it will swell!). In the lung: Unilateral-Wheeze is the clue.
Septal-Hematoma-Hank
THE SADDLE-NOSE-THREAT. Hank traps blood under the septal skin, cutting off the Cartilage-Food-Supply.
Emergency! If Hank isn't drained, the septum dies, and the nose collapses into a Saddle-Shape.
Ludwig's-Luke
THE TONGUE-LIFT. Luke inflames the floor of the mouth until the tongue is pushed up and back, choking the patient.
Usually a Dental-Infection-Riot. Luke is an Airway-Assassin in disguise.
Necrotizing-Nick
THE BONE-ROT. Nick is the Final-Evolution of Ex-Externa. He eats through the ear canal and into the skull.
Nick targets the cranial nerves. If Nick isn't stopped with IV antibiotics, the Brain-Fortress falls.
The Centor-Scribe
THE ANTIBIOTIC-KEY. The Scribe tells us who gets the Penicillin-Pen and who just needs tea.
Prevents Resistance-Rob by only attacking the Sgt when he's actually present.
The Tuning-Fork-Trio
THE BRIDGE-CHECK.
Lateralizes to the bad side? Conduction fail! Lateralizes to the good ear? Sensorineural fail!
The Hot-Potato Voice
THE SOUND-MUFFLE. The patient sounds like they are trying to talk with a scorching hot potato in their throat.
Caused by massive swelling in the oropharynx, preventing normal Sound-Reflection.
The Steeple-Sign Sentry
THE CROUP-CONFIRM. The trachea looks like a church steeple instead of a square pillar.
The trachea looks like a church steeple instead of a square pillar.
The ENT Attending (Doc FrizzleBob)
THE ORIFICE-ORACLE. Doc: Look past the wax. Feel the neck. Is the airway safe? If not, who are you still holding a tongue depressor? Stay fluffy!
MedKayfabe! Stay fluffy!
Synthesis Quest 1
Identify the Media-Mitch and explain why the pain vanished.
A 6-year-old wrestler has a fever and a red, bulging drum. Suddenly, the pain stops and yellow fluid leaks out.
Synthesis Quest 2
Identify Singer-Sarah and decide: Surgery or Silence?
A lead singer has been hoarse for 2 weeks. The On-the-Scope shows two small bumps at the edges of the white ribbons.
Synthesis Quest 3
Identify the room spinner and confirm the Epley-Adjustment.
A patient says the room spins for 30 seconds every time they roll out of bed. Weber: to bad ear? Rinne: Bone > Air. Rinne is normal.
Apoptosis-Arnie (The Clean Exit)
The Programmed Suicide. Arnie shrinks and packs his bags without waking the Immune Police.
Follows orders(BCL-2/P53). The Quiet Sacrifice — preventing viral punks or cancerous revolts.
Necrosis-Nick (The Messy Death)
The Toxic Explosion. Splits DAMP-Guns everywhere.
Result of Ischemia/toxins. Triggers a Neutrophil-Riot (causing secondary neighbor damage).
Atrophy-Artie (The Shrinker)
The Size-Reduction. Gets smaller to survive a Famine-Match.
Digests his own organelles to save metabolic rent. Efficient but weak.
Metaplasia-Mel (The Shape-Shifter)
The Tissue-Swap. Replaces a sensitive wall with tough armor to survive chronic irritation.
A defensive move, but a Pre-Cancer-Risk that can evolve into Malignant-Mel.
Neutro-Nathan (The First Responder)
The Kamikaze Attack. Arrives first to spray Oxygen-Bleach (Free Radicals).
Short-lived. Dies in the trenches, forming the Pus-Puddle of acute inflammation.
Macro-Maggie (The Cleaner)
The Garbage-Eater. Cleans Nathan's mess and decides if it's time for Building-Henry.
The Director who presents the enemy's head to the T-Cell-Tacticians.
Granuloma-Gerry (The Lockdown)
The Eternal Prison. Builds a wall when Stubborn-Strep or Tuberculo-Tot can't be killed.
Type IV hypersensitivity — the wall breaks via immunosuppression, prisoners escape.
Fibro-Fiona (The Scar-Maker)
The Permanent Patch. Fills holes with Biological-Cement (Scar tissue).
Provides strength but loses function — heart patched by Fiona won't pump.
Benign-Benny (The Localist)
The Slow-Growing. Just wants to grow in his own little bubble.
Only danger is Pressure (e.g., in the Brain-Bunker where space is limited).
Malignant-Max (The Invader)
The Border-Breacher. Doesn't respect the Basement Membrane.
Cuts through walls and hitchhikes on the Lymph-Highway to reach distant lands.
Metastasis-Mitch (The Traveler)
The Global Colonialist. Sets up Sub-Malitias in distant organs.
Stage IV war. Once Mitch colonizes, the Stain-Brigade rarely wins alone.
PS3-Peter (The Guardian)
The DNA-Police. Checks blueprints for errors and calls Apoptosis-Arnie to end mutated cells.
If Peter is deleted (Li-Fraumeni), the Anaplasia-Assassins go completely unchecked.
Livor-the-Livid (Post-Mortem Lividity)
The Gravity-Stain. Shows where blood settled after the Heart-Pump stopped.
If Livor is on the back but the body is face-down, the Scene-Scenery was tampered with.
Rigor-the-Stiff (Rigor Mortis)
The Muscle-Lock. ATP-Batteries run out, and Calcium-Gates leak.
The Corpse-Handcuff that starts at the jaw and moves down.
Algor-the-Cold (Post-Mortem Cooling)
The Thermal-Drop. Cools the body to match the Arena-Temperature.
Used via the Henssge-Nomogram to build a Time-Since-Death clock.
Putrefaction-Paul (The Decomposer)
The Gas-Factory. Uses Internal-Bacteria-Punks to digest from the inside out.
The natural Cleanup-Crew that turns the body green and distended.
Abrasion-Abby (The Scuff)
The Friction-Sign. Shows the direction of the Slide from a Scrape-Match.
Yellow/dry = happened after the bell. Red/crusty = happened during the fight.
Contusion-Connie (The Bruise)
The Inner-Leak. A Hemorrhage-in-Hiding. Skin intact, but pipes broken underneath.
Follows the Heme-Breakdown-Road (Hemoglobin → Biliverdin → Bilirubin).
Laceration-Larry (The Tear)
The Blunt-Force-Rip. Caused by crushing, leaving messy bridges behind.
Hallmark of the Hammer or Fist (unlike an Incised clean cut).
Bullet-Bill (The Entrance vs. Exit)
The Kinetic-Tunnel. Entrance-Gate is neat; Exit-Gate is a chaotic mess.
Contact-Range shots leave a Muzzle-Stamp or Soot-Shadow on the skin.
Hanging-Harry (The Ligature)
The Gravity-Choke. Uses body weight to shut the Oxygen-Highway and Carotid-Pipes.
Death is usually from Brain-Ischemia, not a broken neck.
Strangling-Stella (The Manual Choke)
The Hands-on-Halt. A Closer-Combat move.
Causes Tardieu-Spots (petechiae) as veins are blocked but arteries keep pumping.
Drowning-Drake (The Wet-Lung)
The Fluid-Invasion. Fills the lungs with Arena-Water.
Diatoms (algae) deep in the bone marrow prove the wrestler was breathing water before dying.
Cyanide-Cy (The Bitter Almond)
The Mitochondrial-Jam. Stops Cellular-Engines from using oxygen; blood stays red because cells can't eat it.
Kills the Electron-Transport-Chain. The victim suffocates despite O2-rich blood.
Nutmeg-Nancy (The Congested Liver)
The Backflow-Stain. Happens when Cardio-Carl fails and blood backs up into the Liver-sponge.
Central-Veins flood with red while edges turn tan.
Sago-Spleen (Amyloidosis)
The Protein-Clog. Amyloid-Alice deposits Sticky-Goo in the spleen.
Misfolded proteins that body can't clear turn the organs into Stiff-Statues.
Bread-and-Butter Bill (Pericarditis)
The Rough-Surface. Coats the heart in Fibrin-Glue.
The inflammation makes the heart scratch against its housing (friction rub).
Shrunken-Sheila (Chronic Pyelonephritis)
The Kidney-Contractor. Turns the kidney into a Micro-Lump after too many UTI-Uprisings.
Renal-Pipes block with pink goo, appearing like Thyroid-Tissue under the scope.
Shock-Shaun (MODS)
The Global Shutdown. Occurs when Total-Pressure fails and all organs starve.
The Death-Spiral. If Lungs (ARDS) and Kidneys (ATN) fail, the match is lost.
Gouty-George (The Crystal-Stab)
The Toe-Torture. Drops Uric-Acid-Needles into Joints, joining an Inflammation-Riot.
Loves the Big-Toe-Ring. Podagral. Rich Purine snacks are his fuel.
Lupus-Lucy (SLE)
The Self-Sabotage. Her immune-army gets confused and attacks the Kidney-Filters and Skin-Shield.
A Type III hypersensitivity Immune-Complex war.
Sarcoid-Sarah (The Non-Caseating)
The Mystery-Lump. Builds Granuloma-Gerry's everywhere, but crucially without the Caseous-Center.
A mysterious immune-revolt that loves to hide in the Lung-Gates.
Athero-Al (The Plaque)
The Pipe-Narrower. Builds Gunk-Walls inside arteries, slowing Oxygen-Traffic.
If Al's wall pops, he triggers the Clot-Monster for a Heart-Halt.
Aneurysm-Annie (The Bulge)
The Weak-Wall-Balloon. Stretches the Pipe-Armor until it bursts.
A Berry-Burst causes a sudden Thunderclap-Headache.
Thrombos-the-Clot (The Jam)
The Static-Stoppage. Builds a Blood-Dam that halts flow completely.
Born in a moving stream = Lines of Zahn. Born after death = Currant-Jelly.
Embolus-the-Exile (The Drifter)
The Long-Distance Strike. A piece of Thrombus that breaks free to jam a Smaller-Pipe.
A Saddle-Embolus blocks the main Lung-Highway, ending the match instantly.
Emphy-Sema (The Air-Trapper)
The Wall-Dissolver. Eats the Alveolar-Balloons into useless, flabby Air-Sacs.
Loss of Snap (Elasticity). Can get air in, but can't get it out (Pink-Puffer).
Bronchitis-Bill (The Blue Bloater)
The Mucus-Flood. Fills Airway-Tunnels with blue sludge.
Chronic irritation leads to Gland-Expansion, the king of the Smoker's Cough.
Pneu-Moni (The Lung-Solidifier)
The Liquid-Lung. Fills the Air-Balloons with pus/blood until the lung is Solid like a liver.
Gray Hepatization: RBCs die but the fibrin-armor stays, permanently stealing the Air-Space.
Silic-the-Stoner (Silicosis)
The Sand-Lung. Breathing Rock-Dust turns soft lungs into hard, scarred stone.
Macro-Maggies eat the dust but die, calling Fibro-Fiona to build a permanent scar-tomb.
Nephritic-Nate (The Blood-Leaker)
The Clogged-Filter. Inflames the Glomerulus-Grit until blood leaks and the Pressure-Alarm sounds.
Post-Strep Nate is a Type III War. Immune-Complexes riot in the filter.
Nephrotic-Nelly (The Protein-Drain)
The Sieve-Leak. Filter is so broken that all the Albumin-Gold drains out, causing whole swelling.
MCD-Molly (Minimal Change Disease) attacks junior wrestlers, erasing the Podocyte-Feet.
ATN-Andy (Acute Tubular Necrosis)
The Pipe-Melt. Renal-Pipes die and fall apart, clogging the system with Muddy-Debris.
Most common cause of Acute Renal Failure. If the host survives, pipes can regrow.
Renal-Cell-Ray (The Gold-Tumor)
The Yellow-Invasion. A bright yellow tumor that loves to grow into the vein and travel to the heart.
Clear Cells are full of lipids. Ray is a Vascular-Master who builds his own blood supply.
H&E-Holly (The Standard)
The Pink-and-Blue Vision. Provides the Standard-Map of Punk-Villain-Battlefield.
Blue means Acid-Lover (DNA/RNA); Pink means Base-Lover (Cytoplasm).
PAS-the-Sugar-Seeker
The Glycogen-Glow. Highlights everything sugar: Basement Membranes, Fungal Punks, Sugar-Stores.
A thick Basement Membrane glows as a solid, unmistakable bright magenta line.
Prussian-Blue-Pete
The Rust-Finder. Turns hidden Iron-Stores (Hemosiderin) bright blue.
Used to find where Hank-Hemorrhage was hiding or to catch iron-overload.
IHC-Isaac (Immunohistochemistry)
The Identity-Tag. Uses Special-Key-Antibodies to unlock the true name of an Anaplastic tumor.
CD20+ = B-Cell-Brawler. CK7+ = Epithelial-Elite. Isaac never guesses; he proves it.
The Y-Incision-Yoda
The Total-Access. Opens the Body-Box to expose all the organ-tenants.
The very first step of the Sectio-Session. Everything starts with Yoda.
The Rokitansky-Roll
The Block-Lift. Removes all the tenants in one connected package.
Preserves the Connections to see if a Bile-Bandit escaped into the blood.
The Virchow-Slice
The Detail-Cut. Takes organs out one-by-one and slices them to find Hidden-Scars.
The Old-School way. Perfect for hunting tiny pneumonias deep in the lung.
The Tox-Sieve (Toxicology)
The Ghost-Hunter. Finds the Chemical-Saboteurs the eyes can't see.
Vitreous-Humor is the ultimate vault for sugar or alcohol — it stays clean the longest.
The Path-Attending (Doc FrizzleBob)
The Morphological-Oracle. The eyes see what the mind knows.
Inflammation, infarction, or infection? Show me the Basement membrane!
Synthesis Quest 1: The Nutmeg Shadow
The Backwards Flow.
Identify the Pump-Failer (Cardio-Carl) and explain why the liver looks like a spice.
Synthesis Quest 2: The Silent Thief
The Plaque-Pressure.
Explain the connection between the Pipe-Gunk and the Brain-Bleed in a Berry-Annie burst.
Synthesis Quest 3: The Golden Leak
The Melted Feet.
Identify the syndrome and name the character responsible for erasing the Podocyte-Feet.
Apgar-the-Scribe (The First Score)
The Welcome-Check: Judges the Newborn Knight at 1 and 5 minutes for Resuscitation-Rescue.
Score <7 is a call for backup. Reports only on the Transition-Triumph from the womb.
Surfactant-the-Slippery (RDS)
The Anti-Collapse: Reduces tension in Alveolar-Arenas, keeping them open.
Without it, lungs turn to Stiff Stone (Hyaline Membrane). Give Steroid Stella to mom.
Bilirubin-the-Yellow (Jaundice)
The Skin-Stainer: Liver Factory is too slow or Red-Cell-Inventory breaks too fast.
Yellow-Mist crosses the blood-brain barrier into the Basal-Ganglia-Bunker (Kernicterus). Blue light fixes it.
Duct-the-Diverter (PDA)
The Fetal-Shortcut: Bypasses lungs in the womb, must Snap-Shut after the first breath.
Use Indo-Lock to close, or Prostin-Plug to keep open for Cyano-Secrets.
VSD-the-Vortex (Ventricular Septal Defect)
The Wall-Leak: Oxygenated blood spills back into the Lung-Pump.
Most common defect. Pressure rises until the Shunt-Flips to Eisenmenger-the-End-Game.
Tetralogy-the-Tet (Cyanotic Heart)
The Blue-Spell: Crying makes them turn blue as blood bypasses lungs.
The Squat-Move increases systemic resistance, forcing blood back to lungs.
Coarct-the-Kink (Aortic Coarctation)
The Pressure-Split: Narrowing in the Main-Highway stops flow to Lower-Limb-Lands.
Turner-the-Kink association. Heart pumps like a maniac to get past the Kink.
TGA-the-Switch (Transposition)
The Parallel-Paradox: Lungs and body are in two separate circles.
Lethal without a Mixing-Hole. A Keep-It-Open Emergency for Duct-the-Diverter.
RSV-the-Wheezer (Bronchiolitis)

Paraneoplastic Spells

The Pulm Attending

Quest: The Silent Choke
The Drive Drop
Hypoventilation. The lungs work fine (A-a is normal), but the brain forgot to breathe.
Dopamine-Dino
The Euphoria Spike. Too much in the mesolimbic track = Hallucinations. Too little in the mesocortical track = Flat affect.

Serotonin-Sally
The Rhythm Keeper. Controls sleep, appetite, and the will to wrestle.

GABA-Garry
The Big Chill. Tells the neurons to shut up and relax.
Benzodiazepines strengthen Garry's grip. A sudden withdrawal means brain on fire (seizures).
Glutamate-Gus
The Spark. Gus is Garry's archnémesis. He turns on the lights and lets the sparks fly.
Too much Gus leads to excitotoxicity. Ketamine blocks Gus to perform a hard system reset.
Schizo-Sam
The Delusion Bubble. Sam creates a reality where only he knows the rules.
Driven by Dino's rampage in the mesolimbic system. Requires at least 1 core symptom: delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech.
Schizoaffective Sid
The Dual Threat. A dangerous mix of Sam's delusions and Barry's mood swings.
Sid is a border-crosser. He must prove his psychosis can exist even without the emotional roller coaster.
Brief Psychotic Berty
The Snap. A sudden break with reality, usually after a traumatic match.
A temporary system failure. Berty returns completely to his old self after the match concludes.
Delusional Dan
The Unshakable Belief. Dan firmly believes the referee loves him or the FBI is hunting him.
Aside from his one quirk, Dan functions perfectly. He's not schizophrenic; he's just extremely stubborn.
Bipolar Barry
The Flight of Ideas. Builds a skyscraper ego in one night or feels like a crushed bug.
During mania, Barry needs no sleep and spends all his gold tokens. He thinks he is the invincible champion.
Major Depressive Debbie
The Gravity Well. Debbie makes every movement an ordeal. Even breathing feels like wrestling against lead.
Massive withdrawal of Sally and Nora. The world loses its color and value.
Persistent Polly
The Eternal Grey. Polly isn't as heavy as Debbie, but she never goes away.
A chronic state of not-quite-happiness. She is the rain that never stops.
Cyclothymic Cy
The Constant Ripple. Cy is never stable, but his waves are small enough to stay out of the hospital.
The lite version of Barry. Most unstable character on the roster, but always stays in the ring.
Panic-Pete
The Suffocator. Pete makes the heart race and the throat tighten with no opponent in the ring.
A false alarm from Norepi-Nora. Pete thinks he's dying even though he's just standing in a supermarket.
Agoraphobic Abby
The Locker Room Lockdown. Abby fears places where she cannot escape quickly.
Often the result of Pete's attacks. Abby shrinks her world until only her house remains.
OCD-Otto
The Endless Reset. Otto must tie his shoes 50 times, otherwise the stadium will explode.
The action (compulsion) only serves to temporarily silence the agonizing thought (obsession).
PTSD-Paul
The Time Warp. Paul is catapulted back into his worst match by a sound or a smell.
The brain has not archived the trauma. It remains an open wound that can tear again at any time.
Hali the Haloperidol

The Ultimate Override. The only one who wins when all other antipsychotics have failed.

Rizzy the Risperidone
The Prolactin Leak. Dampens psychosis but lets hormones go wild (gynecomastia/lactation).

Olly the Olanzapine
The Metabolic Expansion. Stops voices but makes the wrestler twice as heavy within weeks.

Lexy the SSRI
The Vacuum Plug. Plugs the drains so Sally can stay in the ring longer.

Venny the SNRI

Ty the TCA

The Old Guard. Unpopular due to anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation).

The Smooth Landing. Used to bring wrestlers safely through alcohol withdrawal.

Paranoid Pat
The Conspiracy Theory. Thinks everyone in the crowd and his partner wants to betray him.
Not psychotic; just extremely suspicious. Reads hostile intent into harmless comments.

Hot-Spot-the-Isotope

Cold-Node-the-Void

Pet-the-Sugar-Eater

V/Q-the-Mismatch

Seldinger-the-Entry

Stent-the-Scaffold

Drainage-the-Drain

FAST-Fiona

Tension-Tony

Deep-Sulcus-the-Sign

Aortic-the-Dissection

Birads-the-Score
The Risk-Meter. Tells the surgeon exactly how worried they need to be about a Lump-Max.

Spiculated-the-Shadow
The Malignant-Signature. The distinct radiographic look of cancer Reaching-Out to invade.

Micro-Calc-the-Dots

Ockham-the-Razor-Edge

Entities should not be multiplied without necessity.
Scientism-the-False-God

RCT-the-Gold-Standard

P-Hacker-the-Cheat

Precision-the-Genetic-Sniper

Pre-Print-the-Speedrunner

Open-the-Access-Knight

Number-Needed-to-Treat (NNT)

Hazard-the-Ratio

Case-Control-the-Flashback

Cohort-the-Follower

Double-Blind-the-Justice

Belmont-the-Protector

Informed-the-Consent-Scroll

IRB-the-Gatekeeper

Declara-the-Helsinki

The ethical Constitution of the World Medical Association.
Big-Data-the-Giant

Confound-the-Distractor

Correlation is not Causation. The nemesis of Logic-the-Razor.
Registra-the-Trial-Tracker

Replicat-the-Validator

Petri-the-Culture-Dish

Western-the-Protein-Blot

Molecular biology. The Hardware-Audit of the cell.
Knock-Out-the-Deletion

Functional genomics. If the wrestler Crashes, we know the gene's Power-Level.
Grant-the-Fuel-Source

IP-the-Patent-Guard

Peer-the-Reviewer-No-2

Archie Appendicitis
The Pecalith Jam. Archie starts with a belly-button ache and ends with a sharp, right-sided stab.
Obstruction of the lumen leads to intraluminal pressure spikes, ischemia, and eventually a Blowout (Perforation).
Peritonitis Pete
The Chemical Riot. Pete floods the peritoneal space with bile, stool, or blood, turning the ring into a toxic swamp.
Inflammation of the serous membrane causes a massive shift of fluid, leading to hypovolemic shock if not drained.
Obstruction Otis
The Traffic Jam. Otis stops the flow. Everything upstream swells; everything downstream is The Ghost Town.
Obstruction is most often caused by Adhesions (scar tissue). Otis leads to severe Vomitus and distension.
Volvulus Val
The Strangler. Val twists the bowel around its own blood supply (Mesentery), cutting off oxygen instantly.
This is a vascular emergency. If Val isn't Untwisted, the segment turns gangrenous in hours.
Chole-Cathy
The Gallbladder Squeeze. Cathy tries to push a stone through a tiny pipe after a fatty meal.
Cholecystitis occurs when a stone blocks the Cystic Duct, causing the Gallbladder Wall to swell and inflame.
Jaundice Jack
The Bile Backup. The pipeline is blocked by a stone or Pancreas-monster.
Conjugated bilirubin can't reach the gut, so it leaks into the blood and out through the skin and eyes.
Pancreas-Phil
The Auto-Digest. Phil gets angry and releases his enzymes inside himself, cooking his own tissue.
Often triggered by Gallstones or Alcohol. Phil can trigger a deadly Cytokine Tsunami (SIRS).
Cholangitis-Chuck
The Septic Storm. Chuck is the ultimate biliary emergency. Infection is trapped under pressure in the bile ducts.
Put under pressure (Charcot's Triad +). He needs urgent decompression (ERCP).
Inguinal-Izzy
The Escape Artist. Izzy finds a weak spot in the abdominal wall and shoves the bowel through it.
Indirect Izzy follows the Spermatic Cord; Direct Izzy just punches straight through the Hesselbach Floor.
Strangulated-Stan
The Death Grip. The hole is too tight to let blood can't get in, and the trapped bowel starts to die.
A Reducible hernia is a nuisance; a Strangulated Stan is a surgical race against the clock.
Femoral-Fiona
The High-Risk Escape. Fiona uses a tiny, tight canal. She is highly prone to rapid Strangulation.
The Femoral Canal is rigid and narrow. Fiona doesn't play the mechanical marvel—Fiona traps the bowel almost immediately.
Incisional-Ina
The Scar-Breaker. Ina passes through the shock of a previous cut, where the Fascia-Armor never rebuilt.
Failure of primary healing. Ina is the reason surgeons choose over Future Tension.
Triple-A-Arthur
The Silent Bomb. Arthur waits. He grows slowly and painlessly until he suddenly Pops.
Weakening of the tunica media. If Arthur ruptures, the Scrimmage is done without instant OR access.
Mesenteric-Mitch
The Gut Stroke. Mitch cuts off blood to the intestines. The patient screams, but the belly feels soft.
Embolism in the SMA. Without blood, the bowel lining dies, leading to massive bacterial invasion.
Varicose-Vince
The Backflow. Vince occurs when the valves in the legs fail, allowing venous blood to pool in the ankles.
Chronic venous hypertension leads to severe skin changes and Ulcer Formation (Lipodermatosclerosis).
Claudication-Claude
The Walking Stop. Claude starves the muscles of oxygen, making the calves burn after just 500 meters.
Atherosclerosis of the Iliac/Femoral arteries. Claude is a blaring warning siren of Global Vascular War.
Peptic-Percy
The Acid Burn. Percy eats through the stomach lining. The Acid Militia fires at the Gastroduodenal Artery.
Imbalance between gastric acid and mucosal protection. Perforation leads to lethal Free Air under the diaphragm.
Mallory-Weiss Mel
The Retch-Rip. Mel occurs when violent vomiting tears the delicate junction between esophagus and stomach.
A longitudinal mucosal tear. Mel usually stops bleeding on his own, but the hematemesis is terrifying.
Boerhaave-Bob
The Full-Thickness Blowout. Bob is the Final Level of Mel. The esophagus actually pops entirely open.
Transmural rupture leads to Mediastinitis, affecting the heart and lungs. A 911 absolute emergency.
Achalasia-Ace
The Food Trap. Ace keeps the Bottom Door of the esophagus locked shut. Food sits, stacks up, and rots.
Loss of the Myenteric Plexus. Ace needs a surgical Heller Myotomy to forcefully kick the door down.
Divertic-Dan
The Left-Sided Appendicitis. Dan occurs when tiny structural pouches in the colon get clogged and infected.
Diverticulosis is simply having the pouches; Diverticulitis is when Dan starts the inflammatory riot.
Poly-Pete
The Silent Grower. Pete isn't cancer yet, but he's Applying for the Job.
Villous adenomas carry the highest risk. Snipping Pete out during a colonoscopy stops this war before it begins.
Hemorrhoid-Harry
The Pressure Leak. Harry occurs when the venous cushions in the Basement (Anus) swell and prolapse out.
Heavy straining increases intra-abdominal pressure, forcing Harry violently out of his hiding spot.
Fissure-Fred
The Knife-Cut. Fred is a small tear in the lining that refuses to heal because the Sphincter-Muscle is spasming.
High sphincter tone causes localized ischemia. Nitro-cream or Botox can force the muscle to relax and let Fred heal.
Thyroid-Theo
The Metabolic Overdrive. Theo controls the match speed. If he goes hyper, the heart races and heat rises.
Cold nodules are more likely to be malignant. Theo's biggest surgery risk is severing the Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve.
Para-Thyroid Pat
The Bone-Breaker. Pat violently steals calcium from the bones and dumps it into the blood and kidneys.
Usually a single Adenoma (Pat's Hideout). Surgery to evict Pat fixes the classic Stones, Bones, Groans, Moans.
Adrenal-Addie
The Adrenaline Surge. Addie creates sudden, massive spikes in blood pressure and heart rate.
Rule of 10%: 10% bilateral, 10% malignant, 10% extra-adrenal. Always Alpha-block before you Beta-block!
Insulin-Ian
The Crash. Ian releases too much insulin, causing massive hypoglycemia and making the patient faint in the ring.
An islet cell tumor of the pancreas. Ian is incredibly rare but acts as a highly dangerous metabolic assassin.
Scalpel-Stan
The Access Point. Stan achieves the very first goal of any surgical encounter: Exposure.
Stan must collaborate with Yellow Langer's Lines to ensure the final scar heals like a zipper instead of a scream.
Bovie-Bill
The Duke & Steak. Bill uses high-frequency sparks to cut tissues and literally Fry Bleeding vessels shut.
Bill absolutely requires a Grounding Pad (Return Electrode) or the patient receives a severe accidental Burns.
Laparo-Leo
The Keyhole View. Leo uses a camera and long chopstick-arms to conduct the entire fight through a tiny hole.
Decreases pain and hospital time. Beware of the Phrenic-Phantom (referred shoulder pain from trapped CO2 gas).
Suture-Sam
The Structural Knot. Sam securely holds the Fascia-Armor together until the body can build its own strength.
Tensile Strength is the absolute law. Sam is the sole reason the Belly-Burst (Dehiscence) doesn't happen.
Triage-Tim
The Life-Sorter. Tim acts as the gatekeeper, deciding who gets the Blade-Brigade first and who has to wait.
In a mass-casualty rampage, you don't save everyone; you ruthlessly optimize to save the most people possible.
FAST-Fiona
The Fluid-Finder. Fiona searches for hidden, pooling blood in Morison's Pouch or around the heart.
If Fiona is positive internally—they bypass the ER and go straight to the OR.
Chest-Tube-Chester
The Lung-Reinflater. Chester aggressively drains air to let the crushed lungs breathe again.
The tube MUST stay above the rib margin to avoid lacerating the Neurovascular Bundle running along the rib.
GCS-Gabe
The Consciousness Meter. Gabe instantly tells the trauma surgeon exactly how hard the brain was hit.
GCS of 8, Intubate! If Gabe calculates the score is low, the patient's airway is no longer safe.
Malignant-Max
The Invasive Lump. Max hides in the upper-outer quadrant and slowly spreads his tendrils to the Axillary Node.
Targeted therapy (Tamoxifen) or Wide Local Excision (Lumpectomy) are Max's surgical kryptonite.
Sentinel-Sid
The First Sentry. Sid is the very first lymph node that Max drains to. If Sid is clear, the army is safe.
Performing a Sentinel Node Biopsy strictly prevents the enormous Lymphedema cost by sparing unnecessary surgery.
Melanoma-Mel
The Deep Dive. Mel starts superficially as a dark spot but engages and plunges through the skin layers.
Depth is everything. A low depth is the clinical line in the sand that mandates significantly wider surgical margins.
Burn-Ben
The Fluid-Leech. Ben destroys the skin-barrier, letting the body's plasma evaporate or hemorrhage instantly.
The Parkland Formula is Ben's specific counter-spell. (Massive volume IV resuscitation is the only key to survive.)
Dehiscence-Dan
The Wound-Split. Dan occurs when Suture-Sam's knot fails and the carefully constructed Belly-Armor tears open.
If the deep Fascia falls and the guts physically fall out, it escalates to Evisceration—live—an absolute surgical nightmare.
Atelectasis-Al
The Shallow Breath. Al closes the tiny Alveolar Balloons because the patient is in too much pain to breathe deeply.
The Incentive Spirometer is the physical counter-spell. You have to force Al to expand and breathe!
DVT-Doris
The Leg-Jam. Doris stops the blood in the calf. If she dislodges and moves to the Lungs, she becomes the deadly PE-Phantom.
Prophylactic Lovenox injections and early walking/ambulation are Doris's sworn enemies.
Post-Op-Paul
The Sleepy Gut. Paul happens when the bowels are handling too roughly during surgery and decide to Go on strike.
Paul is usually temporary. Surprisingly, Chewing Gum and early walking trick the nervous system into waking him up.
Fever-Fiona
The Temperature Spike. Fiona tells the surgeon exactly where the hidden infection is located based on post-op timing. Day 1 = Wind (Lungs). Day 3 = Water (UTI). Day 5 = Wound. Day 7 = Walking (DVT).
Day-by-day fever mapping makes every post-op temperature spike a diagnostic performance — immediately actionable.
Sepsis-Sam
The Total-Body Riot. Sam turns a minor local wound into a global vascular collapse. BP bottoms out; organs fail.
Massive vasodilation. Sepsis-Sam desperately needs 30ml/kg of Crystalloid Juice and immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
Hemorrhage-Hank
The Tank-Drain. Hank is the silent killer. Blood is rapidly leaving the system, and the patient is getting dangerously sleepy.
Class I to IV hemorrhagic shock. By Class III, crystalloids aren't enough—you need Liquid Gold (Blood transfusions).
Anesthesia-Annie
The Metabolic Inferno. A rare, lethal reaction to anesthetic gas that turns the patient's body into an uncontrollable oven.
Defect in the Ryanodine receptor. The specialized drug Dantrolene— is the absolute only weapon that can stop Annie.
Consent-Clerk
The Legal Shield. Ensures the patient actively knows exactly what Anatomical trespassing is about to legally occur.
Emergency-implied consent only exists when the patient is completely unconscious, dying, and unable to speak for themselves.
Scrub-Siren
The Germ-Wall. The Siren rigidly ensures no Microbe-Monsters hitch a ride into the sterile Surgical Scrimmage.
Blue is Sterile. In the operating theatre, anything that isn't draped in sterile blue is treated as a lethal threat.
Pathology-Pack
The Final Verdict. They dictate via microscope if the Cancer-Monster is fully gone, or if the surgeon needs to cut wider.
Frozen sections give an intraoperative answer in minutes; permanent Formalin sections take days to process.
Recovery-Ranger
The Wake-Up Call. The Ranger guards and monitors the patient as their brain slowly reboots post-battle.
Airway, Pain, and Pulse are the three deadly enemies that the Ranger must fight in the Post-Anesthesia Care Unit.
The Boss
The Master-Trespasser. He oversees the Scrimmage, ensuring no one blindly cuts without understanding the Lore.
Is the patient stable? Is the anatomy clear? Why are you still holding the Bovie when you should be tying? Stay fluffy!

Why-Wait-Wolf

Zen-Panda-Prime

Wait-and-See-Owl

Sunset-Swan

Achieves 100% True Stealth Mode.
The ancient magic Big Tech banned. The only absolute guarantee that a device isn't recording your location and conversations.
Graphene OS

A privacy-respecting operating system. Security hardening measures built into a fortress they cannot penetrate.

The Unwanted Apps

Tactical Flight Mode

Wins the game. Reclaims human freedom.
You must withdraw from the network of total surveillance while you still can. The seductive convenience of the observation economy has a high price: Freedom.

Moves the sun by treating it like a ball of poop. It's a living.

Queen of Magic. Conned the sun god for his password. Loyal to a fault.
Set (The Heel)

Chaos Aardvark. Killed his brother over a chair shot. We all hate him; he loves it.
Horus (The Golden Boy)
Vengeance Strike: Double damage against "Heel" cards.
The Falcon Heir. Fed his uncle a salad with a "secret ingredient." Issues.
Anubis (The Bouncer)

God of Mummification. If your heart is heavy, you don't get into the club.

Cosmic Order. The feather that ruins your afterlife. No cheating allowed.
Ammit (The Disposal Unit)

The Devourer. Only eats the hearts of sinners. Zero calorie diet.
Thoth (The Scorekeeper)
Wiki-Edit: Change the text of one card's Lore for the turn.
Inventor of writing. Knows the cheat codes. Gambled with the moon and won.
Sekhmet (The Drunk Tank)
Rage Virus: Attack every card on the table, including your own.
The Eye of Ra. Tried to delete humanity. Stopped only by a keg of red beer.
Bastet (The House Cat)
Claws & Cuddles: Heal one card or scratch one enemy.
Goddess of perfume and ointment. Sekhmet on a 'good' day. Don't touch the belly.
Montu (The Raging Bull)
Trample: Ignore defense stats.
The War God. Represents the Pharaoh's desire to hit things very hard.
Shezmu (The Presser)
The Squeeze: Convert defeated cards into "Perfume" tokens.
God of wine and slaughter. Crushes skulls like grapes. A true artisan.
Sobek (The Teeth)
Ambush Drag: Pull an opponent's card into the "River" zone (discard).
Lord of Semen. Loves robbery. Eats tourists. A complex guy.
Tawaret (The Heavy Hitter)

Goddess of childbirth. Hippos kill more people than crocs. Do the math.
Khnum (The Potter)

Moulds babies out of river mud. The original 3D printer.
Hapi (The Flood)

Intersex deity of the inundation. Brings the silt, brings the life, brings the wet socks.
Bes (The Mascot)

Protector of households. Scares demons by being ugly and loud. A true hero.
Medjed (The Sheet)

The Smiter. He shoots with his eye. He is unseen. He is a meme.

Chief of the Baboons. Eats entrails. His virility is the mast of the underworld ferry. Gross.
Serket (The Stinger)

She who tightens the throat. Doctors love her. Scorpions are just misunderstood land-lobsters.

Millions of years, zero maintenance. Defense against the dark snake.
The Scales of Justice (The Ref's Tool)

Shepherd the people, beat the grain. The duality of management.
The Eye of Ra (Heat Ray)

Remote-controlled drone strike of the ancient world.
Seshat (The Architect)
Blueprint: Look at the top 3 cards of the deck.

Ptah (The Creator)

Thought the world into existence. The ultimate introvert creation myth.

Was a mortal, built a pyramid, got promoted to God. The corporate ladder works.

The World Encircler. Ra's umbilical cord gone wrong. Pray AGAINST him.

Desert dweller. A visual non-sequitur designed to scare tourists.

Swarm: 7 small attacks instead of 1 big one.
Isis's bodyguards. They stung a rich lady's son because she was rude. Class warfare.
The Red Cloud (Storm Front)
Blindness: All accuracy stats reduced to zero.
The angry breath of Set. Red is the color of bad things in the desert.
Nekhbet (South)
White Crown: +5 Defense if played with Wadjet.
Patron of Upper Egypt. Vultures are good mothers. It's a cultural thing.

Red Crown: +5 Attack if played with Nekhbet.
Patron of Lower Egypt. Fire-spitting snake. Put her on your forehead for protection.
Shai (Destiny)

The concept of Fate. You can't fight the booking committee.
Renenutet (The Nurse)
Harvest Gold: Gain resources each turn.
Goddess of the harvest and nursing. Snakes and milk. Don't think about it too hard.
The Duat (Backstage Area)
Graveyard cards can attack from here.
The Underworld. Dangerous, full of snakes, and you have to pass 12 gates to leave.
Heliopolis (The Main Stage)
Solar gods get +2 Stats.
City of the Sun. Where the Ennead holds their board meetings.

First card played gets "High Ground" advantage.
The first solid ground. Everything starts here. King of the Hill rules apply.

Set ate salad with Horus's... dressing. A gold disk appeared on his head. Awkward.

She thought it was blood. It was dyed beer. The original hangover.

Isis found 13 pieces of Osiris. The fish ate the 14th. Had to make a gold replacement.

Nut couldn't give birth in the 360 day year. Thoth won 5 extra days gambling. Loophole!
Nietzsche
Hammer of Transvaluation. Breaks stable fields to force new values.
Alignment: Poetic-Explosive.
Plato
Effect: Gives quest 'Leave the Cave'. Wants you to find Truth so he can rule.
Quest giver or manipulator? He wrote the simulation!

Heavy emotional baggage inside. Send it already!

No North, only vibes. Lost but making good time!

Break the fourth wall. Home sweet home?
Lvl 1: The Foreclosed
You read the eviction notice. You feel a small fire start in your chest.
The crown takes the field. The field remembers.
Lvl 2: The Pitchfork-Sworn
You take what was once a farming tool and use it for something else.
Every revolt starts with a tool that was always a weapon.
Lvl 3: Of the Borrowed Torch
You set fire to what they built on your field.
They paved a holiness over and called it progress.
Lvl 4: The Rebel Rouser
You cause a revolt. Chant a rebel rant; move the Quest Die ±2.
A man with a field becomes a man with a mob, and neither one was the goal.
Lvl 1: The Cheap Blade
You take the next contract. You don't read the small print.
A blade for hire is honest in a way that a blade for principle is not.
Lvl 2: The Reputation
You raise your rates. The contracts come faster.
A reputation pays better than a sword and shows up faster.
Lvl 3: Of the Four Contracts
You take contracts from all four spheres at once. Nobody knows.
Loyalty is for the man who can afford it.
Lvl 4: The Last Talker
You read the contract. The contract is the only thing that talks back.
To win every job is to lose every name that called you something else.
Lvl 1: The First Bellows
You build the small device. The small device works.
A first device that works is a promise the workshop has not yet broken.
Lvl 2: The Second Bellows
You build a bigger device. The bigger device explodes.
Scale is the workshop's enemy and its only honest tutor.
Lvl 3: Of the Self-Explaining Engine
You build the device that explains itself.
A machine that explains itself by exploding has explained more than most teachers.
Lvl 4: The Explosion Herself
You are the explosion. The party loves you and fears you.
The body that survived its own invention has no use for warnings anymore.
Lvl 1: The Tracker
You see the trail others walked past.
A path is a story. The hunter is its first reader.

You wait. The shot finds itself.
Patience is a kind of speed nobody has yet measured.
Lvl 3: The Tracker of People
You track the one who asked not to be tracked.
A trail you find is a question. The asking is sometimes the whole answer.
Lvl 4: The One Who Shot the Deer
You find what you hunted. You find what you hunted for.
A perfect shot is a question with no place left to land.

You win the bar-fight. They put your name on a chalkboard.
Strength remembered loud is strength remembered last.
Lvl 2: The Tournament Winner
You win the tournament. The tournament was rumored to be fixed.
A win is a win until someone counts the coins.
Lvl 3: Of the Useful Rumor
You let the rumor stand. The rumor wins fights for you.
A name that does its own work has stopped belonging to you.
Lvl 4: The Second Weapon
You carry the rumor. You let it cut.
A reputation outlives its body. Sometimes too long.
Lvl 1: The Young Rage
You charge first. You hit hardest. You don't think yet.
Rage is the dwarf's first prayer and his last excuse.
Lvl 2: The Decorated Veteran
You take the pace. They name a battle after you.
The medal is heavier than the comrade it replaced.
Lvl 3: Of the Unstopping Hammer
You cannot put the hammer down. The hammer asks.
The peace between the wars is the harder war.
Lvl 4: The Wrong Joke
You apologize. You swing again next time.
A joke about a beard is the cheapest way to die in this country.
Lvl 1: The Herbalist
You make the salve. The salve works.
A small good is the medicine that does not need a bigger story.
Lvl 2: The Salve-Mistress
You stitch what others left bleeding.
A healer's hands learn before her heart catches up.
Lvl 3: Of the Mercy That Spreads
You heal the wounded monster. The party will not understand.
Mercy that asks no questions answers more questions than it asks.
Lvl 4: The Resurrectionist
You resurrect any card from the discard pile.
To save everyone is to save no one in the order they hoped.
Lvl 1: The Apprentice of Frames
You make the small illusion. The small illusion holds.
The first trick is recognising that everything is a trick.
Lvl 2: The Stagecrafter
You bend what the room agrees to see.
A stage is a contract. Most contracts are stages.
Lvl 3: Of the Recognised Match
You see the match. The match has been fixed since before the start.
A continent that fits inside a single phrase has been written by someone with terms.
Lvl 4: The Card-Replacer
You replace any card with any card from any deck.
The trick was never the trick. The deck was the trick.
Lvl 1: The Corpse-Looter
You take what others called 'body' and call it 'parts'.
A scholar's hands have not yet learned which questions are answered better unasked.
Lvl 2: The First Homunculus
You build the small one. The small one looks back.
Every parent says hello before realising what they have done.
Lvl 3: Of the Walking Letter
You build the one who can carry the letter back.
A creation that writes is a creation that has noticed you.
Lvl 4: The Father of the Friendly Army
You command the army. The army was the only company that stayed.
A father who built his children has only the hello he wrote into them.
Lvl 1: The Keynote Barbie
You get the room laughing before the trouble walks in.
A first song is a friend the room has not yet betrayed.
Lvl 2: The Festival Circuit
You sing the song everyone already knows. They sing it back.
A song that catches has caught more than the singer.
Lvl 3: Of the Quiet Suspicion
You hear the song you wrote and recognise it from somewhere else.
A lyric that flatters power was written by someone power flattered first.
Lvl 4: The Lore-Keeper
You sing the song. You know what it is doing.
A continent is what its songs let it remember about itself.

You take the oath. You believe every word.

You lead the charge. The institution leads with you.

Lvl 3: Of the Quiet Doubt

A doubt that does not yet have a name has already started its work.
