You command the Guard. The Guard is loyal to the throne. The throne changes occupants.
A polished oath outlives the cause and recruits its own believers.

A reform begun in solitude is a reform that already wants company.

You print the pamphlet. The pamphlet circulates.
A heresy in print is a heresy that has hired its own messengers.
Lvl 3: Of the Krooked Krypt
You replace the dragon's coin with your own promise.
A new currency is an old faith that found new believers to charge.

You hold the new gold. Goldspleen is now only shiny.

Lvl 3: King Kayfabian VIII, the Replaced

A campaign is the breaking. The module was the misunderstanding.

You set the table. The players arrive. You do not pretend.
Stay fluffy.

The Manufactured Emergency
Frames an existing condition as immediate and universal to justify a response not otherwise available.
The condition may predate the framing; the urgency is introduced when the response requires it.
The Invisible Threat
Sustains alertness toward dangers whose evidence cannot be independently examined.
Vigilance is maintained for threats described as classified, structural, or too complex to summarize for a general audience.
The Expanding Crisis
Extends emergency framing into adjacent domains as each measure reveals new requirements.
The original threat remains formally unresolved while response infrastructure enters areas it never initially addressed.
The Permanent Exception
Converts a temporary emergency designation into stable infrastructure once adaptation removes the pressure to remove it.
The emergency expires; the systems built under it are now the standard and are no longer described as temporary.
The Directed Outrage
Channels existing frustration toward a specific named target at a specific moment.
Diffuse dissatisfaction acquires an address; the structural conditions producing it do not.
The Scapegoat Engine
Concentrates distributed accountability onto a single identifiable figure.
A name is provided; the structural conditions that produced the outcome are not named in the same sentence.
The Moral Panic Loop
Converts directed anger into a self-sustaining cycle that requires no further external input.
Each event in the cycle increases receptivity to the next; the cycle no longer needs curating.
The Polarization Machine
Produces a population sorted into opposed groups whose primary energy flows toward each other rather than outward.
Attention concentrates on the division; the mechanism that produced it operates outside the frame.
The Information Flood
Saturates available processing capacity through volume, making navigation more expensive than the decision it informs.
Navigation requires more time than is available; most content goes unread without being suppressed.
The Contradiction Field
Places credentialed opposing voices on each contested question until no stable factual baseline holds.
For each expert position, a peer-reviewed counter-position is available at identical distribution.
The Expert Fragmentation
Distributes authority across subspecialties until no synthesizing voice is structurally available.
The question requires cross-domain assessment; the institution that would coordinate that assessment has not been organized.
The Decision Fatigue Trap
Converts unresolvable information load into passive acceptance of the default already in place.
After sufficient exposure to contradictory authoritative claims, people stop choosing and accept what is already there.
The Safety Net Conversion
Introduces genuine support that gradually becomes the only available path for the need it serves.
The service is real; the dependency it produces is a structural output, not a design flaw.
The Access Gate
Conditions essential access on continued enrollment, making exit structurally expensive.
Leaving the system means losing access that was built only through being inside it.
The Subscription State
Converts one-time transactions into recurring relationships requiring active effort to exit.
The service is unchanged; the delivery model ensures return and places exit responsibility on the user.
The Conditional Freedom
Expands available choices within the system while the practical infrastructure for choices outside it contracts.
Freedom of movement within the system increases as the conditions for movement outside it quietly contract.
The Group Lock
Ties self-concept to membership until belonging becomes a structural rather than voluntary condition.
The group provides genuine benefits; those benefits become reasons not to evaluate the group on its own terms.
The Loyalty Test
Introduces visible periodic tests that sort members from non-members without stating the evaluation criteria.
The content of the test matters less than the visible act of passing it.
The Belief Badge
Converts private doubt into required public display of certainty as the currency of membership.
Public performance of belief becomes required; private disagreement is present but quiet.
The Exit Cost
Accumulates relationships, infrastructure, and identity inside the group until leaving means losing several things that cannot be recovered simultaneously.
The exit cost was not imposed as a penalty. It accrued through ordinary participation.
The Soft Mandate
Establishes a preferred behavior through expectation rather than requirement.
The behavior is formally optional; consequences for non-compliance distribute informally and consistently.
The Social Proof Cascade
Uses observed compliance as the primary evidence that compliance is correct.
The behavior spreads because it is visible; the reasoning behind it is rarely articulated.
The Incentive Nudge
Arranges the choice architecture so the preferred option requires measurably less friction than alternatives.
The choice is genuinely available; the costs of choosing against the design accumulate in small unannounced increments.
The Silent Penalty
Produces consistent behavioral alignment through distributed informal costs that are never announced.
No mandate was issued. No penalty was declared. The behavior is consistent.
The Frame Selection
Determines which context a fact arrives with before the fact can be examined independently.
The same event produces different public understanding depending on the surrounding material — which is selected.
The Narrative Sync
Aligns multiple institutional voices around a single interpretation in the same window of time.
The alignment is described as independent consensus; its timing is documented and rarely explained.
The Repetition Loop
Converts a claim into familiarity through repetition, and familiarity into assumed truth.
The claim does not become verified; it becomes recognizable — which produces a similar effect.
The Memory Hole
Allows contradicting information to become inaccessible without active removal.
The prior account was not deleted; the new account was placed higher, in larger type, in more locations, for longer.
The Gradual Shift
Introduces change at a rate calibrated to fall below the threshold that reliably triggers active resistance.
Each step is unremarkable; the cumulative distance becomes significant only when measured from the original position.
The New Baseline
Converts an exceptional condition into the standard through sustained duration and adaptation.
After sufficient time, the exceptional condition is no longer described as exceptional.
The Retroactive Justification
Produces explanations that position the current state as the natural or inevitable outcome.
The trajectory is legible only toward the current position; alternative paths are no longer visible from here.
The "Always Like This" Effect
Converts sufficient duration into apparent permanence, and apparent permanence into natural fact.
Those who arrived after the shift describe the current state as normal. Those who arrived before it are fewer.
The Price Shock
Introduces a sudden cost increase that disrupts established behavior before alternatives can be organized.
The shock produces rapid adaptation; the adapted state accepts the new cost structure as the baseline.
The Scarcity Lever
Reduces — or appears to reduce — the supply of an essential good to redirect behavior at scale.
Scarcity may be real or managed; the behavioral response is structurally identical in either case.
The Debt Harness
Converts future income into present compliance through obligation structures accepted under prior conditions.
The harness is taken on voluntarily at a specific moment; the future it governs was not fully legible at that moment.
The Inflation Drift
Reduces the real value of resources incrementally while the nominal value remains constant.
The number is the same. The quantity it purchases is smaller. The adjustment is continuous, distributed, and unremarkable.
The Convenience Trap
Makes the preferred option sufficiently easier than alternatives until alternatives become effectively unavailable over time.
The alternative remained technically accessible; the friction required to reach it accumulated into practical impossibility.
The Automation Shield
Replaces human decision points with automated processes that cannot be questioned on the same terms as human decisions.
Responsibility for the outcome follows the system's design rather than the system's output.
The Black Box Decision
Produces consequential outcomes through processes whose criteria are inaccessible to those they affect.
The decision stands; the criteria are proprietary; an appeal is available at significant time and cost.
The Interface Constraint
Shapes available action through design until the design becomes the perceived space of possibility.
Users describe their choices as free; the choices listed were those that remained after the design was finalized.
The Expert Seal
Attaches institutional credentialing to a position, elevating its authority above independent examination.
The seal confirms domain expertise; it also confirms institutional alignment with the body that issued it.
The Institutional Echo
Circulates an aligned position through multiple institutional channels until simultaneous publication registers as independent consensus.
The positions arrived at similar conclusions within the same period; any coordination is not documented.
The Regulatory Capture
Converts oversight institutions into endorsement institutions through sustained personnel and incentive alignment.
The regulator was designed to monitor the industry; over a sufficient period, the industry shaped the regulator.
The Oversight Theater
Maintains the visible form of accountability while the functional capacity for it is structurally unavailable.
The committee convenes; the questions are asked; the record is complete; the practice continues.
The Discredit Move
Redirects attention from a position's content to the credibility of its source.
The argument is not answered; the arguer's qualifications, history, or associations are examined instead.
The Isolation Effect
Removes the visible social infrastructure around a position until it appears to stand alone.
Others who hold the position become quiet; it appears fringe when it describes something widely experienced.
The Deplatform Funnel
Routes a position from high-distribution channels to low-visibility ones without formal suppression.
The position continues; it reaches a fraction of the prior audience; it no longer affects consensus-forming conversations.
The Legal Drag
Converts the cost of contesting suppression into a structural disincentive for future challenges.
The case resolves; it requires years and resources beyond most challengers; the effect on future challenges is structural.
The Self-Policing Loop
Converts external behavioral requirements into internal monitoring, removing the need for visible enforcement.
The behavior is maintained without surveillance because the person no longer registers its absence.
The Identity Merge
Binds behavioral compliance with self-concept until non-compliance requires personal revision.
The behavior is no longer performed for the institution; it is performed for who the participant understands themselves to be.
The Learned Helplessness
Converts a history of failed attempts to affect outcomes into a stable belief that outcomes cannot be affected.
The belief was rational given the prior evidence; it persists after the evidence changes.
The Voluntary Compliance
Produces consistent alignment without enforcement because the system's requirements have been adopted as personal values.
At this stage, no enforcement is required. The participants carry it for free.
The Pattern Denial
Frames the identification of a recurring structure as evidence of interpretive error rather than pattern recognition.
Naming the structure is described as projection; the structure continues while the naming is contested.
The Coincidence Stack
Maintains that repeated outcomes in the same direction are each individually and separately explicable.
Every instance has a different explanation; the explanation for the pattern is that there is no pattern.
The Complexity Shield
Uses the genuine complexity of systems to make pattern description appear naïve or incomplete.
The system is genuinely complex; what it consistently produces is not.
The Move Itself
At sufficient scale of internalization, the pattern no longer needs to be performed — it becomes the ambient condition.
The move is complete when it stops being a move and becomes the environment.

Disguise. You cannot be targeted by attacks this turn.

The Version
Defines the thing with an account of the event.
The account becomes the thing — repeatedly cited until it seems to have authority.
Retcon
Rewrites the past from the present — so the story took it for granted.
The revision was accepted so smoothly that nobody remembered it as a revision.
Memory Drift
Dramatically alters the story over time — sometimes to protect others.
Everyone slightly remembers it differently, and somehow all those versions point to the same core story-line.
What Happened?
Transforms speech by context instead of any new information.
The phrase lands differently depending on who says it and when. The question contains the verdict.
Blödsinn!
Says 'Ridiculous!' enough times until everyone's agreement is built around avoiding the label.
The label 'Ridiculous' becomes the rule. Nobody wrote it down. Nobody needs to.
Frame Control
Shapes what is performable — and what seems out of bounds.
Was classified as a misunderstanding. The category was gone — the case was gone.
Consensus
Locks in a specific version of events without anyone needing to agree to it.
Agreement reached critical mass. Nobody voted. The version was simply — there.
The Witness
Someone who watches, attends, and records — without participating or speaking.
Presence without participation changes what gets said.
The Outlier
Names the group by pointing to what falls outside the group — making the story hold.
Someone always plays the outlier. Nobody asks why they always play that role.
Status Leak
Communicates hierarchy even when suppressed — especially through error.
When something went wrong, the group looked to the same animal. Nobody had appointed them.
Invisible Agreement
Between two groups that was never stated — and now governs their interaction.
Someone broke the rule everyone had. No-one knew there was one.
Polite Fiction
Maintains group function by allowing everyone to pretend something isn't happening.
A polite fiction that has gone on long enough often gets mistaken for policy.
The Audience
Determines what is performed — and performance changes decisions — even if audience is silent.
Who's in the room is never accidental.
Side Conversation
Runs the first version of decisions before the meeting begins.
The real decision happened somewhere else. The meeting was the performance of agreeing.
The Attending
Changes institutional throughput through the performance of arrival.
Being there was the move. Everything else followed from the presence.
Good Neighbor
Performs goodwill to prevent group forming against it.
Nobody could say exactly what the Good Neighbor had done. They knew it had worked.
The Quest
Reorganizes collective identity around a problem.
Something is at stake — so the group holds.
The Stage
How a scene was played in a different context — context not set in advance.
The same move lands completely differently depending on what stage it's played on.
Yes, and
Accepts and extends every offer — by accepting everything, creates a frame that cannot be said no to.
Someone introduced Yes, And — treating every rule as a story choice. Somehow it worked.
Escalation
Confirms and amplifies the previous scene — the last move is now the baseline.
Each escalation made the previous level feel normal. Nobody noticed when the ceiling became the floor.
Character Switch
Changes identity mid-scene — and the story absorbs the new one faster than anyone shifts.
A player swapped cards without warning. The story accommodated the new character more easily than expected.
No, but
Refuses without exiting — turns refusal into a scene, not an escape.
The player said No. The Quest Die fell. The scene went deeper than any you had gone.
Reset
Returns to before the current tension — and carries the tension forward as subtext.
A scene collapsed. The group backed up two turns. The collapse was still there. Everyone felt it.
The Finale
Declares the ending — and makes everything before it retroactively about what the ending needs.
The Quest Die fell. The player paused. What they said made the previous hour cohere. It wasn't planned.
Tryhard Energy
Makes visible effort that should be invisible — and the effort is all anyone sees.
A player performed their card so hard the card disappeared. What remained was the performance. Nothing landed.
Joke Without Stake
Deploys humor with no cost — and removes the table's ability to take anything seriously afterwards.
The table laughed. Nobody noticed what the Quest Die hadn't moved in two rounds.
Dead Scene
Extends a moment past its function — draining the energy of everything that follows.
Everyone was waiting for someone else to move the story. The Quest Die stayed at 3 for four turns.
Forced Ending
Imports a conclusion that wasn't earned — and the table knows it, immediately, without discussion.
It landed like a door closing before the room was finished.
Overexplaining
Unpacks a statement until no-one is willing to respond.
A player unpacked a joke for five minutes. By the end, everyone agreed. No-one had laughed.
Rule Lawyer
Substitutes the rule for the play — and thus the game stops proceeding.
They were right about the rules. They were right about what was legal. They weren't right about the game.
Silence
Announces itself without action — sometimes stronger than anything said.
A player who had been silent for 40 minutes said nothing. The others played as though they had.
Meta Collapse
Makes the game collapse by discussing the game — sometimes accidentally.
A player discovered they were losing badly — started asking how people were deciding to play. The game stopped. No-one knew why.
Ambivalence
Holds two positions — and forces everyone else to commit to one while you remain uncommitted.
Ambivalence holds more — and holds longer — than most strategies. The trick is not choosing too early.
Paradox Engine
Holds two contradictions simultaneously — and makes both more true for being held together.
The more the group tried to resolve it, the more necessary the paradox became.
Double Bind
Creates a situation where any move confirms the frame.
Every option they tried proved the premise. They kept trying options.
Signal vs Noise
Knows the most important thing being said is almost never what's being said most loudly.
The room was focused on the argument. The decision had been made in the first sentence.
Meaning as Performance
Interprets cooperation through others' exposed actions — the interpretation is the action.
The meaning wasn't in what was said. It was in what happened when someone acted as if they meant it.
Trust Loop
Requires another player to change what you just said — the story becomes its own corrections.
Each correction made the original statement more true than it was before being corrected.
Fiction That Works
Story points to something larger than itself — and that larger thing becomes real through the pointing.
The fiction was never true. But it was truer than the facts it replaced.
The Gap
Leaves a real local story for a later arrival — the gap is the invitation.
The space left in the story was more interesting than the story. Someone arrived later and stepped into it.
King Kayfabian
Gives the system a face when accountability is required — and removes it when it isn't.
A player drew King Kayfabian and suddenly every previous card made structural sense. The game was always this game.
The System
Operates without malice and without exception — consistency is what makes it difficult to address.
THE SYSTEM made a decision. Nobody could object. The decision was correct by the rules that produced it.
The Patient
Makes the abstract concrete — the moment they enter, every systemic discussion becomes personal.
The Patient entered the story. Three cards that had seemed theoretical immediately had consequences.
The Intern
Asks the question nobody else is supposed to need answered — and exposes the Invisible Agreement at the most productive possible moment.
The Intern drew a card, read it literally, did exactly what it said. It worked. Nobody could explain why.
The Animal
Strips psychology and leaves only behavior — the story becomes cleaner and more threatening.
The Animal didn't explain its choices. The story became more honest and considerably more dangerous.
The Narrator
Names the story — and the named version displaces the one being played.
A player switched to narration mid-scene. The scene became more true and more distant simultaneously.
The Observer
Ratifies through attention — watching confirms that something worth watching is happening.
The Observer was silent for three turns. Then they spoke. It reframed everything before it. Nobody disputed it.
Uncle FrizzleBob
Observes the story from outside it — and the observation changes what the story is.
FrizzleBob entered, said one thing, left. Everything shifted. Everything that was was slightly different.
This Is Enough
Declares sufficiency — and makes the declaration retroactively true for everything that preceded it.
The session ended before the story did. Three players continued the story elsewhere. It finished differently.
Play Again
Uses the first session to change what the second session can mean — repetition is not repetition.
The group replayed. Three cards landed in the same sequence. The story went somewhere entirely new.
You Missed Something
Withholds partial access — and partial access creates more engagement than total access ever could.
A player said there was a card the table hadn't drawn yet that explained everything. Nobody asked what it said. They wanted to find it.
The QR
Moves attention outside the current system while keeping it in a related one.
Someone scanned mid-session. The game followed them home. They played it three days later with different people.
Start Here
Makes every entry point valid — the story that follows is shaped by which door was used.
Someone asked where to start. Another player handed them one card: 'This one.' The session built from there.
The Hub
Connects isolated instances into a network — the network is only as real as the edges that use it.
Someone asked where to find more. The card was already pointing them — they hadn't noticed until now.
Take This with You
Produces an artifact that outlasts the session — the game continues in whatever the player carries next.
The session ended. A player photographed their hand. They didn't explain why. A week later they sent it to someone.
Don't Explain This
Bypasses explanation and reaches the person who already understands — the card selects its audience.
A stranger picked up a card. Read it. Asked one question. Not about the rules. About the thing the card described.
The Necessary Motion
Generates raw survival.
The bend worn into the earth over generations.
The First Division
Sorts the pack by utility.
The bad knee guards the young; the keen eye takes the high branches.
The Shared Burden
Distributes daylight evenly.
The day ended when there was enough.
The Pattern
Detaches repetition from appetite.
The moment "doing" became "duty".
The Not-Working
Creates the concept of laziness.
The small gap between bending out of hunger and bending out of habit.
The Monastery Bell
Slices the sun into eight prayers.
The day has owners, and they are calling.
The Factory Whistle
Transforms prayer into industrial shifts.
Time is now currency; it is spent, not passed.
The Long Day
Consumes all available existence.
Daylight is the only legitimate limit to availability.
The Hour Saved
Reclaims exactly eight hours for "what we will."
A radical claim that some time belongs to the breather.
The Stopwatch
Fractures fluid movement into cold math.
The future belongs to the system; the past belonged to the beast.
The Optimised Body
Quadruples the load bearing capacity of flesh.
The first manual for treating the body as a gear.
The Pin Factory
Multiplies output by a factor of 240.
Making things without knowing how to make a thing.
The Division of Labour
Severs the maker from the whole.
Ten beasts make forty-eight thousand fragments.
The Alienation
Enriches the system by impoverishing the soul.
The worker grows poorer the more wealth they produce.
The Surplus
Extracts the ghost from the machine.
The factory starves if the worker keeps what they make.
The Iron Cage
Forces the calling into inescapable logic.
No one can leave without ceasing to be modern.
The Commodity Labour
Puts life on a shelf with a price tag.
Land, coin, and sweat become goods.
The For-Sale Hour
Trades the part of the self that fills the time.
The person becomes the meat inside the hour.
The Action Office
Liberates the thinker from the typing pool.
An invention designed to free you, destined to cage you.
The Cubicle Fence
Shrinks the horizon to modular plastic.
A revolution mass-produced into a prison.
The Knowledge Worker
Deploys the mind as the means of production.
Cannot be coerced; must be persuaded, motivated, included.
The Memo
Replaces the physical whip with administrative paper.
The illusion of dignity, infinitely measurable.
The Meeting
Replaces the assembly belt with a conference table.
Where time goes to be collectively sacrificed.
The Cascade
Expands work to fill the allotted void.
It takes six weeks because six weeks were given.
The Quarterly
Warps reality into three-month chunks.
The beast shapes itself to please the analyst.
The Goodhart Proxy
Destroys the underlying value of any measurement.
When a measure becomes a target, truth dies.
The Org Chart
Tells a comforting fiction about how power flows.
The real currents are sideways and in the shadows.
The Reorg
Shuffles the deck while the dealer cheats.
A periodic ritual to pretend the river changed course.
The Performance Review
Forces mutual dishonesty once a year.
Most reviews are dishonest in both directions.
The Calibration Curve
Dooms a percentage of the pack before they begin.
The line was drawn before you entered the room.
The Box-Ticker
Verifies the existence of a corporate lie.
Writing the report no one will ever read.
The Duct-Taper
Patches a glitch that should not exist.
Human glue for digital incompetence.
The Taskmaster
Manages the unmanageable for no reason.
Supervising those who already know what to do.
The Flunky
Magnifies the ego of the superior.
Existing solely to make someone else look important.
The Goon
Counters the enemy's identical minion.
The arms race of corporate lawyers and lobbyists.
The Ladder
Translates feudal advancement into cubicles.
The modern firm calls it seniority; the guild called it survival.
The Title
Merges the core self with the corporate role.
When asked who you are, you answer what you do.
The Achievement-Subject
Exploits itself without external pressure.
The push is internal; the push is the air you breathe.
The Burned
Consumes the self from the inside out.
You cannot stop being the one who runs.
The Intolerable Burden
Turns the passage of time into physical agony.
Alienation felt in the bone, not the book.
The Mended Thing
Defeats the hermeneutics of suspicion.
The carburettor answers you in a way the spreadsheet never will.
The Skilled Hand
Remembers what the mind was trained to forget.
The body knows the whole object.
The Craftsman
Cares for the work strictly for its own sake.
A slowness the modern firm cannot tolerate.
The Onboarded Apprentice
Replaces mastery with a slide deck.
We no longer apprentice; we are processed.
The Quiet Quitting
Delivers exactly what is paid for, no more.
The structural refusal to gift the surplus.
The Lying Flat
Denies the system its desires.
Only by doing nothing can you be the measure of all things.
The Side Project
Harbours the work that actually matters.
The sanctuary of the un-alienated soul.
The Fifteen-Hour Illusion
Promises a leisure that never arrives.
The productivity went somewhere, but it didn't come back to you.
The Always-On
Erases the boundary between dusk and dawn.
The Bed and the Desk have merged.
The Notification
Invades the sanctuary of the mind at 11:47 PM.
The structural unit of the new, endless workday.
The Pyjama Desk
Camouflages the office in domestic cloth.
A costume the office did not know it was getting.
The Forced Holiday
Engineers recovery strictly to fuel more labor.
You rest only to return to the work in better shape.
The Replacement
Waits patiently to inherit your function.
The replacement does not need a quarterly report.
The Obsolete Man
Manifests the shame of our own slowness.
Surpassed by our own products, smaller than ourselves.
The Idle Tool
Sits quietly where the worker used to stand.
The machine that no longer needs us.
The Real Leisure
Reclaims contemplation and festival.
The part of the day that has no purpose outside itself.
Caesar's Commentarii
Third-Person Gaslighting. Play to rewrite an opponent's successful turn as a catastrophic failure. They must accept your version of reality.
The general wrote a clean, elegant memoir acting like a neutral observer of his own continental slaughter.
Divided into Three Parts
Geographic Pretext. Divide the game board. You automatically own the middle. Opponents must pay rent to exist.
The most famous opening line in military memoir history is just a fancy way of saying "I'm about to conquer all three."
The One Million Dead
Institutional Math. Delete half the opponent's deck. Call it "Pacification."
Institutional assessments count corpses as logistics. The Gauls were treated as terrifying so the Romans could justify the math.
Druidic Oral Tradition
Unwritten Memory. Hide three cards in your pocket. The opponent cannot target what they cannot prove exists.
The specific institutional memory of the Celtic world wasn't written down. When the Romans burned the groves, they deleted the hard drive.
The Aedui (The Client Tribe)
Strategic Defection. Switch alliances mid-game. Take all your current ally's resources with you.
Rome's primary client tribe learned the hard way that a Roman alliance has limits military pressure will eagerly expose.
The Helvetii (The Catalyst)
Demographic Avalanche. Move 368,000 tokens at once. Burn your own base so you can't retreat.
A genuine demographic migration that Caesar intercepted, creating the perfect pretext for a war of total conquest.
The Arverni (The Kingmakers)
Displaced Pre-eminence. Gain +5 Attack if you are currently losing. Resentment is your fuel.
The wealthy plateau tribe whose specific resentment over losing top dog status gave the pan-Gallic revolt its political urgency.
The Aeduan Popular Faction
Grassroots Sabotage. Disable the opponent's highest-value aristocratic card using sheer mob noise.
The aristocrats loved the Roman patronage; the people knew it was just an elaborate leash.
The Belgae
Barbarian Distance. Immune to 'Civilizing' effects. The further from the center you play them, the harder they hit.
Caesar called them the bravest because they were furthest from Mediterranean luxury and fought the Germans for fun.
The Nervii
Camp Ambush. Attack while the opponent is still shuffling their deck.
They used terrain and timing to hit the Romans before formations could be completed, nearly ending Caesar's career in an afternoon.
Ambiorix of the Eburones
Fatal Trust. Convince an opponent to discard their hand to 'avoid a trap,' which is the actual trap.
The chieftain who used a client's trust to bait fifteen Roman cohorts out of winter camp and straight into the meat grinder.
The Galatians
Mercenary Range. Play this card on any opponent's board. They fight for whoever pays the most attention.
The Gauls who went East. They had no druids, no base, just a reputation for ferocity that terrified Hellenistic kings into hiring them.
Vercingetorix of the Arverni
Tragic Sacrifice. Surrender this card to save your remaining deck. The opponent gets to gloat for 6 turns.
He built a genuinely pan-Gallic coalition, figured out the correct strategy, and lost because marginally better is enough for Rome.
Brennus
Heavy Sword. When tying a score, throw your sword on the scales. You win.
The Senonian chieftain who sacked Rome and summarized all asymmetric negotiation with five syllables: Vae Victis.
Cassivellaunus
Mobile Skirmish. Never lock into combat. Deal damage and return this card to your hand immediately.
The British chieftain who refused to give the Romans the heavy infantry fight they wanted, opting to ruin their day with chariots.
Dumnorix of the Aedui
Refusal to Cross. Cancel any forced movement effect. You die, but you don't go.
The politician who understood Caesar was a permanent replacement, not a guest, and was killed trying to escape the hostage tour.
Druid Military Function
Divine Exemption. This card cannot be attacked. It directs all your other cards and makes the violence "legitimate."
They weren't just religious specialists; they were the command layer, the legal arbitrators, and the institutional memory.
Diviciacus of the Aedui
Theological Legitimation. Force an opponent to agree with your move because "the gods (or the Senate) said so."
The only Druid Caesar named. His cooperation was structurally necessary for the Roman client system to function in Gaul.
The Head Cult
Cedar Oil Trophy. When you defeat an enemy card, pin it to your board. It generates fear points every turn.
You don't sell your professional credentials. The head contains the soul; taking it transfers the enemy's power to the victor.
The Sacred Spring (Carnutes)
Subterranean Memory. Long after your cards are destroyed, they still produce +1 Resource from the discard pile.
The pan-Gallic druidic council met here. Rome burned it and built a cathedral on top. But the spring remembers.
Naked Warrior (Gaesatae)
Survival Mathematics. Attack with zero defense. Your opponent takes psychological damage just watching you do it.
They fought without armor as a deliberate ritual choice, communicating that normal survival mathematics did not apply to them.
The Carnyx
Acoustic Terror. Opponent must play their next turn with their cards facing away from them.
The tall bronze trumpet with the animal head. Its harsh, discordant shriek was the specific signal that activated the Roman fear response.
The Torque
Honor Advertising. Place on a unit. If defeated, the opponent gets double points. If victorious, you get triple.
The twisted gold neck ring. Armor for the soul, a library of accumulated honor, and the ultimate trophy for a Roman looter.
The Chariot
Aristocratic Extraction. Save one of your defeated cards right before it dies by pulling it back to your hand.
Not an archery platform. A mobility tool for the elite warrior who fights on foot but needs the prestige of a drive-by arrival.
Celtic Longsword
Open Melee. Devastating in open space, but loses power if the opponent clusters their cards together.
90 centimeters of metallurgical superiority designed for slashing. Romans claimed they bent; archaeologists claim Romans lied.
The Gaesum (Heavy Spear)
Socketed Impact. Pierce through an opponent's shield card and hit the unit behind it.
The heavy thrusting weapon that gave the naked Gaesatae their name. Big, iron, leaf-shaped, and terrifying.
The Lancea (Light Spear)
Farmer's Reach. Can be equipped by any low-level card to instantly make them a ranged threat.
Everyone's weapon. The specific equipment the farming warrior carries from his fields to the battlefield and back.
Celtic Shield (Thureos)
Individual Block. Block an attack, but you cannot form a shield wall with other cards.
A personal tool for individual combat, unlike the Roman Scutum. It reflects an honor-based system, not a collective-discipline machine.
Chainmail (Lorica Hamata)
Technological Adoption. When an opponent uses a new tactic, copy it immediately and claim you invented it.
The Gauls invented it. The Romans wore it. Medieval knights get the credit. Historiography is just organized theft.
Celtic Iron Helmet
Ceremonial Distraction. Equip to draw all enemy attacks to this unit, because it looks absolutely fabulous.
From simple caps to spectacular winged parade helmets. The metallurgical sophistication was so high, Roman auxiliary units just wore the local gear.
Scorched Earth
Resource Denial. Burn your own resource deck. The opponent immediately starves and loses half their hand.
Vercingetorix's doctrine: destroy your own grain to break the Roman supply line. The hardest part was convincing the tribes to do it.
The Helvetian Wagon Laager
Mobile Fortress. Turn your discard pile into a defensive wall. It takes three turns to breach.
The moving city of the Helvetii turned into an impromptu fortress at Bibracte, proving that migrating badgers do not go down easily.
Battle of the Allia
Exposed Flank. Attack the card on the far edge of the opponent's board for double damage.
The Gauls wrapped around the unsecured Roman flank. The Roman army collapsed. The strategic psychology of a whole empire was born in this panic.
Sack of Rome (390 BCE)
Capitol Siege. Occupy an opponent's territory. They must pay you gold every turn until you leave.
They weren't screaming barbarians stumbling into an empty city. They conducted a seven-month siege and extracted maximum leverage.
Vae Victis (The Ransom Gold)
Absolute Leverage. Change the win conditions of the game while you are currently winning.
Woe to the conquered. Brennus's response when the Romans complained about the scales. The permanent truth of every asymmetric negotiation.
Battle of Telamon
Pincer Movement. Trap an opponent's card between two of your own to instantly destroy it.
The Romans caught a Gallic army between two consular armies. The last tactical expression of the naked warrior charge in Italy.
Battle of Bibracte
Narrative Management. Even if you lose the battle, you get to write the score sheet.
The Helvetii nearly broke the legions. Caesar claimed victory, ordered them home, and wrote the first chapter of his PR masterpiece.
The Tenth Legion
Flank Rescue. Play instantly when you are about to lose. Save your board and wipe out the attacker.
The Roman reserve that hit the Nervii from the flank just as Caesar was grabbing a shield and fighting for his life in the front lines.
Caesar's Hostage Diplomacy
Political Extortion. Steal an opponent's card. If they attack you, you rip it up.
Caesar attempted to take Dumnorix to Britain as a hostage. Standard Roman operating procedure: hold their kids, take their land.
Avaricum (The Exception)
Fatal Sentimentality. Refuse to destroy one of your own resource cards. The opponent captures it and wins the game.
The one town the Gallic council refused to burn. Caesar took it, used its grain, and continued the campaign. Sentimentality is a tactical error.
The Circumvallation
Double Walls. Build a wall facing your opponent, and a wall facing the rest of the room. You can't move, but neither can they.
Fifty kilometers of earthworks. Fighting on two fronts simultaneously. The most terrifying engineering flex in military history.
The Relief Army
Mass Coordination. Combine the attack power of every single card in your deck for one turn. If it fails, you lose instantly.
250,000 warriors from across Gaul, assembled to break the Roman perimeter. They failed by the margin of one flank attack.
The Desperate Flank Attack
Absolute Commitment. Exhaust your entire hand to add +1 to a crucial roll.
Caesar personally rode along the line with cavalry to stabilize the collapsing perimeter. The final engagement lasted a day and a night.
The Six-Year Wait
